It does not increase from acting nice or polite to individuals. Instead, you'll need to act harsh, stern, and at other times, intimidating.

Respect also increases Obedience, but does not go over a certain threshold. It is the trickiest one to increase out of the four, especially if you want to fully max out all of them.
​
Sooo acting nice and reasonable was pretty useless, then?

You'd have gotten an increase in Loyalty instead, but it's already at 100​

Damn, really screwed up there, didn't I? I mean, well, I guess forcing her to spill everything might've decreased my Affection, and it's so close to being maxed out. Yeah, I suppose both choices were correct in a way, so everything is okay?

You seem satisfied with your choice.​

Again, it's beneficial. I know she loves me, making sure she loves me most is what I want to get here.

...Is that truly what you think?​

Huh?

It just seemed to me that you… well, looked quite honest.​

My brows furrowed in confusion, still not sure what the Game is trying to say. What exactly are you insinuating?

...Forgive me, I meant nothing by it. Please forget what I said.​

I blink and shake my head quickly. Weird, but whatever. Not exactly my concern here.

"So what you're saying is that my school has those devils in it? And heiresses no less?" I fake ignorance, which my mother oddly believes. "And that I'm apparently as important as they are?"

"Well, yes." She nods. "Which is why you must be very careful in school. Thankfully, they're not aware of your powers - you know how to hide it well and must've thrown them off."

"So I guess it was good that I practiced."

"Yep." Mizuki giggled, then lost her smile. "Remember though, don't get too close to them. Whatever they say-"

"Devils are never to be trusted, got it." I nod. I agree with her wholeheartedly. "I won't - I'll keep them at arm's length, maybe spy on them if you'd like."

"That's-!" Her face morphs into one of shock. "That's- I, well, really respect your courage, but that's extremely dangerous. Please don't."

"If you say so." I shrug. "So, you said there's one last thing you wanted to tell me?"

"Yeah." Mizuki yawned. "It's about me, er, us to be more accurate."

"You look tired," I remark. "Are you alright?"

"Mhm, I suppose this whole thing drained me a lot more than I thought it would." She chuckles weakly. "C-can we continue this later? Sorry, love, but I don't feel well."

I try to hide my disappointment, but I'm pretty sure she caught it. Her tiny wince and grimace told me as much. Forcing her would probably mean an increase in Obedience, but a possible decrease in affection and affection is almost filled up.

...Oh well, no rush I guess? She doesn't seem anywhere near as hesitant about this other secret. She'll probably tell me tomorrow or something, hopefully.

"Sure, we can do this tomorrow." I nod. "Go and get some sleep. I'll wake you up real early tomorrow for some magic practice, alright?"

"Sure, that sounds fun~" She waves at me, yawning tiredly as she walks up the stairs. "Love you, Akane."

"I love you too."

As she disappears from view, I blink and look at the time. 8 PM, more than enough time to maybe finish the dungeon. I have the skills, items, and perks needed. Not sure what I'm facing in the last wave, but if I can kill the Paladin in less than a second, I can probably handle it with ease.

I think. Maybe.

I only spent around 30 minutes the first time today, so I have a bit under ninety minutes to finish four waves. I haven't used any of the items I got from wave 6, which were two standard crystals - both for CHA - and five uncommon tokens.

I leave the house and walk for a distance, before entering the dungeon and quickly snapping them all. Nothing truly noteworthy, except for Toxic Throwing Knives, five of them. Won't work on Zombies I don't think, but it's better to keep them as a backup weapon, or for a quick debuff when I have to.

With that, I start my routine, putting on my gear, making a tower, and actually making more than one repeater. I made six all around the little castle, all of them taking a lot out of me. I was about to start the wave, but then I remembered. I have enough MP for that wing spell.

It wasn't difficult to cast the spell, it felt as if it was something I've been doing for a while. Crystal clear ice wings form behind my back, and I look at them in awe as every flap releases a gust of cold wind. Of course, seeing how low my MP is I had to wait for a couple of minutes before I was able to continue.

Once my MP has recovered and my headache clears, I get off the tower and try to fly, instinctively knowing how to use those wings and adapting with only a tiny bit of difficulty.

My flight speed wasn't fast, but I was honest-to-god flying. I'm looking down right now, a little anxious from how high I am, but equally excited that I'm actually flying. No planes or hang gliders needed.

"This is gonna need some time to get used to…" I mumble, my face contorting into a worried but happy smile. "At least it can be used as a shield for now."

I descend slowly, landing safely on the castle. Alright, time to actually start the seventh wave.

(Rias)

"Someone managed to sneak up on you?" The Gremory Heiress parroted in shock. "But how? You're one of, if not the best Sneaks of our generation!"

Koneko looked away, fidgeting uncomfortably, clearly ashamed of the fact. Rias sighed and patted her head to comfort her, Akeno putting a tray on the table in front of the redhead.

This wasn't how Rias thought the first day of school would go. With the news of two new students who were close to the Yakuza attending Kuoh Academy, the redhead thought it was the perfect opportunity to better the relationship between their factions. She was quick to realize that they didn't know about the supernatural, at least, one of them didn't.

She tried to hide it, that Haruka girl, but she and Sona easily noticed the nervous glances she had given them. She's either intimidated by them seeing how famous they are in the school, which Rias doubted, or she genuinely knew what they were.

As for the Amamiya girl. Well, she didn't show any reaction to them. Sona was quick to point it out seeing that they've interacted more than once, and Akane didn't quite care about immediately causing trouble. She sent two students to the hospital on her first day for Lucifer's Sake!

Rias managed to see the entire thing unfold from the window, grimacing when Akane didn't stop even after knocking them out. There is a good chance that they'll be bedridden for years. The redhead thought that the girl went a bit too far. It was just a little peeping, nothing serious.

It was safe to say that the girl didn't know about the truth of this town, and if she did, she's either incredibly brave to pull that stunt or just doesn't care at all. Or maybe, it's an act? Do that to trick them into thinking she's ignorant?

Her sudden disappearance on lunch break that not even Koneko found her was fairly suspicious. Something was obviously amiss here - you don't hide from Koneko when you're just a regular human.

Unlikely that she's unaware, but a possibility nonetheless.

But if she was being honest, there was another student that caught her attention. Ichiban Kasuga.

Something was… odd, about him. She felt subtle energy within him, fiery and primal. Draconic, almost. It wasn't common to sense this, but if her assumption is correct, then he might be a Longinus Wielder. dragon type. Sacred Gears don't give off a lot of energy when they're locked, not unless it's a Longinus of course.

A quick look into his background didn't tell a lot, unfortunately. He was uninteresting and normal, a young orphan boy who got raised in a brothel. His grades were excellent and his guardian had enough money to send him to Kuoh Academy…

...Which sounds a little weird. Something was odd about this and Rias wasn't sure why. Everything about him looked legit, too legit. Sona thought he was a spy but he's very clearly unaware of the supernatural. The only thing that truly got them on guard when connecting the dots was the aura he had, but if he was a spy, why wouldn't he hide it fully? It didn't make a lot of sense to them.

However, they decided to keep an eye on him regardless. If they're overthinking, then Rias can invite him to her peerage. A possible Longinus Wielder would be Lucifersent, especially with the marriage approaching fast.

"And…" Koneko spoke up once more. "There was a cold presence."

"A cold presence?" Rias raised a brow. "How so?"

"It felt cold, freezing." Her Rook said. "...I could see my own breath."

Rias only furrowed her brows.

"Some sort of a supernatural creature, or one skilled in magic, then." Kiba quipped. "Well, that was obvious enough as they managed to sneak up on Koneko, but if they're able to release such presence…"

"Someone powerful." Akeno sighed. "Ara ara~ should we call Lucifer-sama, Buchou?"

"Hmm… no, not yet." Rias shook her head. "We should observe, for now, gauge the threat, then act accordingly. If it's something we can't handle, then we'll inform my brother."

"Are you sure this is wise?" Her Queen tilted her head.

"It could be a Tojo Agent." Her Knight added.

"Doubt it, they won't do something drastic like this." The redhead frowned. "Throwing around threats like these isn't something the Tojo would do. Most likely a third party."

"Could it be Shun Akiyama?" Kiba questioned.

"Had it been Shun, Koneko would've felt a hot presence, not a freezing one," Akeno said. "And if I recall correctly, it was a woman's voice?"

Koneko nodded.

"Regardless, I think we should pull back and observe from afar," Rias said. "Koneko, Akeno, pause the tailing for now. We'll listen to this… Mysterious Bodyguard and stop. We don't have enough information about her to do anything."

The two nodded in affirmation.

"I'll try to befriend them here at Kuoh, it's the safer way." She added. "All of you try to do so as well - I'll inform Sona about this. We should avoid provoking the Tojo or this woman. War is the last thing we want."

Rias can admit that she can be pushy sometimes, but even she knows when to stop. This might be a sign or a message telling her that she's pushing a little too much. They're not exactly in the position to assume that this woman was a Tojo - if they came to the chairman with false accusations it'll only make them look bad.

The peace is already shaky enough. If they can hold on until an official contract is formed, then they can at least breathe again. Rias isn't about to ruin years of her brother's work and is definitely not about to be the one to blame for a war they're not sure they can win.

"How would you get close to Amamiya-san?" Akeno asked with a head tilt.

"Heh, you can leave this to me," Rias smirked arrogantly. "I'm the most popular girl in school. Who wouldn't want to be friends with the Queen of Kuoh Academy?"

"Are you sure?" Her Queen questioned worriedly. "We know she has a short fuse, and we saw how she acted earlier today. What if you say the wrong thing?"

"You worry too much. I got this." She waved off her worries. "I've already made plenty of friends here. How's this gonna be any different?"

So their best bet is getting close to her the old-fashioned way: Be friends. A foolproof plan if Rias had to say, worked every time. Unless she's talking to an individual who wants nothing but to rip her apart, then that'll be a piece of cake.

She just hoped she wouldn't get on her bad side. Seeing that boy get his face dragged across the pavement made her shiver.

...Maybe they should start taking the complaints about perverts seriously before anything truly horrible happens.



(Haruka)

She wasn't sure if coming over to Kuoh was even a good idea - she was practically stuck in a school filled with supernatural creatures, and only noticed when it was too late. Haruka had assumed that she was attending a regular high school until the moment she set foot inside.

Now, Haruka had a rough life prior, almost always getting dragged into Yakuza conflicts along with her adoptive father, and was fairly familiar with the Supernatural. Her father figure had his fair share of tussles with devils and fallen, and seeing how close she was to him, they usually dragged her into their messes.

So seeing that she's practically stuck in this school for the next year at least was terrifying if she's being honest. She likes devils as much as she likes Yakuza, and that means 'not very much'. She went through so much to finally achieve the peace she dreamed of - her father died for it, so the possibility of being pulled into all of it again…

Haruka sighed deeply, taking the ice cream cone off the vendor's hand with a grateful smile. At the very least, Kuoh was a quiet town, a lot less loud than Kamurocho and nowhere near as crowded. It reminded her of Okinawa a bit, just without the humidity or the smell of the sea.

She wondered what the other kids at the orphanage were doing. Without her or Uncle Kaz there, they might be having some difficulties. Thankfully, Haruka still had more than enough money from her career as an Idol, so they can take care of themselves for a while.

Even then, she knew Taichi and Ayako were old enough to hold down the fort while she is gone. The reason she's even going to a school as prestigious as this is to up her chances of going to a good college, then get a good job to support the orphanage by herself, or at least until everyone else can go to a good college themselves.

But of course, the universe had to somehow beat her down a little more and send her to a devil-infested school. She should've researched a little more.

Now, that's not to say that Haruka has any significant problems with devils. She's been taught to not judge people by their appearance, ethnicity, or race. To not categorize people into certain stereotypes. After all, her adoptive father was literally the Fourth Chairman of the Tojo Clan.

But she was worried. She hated dealing with Supernatural or the Yakuza, she wanted to live her life in peace. She didn't know what to do now seeing that two heiresses were in the school, along with what Haruka assumes is their own peerages. It worried her if she's being honest.

And to make it worse, she felt someone following her earlier today. She wasn't sure if she was being paranoid or there was something following her, but it didn't make it any better.

With another tired sigh, Haruka walked across the streets, heading towards her apartment with her cold treat in hand. At the very least, she could take care of herself for a bit - Akiyama taught her a few moves, specifically how to use her legs for some deadly techniques.

Her physique and the constant dancing lessons she took a while ago made it a lot easier for her to learn some of his moves. Even after quitting, Haruka kept exercising more and more, because aside from her being very happy with how her body turned out, she still loved dancing.

It was, and still is, her hobby. Same with singing.

Her expression fell as her thoughts traced back to the school, then brightened up a little when she remembered the new girl she met. This Akane Amamiya felt a little familiar - more specifically, her last name. There was this Yakuza patriarch she knew that had that last name too, right?

It didn't matter though - while the girl was a little strange, wearing a male uniform and all that, she was very nice. She talked a little casually, yet was still fairly polite. Haruka also admired how confident she looked. Even with the weird looks she got, she never gave it any mind.

Haruka wanted to approach her on lunch break but was beaten to the punch by that other guy with the afro. They seemed to know each other, and she backed down, only to be hounded by a lot of girls telling her how cute she looked and whatnot.

She was… a little surprised that nobody recognized her. She made a pretty big name for herself, after all. However, she was sure that Akane knew who she was, the little shock on her face when she said her name told her that much.

Haruka felt very glad that Akane didn't start hounding her with questions and whatever. She respected her privacy, which meant a lot. Heck, she even acted like she didn't know at all.

She appreciated it.

Her… reaction to what she did to those perverts felt a little overboard, but Haruka isn't exactly new to violence. She used to see it almost every day with how many delinquents and thugs swarm her adoptive father.

The only thing that surprised her was that it was a girl doing it this time. She was used to middle-aged men beating the crap out of teens who thought they were hot stuff. She won't lie, it was funny to see sometimes.

And Haruka wasn't exactly sympathetic to perverts. They played with too much fire and got burned.

Severely.

Like, a flamethrower to the face.

As Haruka passed by an alleyway, someone cleared their throat, prompting her to stop in her tracks. She turned her head towards the dark alley as soon as she put the tiny plastic spoon in her mouth, blinking a little when she spotted a man.

Short white hair, red eyes, and a smirk on his face. He wore a simple black shirt, black pants and a cross necklace. "Hey there, girlie. Mind if we have a minute?"

Haruka flinched, her intuition quickly telling her that this man is bad news. She tried to ignore him, quickening her pace, but he stopped her by firmly grabbing her shoulder. Haruka was quick to deduce that this was no normal man.

"Now, isn't it a little rude to walk away like this?" He asked with a knowing look. "I just want a little talk."

She subtly looked around, finding it very suspicious that there was no one around, then turned to look at him slowly with a hardened look.

"Please let go of me." She said politely, but firmly. "I'm busy."

"Aw, c'mon, what's a minute gonna do?" He shook his head. "I just want to talk about our lord and savior~"

"I'm not interested." Haruka pushed his arm away. "Now please leave me be."

As she walked away, almost jogging at this point, the man clicked his tongue audibly, obviously very annoyed at her being dismissive. "Oi, you bitch. I'm being polite here, so you better listen right now."

She ignored him, almost rolling her eyes at his 'threat'. He might look dangerous, but Haruka has seen and stood up against people who can turn this town into ashes in mere seconds. She's not really afraid of him.

The man grabbed her roughly this time, slamming her against the wall nearby as he stared at her with a scowl, her ice cream, unfortunately, falling on the ground. "Don't you fucking ignore me, you slut."

Haruka only narrowed her eyes in defiance. Even when he showed her superior strength, she didn't even flinch. She's seen this scene play out far too many times and by people hundreds of times scarier than him.

She was ready for a fight, though she was hoping she wouldn't have to - she didn't exactly like fighting. Haruka hated hurting people after all, but sometimes, she had to.

She clenched her fists as he growled. "The fuck is up with that look, huh? You looking down on me, you dumb bitch-?!"

It was then when an arm grabbed his, and without even giving the two a chance to react, a fist made contact with the creep's face, sending him stumbling back as he held his nose in pain. He hissed and sneered at the assailant, who to Haruka's surprise, was her classmate.

Akane retracted her arm back, glaring at him as her visible eye glowed crimson in the dark. "Girl isn't interested. Fuck off already."

"You…" He growled. "You stupid bitch…"

"At least I'm not the dude with a broken nose." She shot back with a smug smirk. "Want me to fix it for you? Cuz I can do that, free of charge~"

The man clenched his fists as a growl left his throat.

"A-Akane-chan?" Haruka mumbled. "What are you doing here?"

"Nothing. Was taking a walk, saw this cunt harassing a classmate, and my fists began to itch." She shrugged. "Besides, let's be honest, he has a really punchable face."

The man was looking as if he was gonna pop a vessel, and the smirk on her classmate's face only angered him further. Haruka realized that this man most likely had contact with the supernatural, so Akane possibly has no idea what she's getting herself into.

Haruka needed to protect her, even if that punch was fairly impressive.

"You dumb whores…" He snarled. "You'll pay for this!"

"Speaking like a shitty anime villain doesn't make you intimidating, it makes you look like a chuuni." Akane scoffed as she crossed her arms. "C'mon, people don't say that shit in real life. Do better."

Haruka stifled a giggle, quietly agreeing with her. He did sound like one just now.

Another growl left his throat, and Akane took it upon herself to humiliate him some more.

"And now he's growling like some fucking animal." She said. "C'mon boy, bark! Show a trick or two!"

That almost did it- he almost charged at her but stopped completely as his eyes darted back and forth, narrowing before he backed away. He looked at Akane with a scornful glare as he slowly walked to the alley he came from.

"You." He pointed at her classmate. "I'll remember you."

"I'm honored, though I can't say the same." She said, continuing her mockery. "You dumbass thugs are starting to blend in together. Can't tell if you're real or some robots made by the government at this point."

He clicked his tongue and disappeared in the darkness, Akane chuckling a second later. "Yeah, that's what I thought, bitch."

"Um, Akane-chan?" Haruka called out to her, who turned back to look at her. "Thank you so much for the help."

"Don't mention it. I was bored anyway." Akane shrugged. "Should've kicked him in the balls, though."

"I was gonna do that." Haruka smiled. "But you handled it before I could."

"Heh." She grinned. "Say, you have anything important to do?"

"Um, not really." Haruka felt a little surprised at the question but answered truthfully. "Why do you ask?"

"I was thinking we can go check out this place together?" Akane offered. "You're new here too, right? So why not explore this town for a bit? Still have a few hours before midnight."

Haruka blinked then smiled softly. "That sounds nice."

"Cool." Her classmate led the way as Haruka began walking next to her. "Heard the arcade was this way. Let's go there first."

Haruka wasn't quite sure what happened, or why that strange man retreated so suddenly, but she felt admittedly safe around her new friend. Maybe it's how charismatic she was, or how very brave she'd been to stand up against that man.

Haruka wasn't exactly the most… intimidating of individuals - she preferred persuading and simply ignoring instead, so seeing a girl her age who looks like one of the friendliest people she's seen act that way was a little weird, though admirable.

She could do without the dirty language, even if it was funny...

#165
I was… admittedly a little too excited to sleep well last night. I try to keep these emotions in check, but actual training with an expert is something I've been wanting to do since the moment I got my magic.

I woke up very early, at six in the morning, quickly woke my mom up, who took thirty damned minutes to get up, then headed straight to wherever we're supposed to be training. School starts at 8:30, so we have a solid two-hour training session before we can leave.

I debated whether I should reveal my ID-Create, but thankfully she had a place. It wasn't that close, but not very far either. Took us around 25 minutes to arrive there on foot. Mizuki explained a little about herself, or more accurately, her relationship with the Tojo.

Turns out I was right. My father wasn't a regular grunt, but a patriarch of a powerful family. He was so respected that everyone under him bowed in his presence, though he didn't necessarily care if they did or not.

She said that he was very loyal to the clan, but when he had me, he left it to raise me alongside my mother. He thought that being too close with the Tojo would endanger me in some way.

I wanted to ask how he died, since being a lieutenant must mean he was powerful but had to drop the conversation since we arrived. It… didn't look as good as I thought it would.

I take a look around the 'training grounds' my mother chose: an abandoned warehouse where the lights keep flickering and dust everywhere you lay your eyes on. I scratch my cheek, and while I do agree that it's a nice, hidden place to train in, it's not… really optimal.

I grimace as I see a rat scurry over to the other side of the place, then turn my gaze to my mother. "So how did you find this place?"

"A friend's recommendation." She shrugs.

"Right…" I mutter. "And how are you sure the devils won't be able to sense what we're doing?"

We've had fun at the arcade, karaoke, and the batting center, even if I was a little hesitant about that last one. You don't know what sort of high-ranking yakuza hangs around that place. I'd rather not bump into one again, even after knowing how important I am to them. Almost had a heart attack that time.

Once we were done with our fun, we decided to have dinner, which went as normally as you'd expect. We would've ended it there, but then Haruka suggested we stop by a cafe for a chat, and I thought why not.

"So after those guys interrupted us, we made a temporary truce and kicked their asses instead," Ichiban said, telling the story of how we met. "It was kinda hard since we were already tired, but we scared them off."

"Oh?" Haruka looks interested. "Then?"

"I dunno, we just hit it off, I guess." He shrugs. "It was weird - we were literally about to kill each other, then we let off some steam on those morons and became friends."

"You still owe me, Ichi." I quip casually. "I paid dinner for the both of us that time. Where's the money?"

"I-it's been years- how the hell do you still remember that?!!" He looks at me in shock.

"Money is money," I say simply. "Now hand it over."

"Aren't you rich?" He tries to argue. "You don't need a couple of hundred Yen, do you?"

"A couple of hundred?!" I scowl at the absurdity of his statement. "I paid tens of thousands you dipshit! It was Korean BBQ! That stuff isn't cheap!"

"Thousands don't make a dent on your wallet." He sneers back. "Stop being so stingy! It's already been years damn it!"

"I'm teaching you that people don't forget what they're owed." My eyes narrow. "Now give it here or I'll shove your wallet so far up your ass you might as well be the first-ever human ATM."

"Ugh… fine." He relents, fishing out his wallet.

The amused giggle of our third member catches our attention. The both of us turn to look at Haruka, who puts her teacup back on the table.

"You two are really close, aren't you?"

I blink. "I suppose."

"We've known each other for a long time." He added. "We might not have spent a lot of time together at the time, but we made the most of it. Heh, every moment was a thrill back then."

"Oi, people might get the wrong idea, dumbass." I deadpan. "We were close, but not that close."

"I didn't mean it that way!" He scowls, cheeks burning red at the implication. "God, can you stop saying that stuff? You know exactly what I meant!"

"Yeah." I grin. "Still funny to call you out on it."

"Tsk, whatever." He sighs, then turns back to Haruka. "What about you, Haruka? Do you have anyone close?"

"My siblings." She nods. "I live in an Orphanage with a lot of other kids. I'm the oldest one, so I'm doing my best to get to a good college since we don't have a lot of support right now."

"Heh, you're responsible." Ichiban compliments with a smile. "Must be pressuring, though. Is that why you got into Kuoh? Cuz it's a pretty good school."

I notice a tiny wince from Haruka, making me hum quietly. Does she know something?

"Y-yes, I think graduating from Kuoh Academy will help me immensely." She confirms. "And I don't feel much pressure. I'm confident I can get a good job in the future. I'm just worried that they're gonna struggle because I take too long."

I try to look interested and sympathetic, though I couldn't help but groan on the inside. So dumb. If I was in her place, I would've just given them the middle finger as I lived my own life. Tying myself to emotions like this is only gonna bring me down.

Think and live for yourself, not others. Otherwise, what's the point?

"...You know, if you need any help, we can lend a hand." Ichiban offers with a confident smile, and I couldn't help but pause at the 'we'.

...I don't like this.

"Eh?" Haruka blinks.

"Yeah. I personally know some people that might be able to help if I try really hard to convince them." He says, then points at me. "And this girl here is richer than all of Kuoh Academy combined."

Oh for fuck's sake.

"Oi, don't go around spouting people's wealth like that." I frown in annoyance. "The money isn't even mine in the first place."

"And you think your mom is gonna ignore a chance to help some children in need?" He crosses his arm.

I open my mouth to argue, then realize that he has a point. "Fair. Knowing her, she'd be all over Haruka right now."

"Y-you really don't have to." She stands up from her chair, looking a bit flustered. "I appreciate it, really! But I can handle this on my own."

"You don't have to, though." He shrugs. "We're willing to help, and it's okay to take us up on our offers. If you're really in need, then don't shy away from asking for help."

She looks at the two of us, most likely touched by this gesture, then a warm smile takes over her face as she sits down. "Thank you. I'm… very glad to have met you two."

"Hehe, anytime!"

10 Reputation with Ichiban Kasuga [70/100]

20 Reputation with Haruka Sawamura [55/100]

Oh.

Well, thanks Ichiban. Did all the work for me.

I pull out my phone and check the time, frowning slightly. It's late - checking up on that abandoned church is probably a bad idea now. Better do it in daylight instead, safer that way.

Oh well, guess I can spend the rest of the night grinding my spell levels in the dungeon, maybe finally finishing the last wave.

"I think I've had enough fun today," I state, getting up from my seat, giving them a small smile. "It's been great hanging out, but I have to get home."

"Me too." Haruka nods. "I've had so much fun today. Thank you, Ichiban-kun, Akane-chan."

"Already?" Ichiban raises a brow.

"We're in school, Ichi." I deadpan. "That means studying and sleeping early."

"Oh right." He chuckles sheepishly. "Guess I gotta head back too, then."

"Oh don't sound so disappointed." I wink. "You'll see me tomorrow anyway."

A strangled noise leaves his throat as he blushes a little, making Haruka giggle. "T-this wasn't about you."

"I'm sure," I say, then give them a wave. "See you."

I walk away, almost skipping steps as I wonder what the rewards for the final wave will be. They gotta be powerful, right? I've been getting meh stuff the last few waves, so the final one must make up for it all.

Though, I'm more interested in improving my other, powerful spells, like the Crystal Wings spell. I need to refine it more, make it actually useable and not just a 5 minutes flight spell. It acts as a good shield for sure, but 20k is probably nothing compared to the real heavy hitters like Sirzechs.

I need more power if I want to survive. Improve as much as I can with my mother's help. A legendary assassin must have a lot of tricks worth learning after all, and I'm not just talking about magic. Assassins in DxD must have some special abilities that I can learn.

Can't wait till I get some kickass killing moves…



First thing I did was obviously refine my Crystal Wings, leveling them up to +3 from the get-go, which increased the time limit to 11 minutes, decreased the cooldown to 25 minutes, and increased its armor potency to 27,000. This is already a huge upgrade, much better than it was unrefined. I don't know what refining limit this spell has, but I'm hoping for something like 10+.

Then I decided to improve my walls, towers, and turrets for a better base. Same with traps actually. I've refined most of my current spells until I couldn't, increasing their potency significantly. The wings spell is the only one I struggle with since I need to wait for the cooldown.

Though, I think this is enough refining. I'm confident I can take on the final wave and win. I'm a little worried about possible difficulty spikes, but my improved bullets can take it. There's one more wave before that I haven't finished, though, it can be the warm-up wave.

I created my castle, making repeaters here and there seeing that I've improved them a lot. Instead of 3 seconds per shot, it's 1.5 now. Twice as fast, and it deals a good bit of damage. I made 12 all around the little fortress, then filled the outside with traps.

I crack my knuckles and roll my neck, feeling a little excited. Alright, here goes.

Wave start

Defeat 5 Zombie Paladins, 100 Zombie Soldiers, 50 Zombie Archers, 45 Zombie Mages [0/200]

Rewards: 1 Epic Gacha Token, 5 Minor Life Potions, Paladin Shield, 5 Greater Stat Crystals, 500 Credits

That… is a lot of paladins.

I do the smart thing first and quickly take out the mages, as their fireballs hurt my castle walls a lot. Some walls and towers fell since I couldn't kill them fast enough, but overall, they did minimal damage.

My wings were doing an amazing job of protecting me from incoming arrows, which is why I ignore them for now as I turn my focus on the Paladins. Some began charging, ramming into my ice walls and shattering them with ease.

Tiny ice spheres form around me before soaring at the Paladins faster than the eye could see, penetrating their armor and ending them quite easily. Finally, all that remained are the archers, which were easily taken care of.

Not gonna lie, when I turned to look at them, I saw that half of them were already dead. My repeaters and traps did incredible in shaving off their numbers. Tower Defense really is the way to go.

Once done, I smile. That was easy, though I've deliberately over-prepared for it. There's no such thing as Overkill after all.

Wave complete

Rewards added to inventory

Proceed to next wave?

Level up x12

I take out the rewards, of course starting with the stat crystals. Two LUK, two CHA, and one STR. I'd have preferred END or DEX, but oh well. Good enough I suppose.

I snap the token, and a weird, dark blue colored bottle appears in my hand. I raise a brow as I inspect it up close. I can feel… something inside. My senses aren't that good yet, but whatever this thing is, it's very powerful.

I take out the shield and life potion from my inventory, then use observe on everything. The potions were a glass bottle with a colorful liquid, and the shield was similar to the one the zombie paladins used, though in a better condition.

Surprising. I expected another Cryomancy item, but maybe I can use it later.

[Minor Life Potion] - Item

A potion filled with the Essence of Life, a powerful source of energy that can give birth to life-filled planets. Although extremely diluted, it is a useful item.

Restores 10% of HP, MP and SP

[Paladin Shield] - Item

A shield belonging to a Paladin, a warrior of light and the protector of innocents. Created with decent metal and enchanted by the light of certain gods, then given to noble individuals.

Negates 20% of overall damage when blocked with. Becomes 30% when the attack is filled with darkness/unholiness.

[Spinel Tonic] - Item

Pure lunar energy turned into liquid, this tonic gives the drinker a massive increase in power. It is risky, however, as it could turn anyone who drinks it addicted, suffering from heavy withdrawal symptoms and even madness. Drink with caution.

Increases all stats by 120% for 2 minutes, and gives the user temporary lunar abilities

Once the effects wear off, there's a 20% chance to be inflicted with [Lunar Affliction]

Alright, the Tonic is a last resort item, then. I don't know if this Lunar Affliction can affect me with Gamer's Mind, but it's always better to be safe than sorry. I'll keep this in hand whenever I need it.

I do think it's a good drop, though. A 120% increase is immense, even if it's only 2 minutes. I don't know what these Lunar Abilities are, but they gotta be powerful. Moon power is always strong from what I know.

I spend the time rebuilding my stuff, and even enhancing the base seeing that the final wave might be really dangerous. The difficulty spike is worrying - 200 mobs is a lot. More EXP, sure, but I'd rather not get overwhelmed and killed.

I also kept the wings' time limit in mind. I only have four minutes before it dispels. I need to make this quick.

With an enhanced base, I take a deep breath, then start the final wave.

Wave start

Defeat: 1 Lich, 2 Paladin Zombies, 7 Zombie Mages, 100 Zombie Soldiers, 50 Zombie Archers, 15 Zombie Knights [0/175]

Rewards: 2 Random Cryomancy Spellbooks, 1 Grand Stat Crystal, 2 Greater Stat Crystals, 1000 Credits, [Undead Slayer] Title, Frost Katana

A lich?

In the distance, I see the 'boss'. A floating, rotten corpse wearing tattered robes with a glowing staff in its hand. The Paladins and Mages acted as guards, sticking close to it as the rest charged at the ice fortress. He's too far, I can't use Observe on him from here.

Most were taken care of by the traps and repeaters, and I quickly focused on the boss, shooting it with multiple bullets. The staff in its hand flickered, and a purple barrier formed around it and its guards.

I frown in annoyance as I try to break this barrier with more spells. Bullets and spears struck it, and there was progress as cracks began to show up, but then it charged another spell. The staff swirled in magical energy, a purple fireball igniting above it as the lich launched it at me.

I felt something was off about it and quickly flew away, and it was the right decision as the fireball decimated the fortress, swallowing it whole and leaving nothing but scorched earth behind. My jaw drops as I look at the Lich, admittedly intimidated.

...Yeah, no.

I pull out Angel's Sorrow, newly dubbed 'GFR' or 'Get Fucked Revolver' and pull the trigger. The force once again pushes me backward, but not as hard as before as I catch myself from flying too fast.

As you'd expected, the lich, along with the paladins and mages, got deleted. There was a fucking crater where they stood too, making me chuckle at the absurdity. This gun is insane.

Kinda anticlimactic, but hey, I'm not dumb. It's easier to just end them like this.

I took care of the remaining weaker soldiers before landing on the ground with a smile. I'm so glad I got this gun.

...My wrist still hurts a bit, though.

Wave complete

Rewards added to inventory

[Undead] Dungeon Completed!

[Plant] Dungeon Unlocked!

Alert: You are not high enough level to enter the [Plant] Dungeon. Level 150 Required

Level up x16

I dismiss the dungeon message as I see the level requirement. Still not even level 100, close, but not there yet. Guess I'm gonna need to grind here instead somehow, without alerting anyone.

Kinda annoying.

No Gacha Token, which is strange. Got them almost every wave, so what gives? Oh well, I think the Cryomancy Spellbooks will have to do, and a Frost Katana, now that's something. Also, my first ever title, which I don't see being useful since there's not a lot of undead in DxD.

The first thing I do is use the crystals of course. A grand crystal is a 50 points increase, meaning 100 due to my perk, and amazingly, it's a DEX one. The other two greater crystals are END and LUK. This is great - one hundred stats at once?

I love my perks.

Name - Akane Amamiya

Level - 93

Title - Undead Slayer

Primary Class - Cryomancer - LVL 93/100 [11%]

Secondary Class - Engineer - LVL 0/100 [0%]

Race - Human

Rank - Mortal

Alignment - Neutral Evil

MP - 9300 [5580 per minute]

SP - 1900 [190 per minute]

STR - 190

END - 190

DEX - 240

INT - 930

LUK – 190

I take out the Cryomancy spellbooks, which looked almost identical. A thin book with an arctic blue cover, a white snowflake symbol on the front. I blink a few times, thinking I got the same spell twice, but then I used Observe on them.

[Cryomancy Spellbook: Frost Cloak] - Item

A Cryomancy Spellbook detailing the process of using the Frost Cloak spell.

Requirement: Journeyman Rank in [Ice Magic Control]

[Cryomancy Spellbook: Frozen Soldier] - Item

A Cryomancy Spellbook detailing the process of using the Frozen Soldier spell.

Requirement: Adept Rank in [Ice Magic Control]

Oh? I can learn the Ice Soldier spell, and I'm assuming it's a literal soldier that can protect me? That's incredibly useful. It's basically a summoning spell disguised as a Cryomancy one. Ice Magic is so overpowered, and I love it so much.

Let's see what else I got.

[Frost Katana] - Item

An impressive katana enchanted by a wandering frost wizard, giving it an icy edge.

Deals 275 + STRx4 Physical Damage + 200 Ice Damage

Eh, decent I suppose. Compliments my skillset very well I'd say.

Finally, the title.

[Undead Slayer] - Title

You've slaughtered many of the undead to the point of becoming an expert. Whether it's through magic or weapons, you've had your fair share of killing these abominations, enough that you have a special edge against them.

Passive: You are 50% resistant to undead diseases and curses

Active: You deal 25% more damage against undead creatures, as well as take 25% less damage from them

Huh, I assume the active buff means when I have it on the stat sheet? If so, then that's good. At least I get the passive boost all the time.

Well, since I've finished the dungeon, I think I can go back home. I feel a little tired if I'm being honest.

I snap my fingers and dispel the dungeon, returning to the real world. I was pretty far from home, in an abandoned construction site since I needed an open place to train in. It did well, and any damages I caused in the dungeon don't reflect on the real world, so I can rest easy.

I stretch my limbs a little as I walk home, taking out my phone as I scroll through interesting forums. I went through different wikis to look for ice spell ideas, from D&D to WoW. Hey, I might find something I can recreate.

I should ask Ichi for ideas too. He's a fan of Dragon Quest, he must know a few spells or something. The nerd will probably even brainstorm because he thinks it's cool.

A cold gust of wind makes me shiver a little, a frown taking over my face as I slow my pace.

...This feels oddly familiar.

I flinch as I sense something approaching, quickly rolling out of the way, dodging something as I turn around with a scowl, only for me to pause as I take in its familiar appearance. A grotesque, centaur thing holding two spears, which my previous memories recognize as Viser, the first Stray Devil introduced in DxD.

"You dodged." She grins. "And it seems you have fight left in you. Oh, how I love prey like you~!"

I click my tongue in annoyance as I glance at the puddle of acid.

"What a beautiful smell…" She cackles madly. "I wonder what you taste like…?"

"Too bad you're never finding that out," I respond as spears of ice form around me.

Name: Viser

Title: Acid Squirter

HP – 15,000

MP - 10,000

SP - 12,000

Race – Corrupted Devil

LVL - 120

STR - 310

END - 225

DEX - 190

INT – 65

WIS – 35

CHA – 25

LUK – 10

I almost laughed at the title. Fucking ridiculous.

It's significantly stronger than the stray I dealt with, but I'm stronger too. I'm faster and my magic damage is devastating. I can win easily.

I cast Ice Skin as the spears soar towards her, but surprisingly, she was able to block and parry the attacks with her own spears. I narrow my eyes as I switch to bullets instead, and this hurt her a lot.

She cries out in pain as a bullet goes through her front leg, growling in anger as she shoots more acid with her breast. I scrunch my face in disgust and quickly dodge, not really taking this seriously. How can I? What kind of power is "acid nipples"?

Fucking Ishibumi…

Seeing that the bullets are working, I keep shooting this gross moron, shaving off a lot of her HP in mere seconds. She screams loudly, demonic magic circles opening up near her, prompting me to crouch and summon a wall.

The magic coming out of the circles barely does anything to my ice wall, though a spurt of acid melts through it easily. With an annoyed scowl, I aim right at where it hurts, then unleash a barrage of bullets at her top half, blood splattering everywhere as she loses her acid ability right there and then..

It screams in agony, shaking in fear seeing that she really can't do much. I smirk, taunting her with a 'Come at me' gesture, which worked wonders as she charged with a snarl.

She barely had any HP left. A few more shots and she's dead.

I point my hand at her in a finger gun, a small glow forming at the tip of my finger. Right as I was about to shoot, a red blur came flying, making me flinch. I blink, the beast being sent flying to the other side as my uncle turns around, giving me a thumbs up.

"Don't worry, Akane-chan." He assures me. "You're safe now. I won't let it get near you."

...

"...uh…" I scratch my cheek awkwardly. "Thanks, but I kinda had it covered already."

He looks at me in confusion. "What?"

"Yeah, I was sorta kicking its ass," I reveal. "That thing was weak as hell. I was right about to kill it before you showed up."

"Ah…" He chuckles sheepishly. "I-is that so? There goes my cool moment, then."

The stray struggles to get up, groaning and moaning in pain. My uncle sighs, walking over to it as I follow him. "Guess you know what this is?"

"Yep, stray devil." I answer, looking down at it with pure apathy. "Kaa-san told me about them last night."

"That makes things easier." He replies, then whispers under his breath. "...Looks like she's too far gone…"

"Hm?"

"Nothing." He shakes his head. "I suppose all we can do now is put her down."

"Sure." I nod, aiming a bullet at her with my finger. "Might as well make it painless."

5 Affection with Shun Akiyama [25/100]

"That'd be best."

With that, I shoot it, the bullet going through its brain and instantly killing it. It falls down on the ground, limp and unmoving as life leaves its body.

Level up x2

Nice~

"...I guess I have some explaining to do?" I say awkwardly.

"Heh." He smiles. "Make that the two of us."

It was happening eventually, telling my uncle everything. I'm not really mad or annoyed about it - I had a feeling it was happening soon anyway.

I don't know what a stray devil was doing here - you'd think the yakuza would've taken care of it a long time ago, but eh, I suppose it's for the best. I got two levels out of her after all. Five more and I max out Cryomancy.

And I finally get to learn what my uncle really does for a living - where he got so much power, and what he can teach me.

From learning how my magic works to finishing up my first dungeon, and then to this.

All in all, I think this has been a very productive day.

#197
I'm mature enough to admit I'm a spoiled girl.

From the moment I've been born up to now even, I've always been given everything I wanted. From clothes, games, to even traveling. My mother is a pushover, and my father was even worse than her. He likes to exaggerate stuff, one time almost buying a private jet for me.

And I'm not gonna act all bashful about it - I loved every moment of it. I adored the attention my parents have given me, and I acted a little spoiled as a child too. I wasn't a bully or anything of that sort, as I was taught to do the right thing, but I loved sticking my nose where it didn't belong.

It's simply how children act, though I was admittedly more annoying than them. I never kept to myself and was loud too. Opposite of what I've become, from a hyperactive annoying child to a quiet loner.

I snort at the memory.

"What's so funny?" My uncle asks me.

"Nothing," I answer, putting the chopsticks down. "Just reminiscing about the past."

I've outgrown that mindset after my dad passed away and acted a little rebellious once I hit puberty, but I still like how I'm treated. Five-star restaurants almost twice a week, expensive clothes, and a large allowance aren't things I can just decline.

So who am I to say no to my uncle after he offered to talk over sushi? He brought it up for a reason after all, and rejecting the offer is rude. Besides, I am hungry, so might as well eat my fill of Kuoh's best sushi place.

"Heh, what would you be reminiscing about?" He grins. "The last guy you beat up?"

"Is that your way of saying I should keep it to old folk like you?" I raise a brow.

"I'm not old."

"Yeah, you're not," I smirk. "You're what, forty-one? That's not old, that's ancient."

"Straight for the gut, huh?" He sighs, rubbing the back of his head. "You never mince your words."

"If it makes you feel better, you don't look that old," I shrug. "I'd say thirty-two? Or something. I say you still have a chance with Kaa-san."

"That's not the issue here," He groans.

"Though, her type is the scary-looking guys, the ones that look angry all the time," I continue to tease him. "And frankly, you're far from scary-looking. So good luck with that."

"And what do you think I look like?" He tries to change the subject, amusing me greatly.

"Smug," I respond. "You always look like you know something nobody else does."

"Is that a good thing?"

"It makes me want to punch you in the face."

"Guess not," He chuckles. "Well, I'll take it as a compliment. Not the worst thing you said about me."

"I'll stop being mean if you want me to," I remind him.

"It's alright, I know you don't mean it anyway," He waves it off. "You want to order more?"

"Nah, I'm full," I stretch my arms with a satisfied sigh. "Food always tastes better when someone else pays for it."

"I'm sure."

I turn my gaze to inspect the restaurant we're in, seeing the dozens of people eating and chatting away. After dealing with the stray, Akiyama made a call to someone before inviting me out to eat. I asked who it was that he spoke to but simply said that someone will come over to clean up the place.

I shrugged and thought nothing of it. Likely a Yakuza, seeing that my uncle probably knows who they are and that he's their ally or friend. Him being a close friend of my parents proves that with my dad seemingly being a lieutenant.

And I doubt the Yakuza would let someone as powerful as him near me if he's not trustworthy. Though, I'm not sure what he is to them. Is he also a Yakuza? If yes, what is he, a lieutenant? Captain? Patriarch?

If not, how did he get so strong, and what faction is he a part of? I'm sure he's gonna tell me everything now, hopefully everything. There's always the chance of people hiding certain stuff from me, like my mother and her assassin background.

"I'm sure you're curious about what you saw earlier," He starts, prompting me to look back at him.

"Aren't you?" I raise a brow. "Believe it or not, I was kicking its ass like nothing. Not exactly normal for a schoolgirl to manhandle monsters like that."

"Fair, but I have context. I've been in this business for years," he says. "You deserve answers more than I do."

"...Should we be talking here?" I ask, glancing at the other people.

"Don't worry, this restaurant is owned by the Majima Family." He assures me. "Only normal people and Yakuza are here. It's safe."

"If you say so." I trust his words and get back on topic. "I guess my first question would be straightforward. Who are you exactly?"

"Heh, reintroduction? I'm Shun Akiyama, CEO of Sky Finance," He says. "...and the treasurer of the Geomijul."

Okay, I've never heard of this specific organization before, and the name sounds… Korean I believe? Some sort of mafia, or something else altogether?

"Geomijul?" I frown.

"It's a secret organization that only a few know about," He explains. "The three factions alongside a lot of other mythology factions don't know about its existence, and we're trying very hard to keep it that way."

"Why?" I ask. "What's the purpose of it? Is it like a secret weapon or something?"

"The opposite," He shakes his head. "The Geomijul was made for people who don't want to be involved with the supernatural. Sacred Gear users and half-humans mostly.

"It was formed by Seong-hui, a Sacred Gear user, so that people who have nowhere to go can live normal lives if they want, to escape from people hunting them down for their powers and abilities," He continues. "There's no telling what would happen if the other factions knew about it, so it's hidden deep in Ijincho, where no one will be able to find it."

I'm assuming the people hunting means devils? They're the only people who do that stuff as far as I know. Though, I'm not sure if Akiyama hates them as much as my mother does, or if he hates them at all. Mother told me that the yakuza - supposedly the good guys - made a deal with the devils and temporarily gave them Kuoh, though they're still being monitored.

And from what I saw so far, they're doing a good job. If this restaurant is owned by the Tojo, then wouldn't a lot of other places be the same? So they have eyes almost everywhere, and that's slightly worrying. I need to be careful when going to dungeons. Would be pretty hard to explain how I suddenly pop in and out of existence in different locations.

Though, now that I think about it, I didn't feel like someone was following me back home today after school. I know the devils would likely do that, so they got scared off? Maybe? I can figure it out later.

"And you're part of them?" I question, absorbing the information. "When did you join?"

"Two decades ago, give or take a few years," He answers. "I was approached due to my Sacred Gear, like any other person in my position."

"You have a Sacred Gear?" My eyes widen a little. "What is it?"

"Heh, that's what gets your attention?" He smiles in amusement. "Yes, I have one. It's the Sacred Gear with the power of the Vermilion Bird, Suzaku. Burning Rebirth."

If they're planning to strike Ichiban now, then it's safe to assume that they'll get Issei too. As soon as I make sure the idiot is safe, I can rest a little bit. Too bad I don't exactly know where he is but asking his parents will tell me enough.

Ichi had a good idea, so I visited the four eyes idiot, did what I had to, took a cab back to the main town, and now I'm right in front of the Hyoudou household, waiting for someone to answer the door.

I really hope he's there. The last thing I want is the fallen getting their grubby hands on him.

The door finally creaks open, the head of a middle-aged woman peeking out, blinking as she spots me.

"Yes?"

"Hi, Hyoudou-san?" I smile politely, prompting her to smile back. "Is your son inside? I'm a classmate of his, and I'd like to talk to him about something."

"Did he peep on you or did anything perverse?" She sighs deeply. "I'm very sorry for my son's inappropriate behavior. I've really tried beating it out of him-"

"Oh, no, not that. We got over that already," I stop her from babbling about how shit her son is. "I just wanna talk to him over something related to a quiz."

"Oh," She blinks. "Well, I'm afraid you just missed him around ten minutes ago."

I freeze for a second.

…Oh no.

"Do you know where he could be?" I ask, keeping my composure.

"I'm sorry, but I don't," She shakes her head. "I found it odd how excited he looked, though. Haven't seen him like that in months."

Realization hits me harder than a bag of bricks as she utters those words. Don't tell me they plan to take him out today?

Fuck.

"Damn it!" I curse with a scowl on my face, surprising the older woman.

Without even elaborating, I dash to the streets, grimacing as I try to sense any kind of magical activity. The sun is already setting, so if he's on a date, then the fallen should strike soon, and I wasn't prepared one bit.

I don't even care if I'm being overly paranoid or not, that he's not actually in danger. If Rias gets to him first and it turns out that Issei has the Boosted Gear, I'd be losing a very, very valuable asset. I will not risk the chance of losing one of the most overpowered weapons to that useless whore.

I need to get that idiot out of there before he gets killed.



(Kalawarner)

Why did she have to be stuck with this idiot?

Well, yes, she knew what her mission was, but why with him specifically? Couldn't she and Raynare switch? Her bitch leader knew that Kalawarner's type was the delinquent-looking ones, not this boring-ass moron.

Honestly, when she first made contact with this Issei, she thought he'd at least show her a good time around town, but nope. He was the most generic highschool boy out of all the other highschool boys, the worst type in her opinion.

When she heard about his perverted nature, she honestly felt a little excited. She likes kinky guys, might've even dragged him to a love hotel and gave him a 'reward' before killing him if he impressed her, but nope.

Turns out he's a pervert in the most basic sense. She expected groping and touching in public at the very least, and she would've let him have his way with her, but all she got were peeping and taking pictures of fucking panties of all things. She's never been drier in her life before.

And it's beginning to genuinely piss her off.

Of course, Raynare had to take the cute one. Her reasons were sound - since this Ichiban boy had the Longinus, the strongest will have to go with him, but it doesn't mean Kala won't get indignant about it.

Mittelt should've gone with him instead. She'd rather be back in their base.

At the very least, this slog of a date is ending, and right now all she needs to do is to lure him to a quiet and empty place to get rid of him. A simple promise of a 'reward' was enough to make him follow her like a lost puppy.

Kalawarner gave Issei a sultry smile, gesturing for him to get closer as she led him to a quiet alley. "You've been a very wonderful date, Issei-kun. I haven't had fun like this in a long time."

"I'm glad," She whispered in his ears. "But I'm sure I can make it even better for you."

She pulled him close, feeling him shiver as she rubbed his crotch. Slowly, another hand snaked around his neck, a dagger of light forming in it. She tried to sense anything nearby, and feeling nothing, her curiosity got the better of her and she pulled his pants a bit to see what's in there.

Only for her to regret it. Could've at least had some fun, but nope. Not even worth it.

And here she thought this day couldn't get any more disappointing.

Ah well. She sighed internally. You can't win every day, Kala. Just get it over with.

...Is what she thought before a spear of ice grazed Issei's cheeks as it soared towards her. Kala managed to evade the attack at the last minute, unleashing her wings flying back. Issei fell on his ass, grunting in pain before widening his eyes at Kalawarner's true appearance.

"K-Kara-chan?" Issei blinked, pupils shrinking. "W-what the hell is this?"

She glanced at the shattered ice spear and growled, ignoring him as her heart pounded wildly. She's been caught, by whom? Was she being followed? Did they just spot her? Did the light spell alert someone nearby? She expected an agent or two, but when she spotted the attacker…

She didn't expect one of the Yakuza Princesses to be there, arm extended with a scowl on her face.

You've got to be kidding me. Kalawarner grimaced. Why her?!

"Get away from him," The girl said coldly, getting closer.

Issei turned around, seeing the girl with a shocked expression. "A-Akane-san?! What are you doing here? What's going on?"

Kalawarner rushed at the defenseless human, wanting to at least use him as a hostage, but sharp agony made itself known in her shoulder, prompting her to cry out in pain before backing off. She glanced at the small circle-shaped hole in her shoulder, blood pouring out of the wound.

"W-what the hell?!" Issei backed away, looking between them. "What's- what's happening?!"

"Get out of here!" The girl shouted at him. "What are you waiting for?! Move it!"

"B-but-"

Kala flew back and threw a spear of light at Issei, causing the Yakuza Princess to rush forward towards him, forming a wall of ice that blocked the attack. With an annoyed click of her tongue, Kalawarner took the chance to escape.

Only for a spear to lodge itself into her leg, prompting her to fall down as the cold pain forced her to lose her balance.

She groaned and grunted, looking back to see the ice-cold look of rage on the girl's face. It made her shiver in terror, recognizing the sadistic glee in that eye of hers, one that Raynare would show when torturing someone.

"Oi, Akane, what's going on?! W-why are you hurting Karla-chan?!" Issei suddenly said, grabbing the girl by the arm.

"What are you- Why are you still here?!" She scowled and pulled her arm away, making him flinch. "This is too dangerous for you, go!"

"B-but I-"

"I'll explain everything later, just go," She said, a little calmer. "Now leave-"

A click was heard in the distance, followed by a deafening bang. Akane acted quickly and formed another ice wall in front of her and Issei, and this time, Kala did everything in her power to fly away from the battlefield.

A glance back showed her the Saio Triad member, Ed, Who had joined them for revenge against Amamiya, emerging from another alley with a gun in his hand, taking the attention of the two away from the fallen.

Took his fucking time.

Fat Bastard.

10 Obedience with Issei Hyoudou [35/100]

Thankfully, I'm fast enough to casually dodge them, so easily in fact that I'm able to actually see the bullets mid-air. When I attacked using magic, I barely did any damage, but with the bat…

He's down by more than 10k only in two hits to the head, when a whole row of ice spells barely did 5k. Is he resistant to magic?

I duck under a swing and step back, making him growl in anger. "You bitch!"

So I should use my magic sparingly. If it's not effective as a pure offense, then maybe I should use it defensively, or in a way that would slow him down.

I glance at my HP and frown. I'm low, a few hits I perfectly defend against and I'm at 500. A single, direct hit will end me instantly.

Thank you for the ice wings spell, Game.

I tighten my grip over the bat, feeling my heart pounding in my chest. I recast ice skin, focusing on evolving the spell as fast as I can while keeping an eye on the fatass. I can feel the spell improving immensely by the second, and a new notification from the system makes me smile.

[Cryomancy: Ice Flesh] - Skill

The standard defensive spell for Cryomancer. Imbue your soft flesh with magic, hardening it in an instant and increasing your defense by quite a bit.

Protects 750 HP worth of damage before shattering. Takes half as much damage from Ice but double damage from Fire

Costs 200 MP for each body part

I tighten my grip over the bat as he rushes forward, but then a bolt of lightning hits him in the side, interrupting his attack. I turn to the side and see Akeno standing there with an easy smile, alongside Rias and her peerage.

Really? Just as I make a new spell, someone decides to show up?

And it had to be the devils.

"That's enough, whoever you are," Rias commands. "I don't know who you think you are, but I suggest you come with us quietly, or we'll force you to comply."

"Devil bastards…" Ed growls in annoyance as he sees all of them, giving me one hateful glare. "This isn't over, Amamiya."

With that, he quickly throws something on the ground, and an explosion of smoke engulfs all of us. The cloud was big enough to cloak the whole street, and as soon as I breathed into it, I flinched violently, feeling my mana suddenly going haywire.

Anti-magic? Does such a thing exist?

"He has low magic," I clarify. "You'd barely feel it even if you got close to him."

So much for being bodyguards.



(Akiyama)

As he watched the whole scene unfold on the giant screen, he frowned deeply. He didn't want to be stuck here just watching with his hands tied - he really, really wanted to support his niece against that Saio Triad officer. He had no idea where he came from or what he's doing here. That organization was destroyed over a decade ago, but after getting filled in…

Well, he's really glad that he convinced Mizuki to stop babying her daughter too much. Of course, some people will try to take revenge on Tatsu, even if he's dead. Hurting his family is the one thing that will absolutely, 100% piss him off, and Tatsu isn't merciful like Kiryu is.

He will rip you apart with his bare hands and make you suffer, but seeing that he's currently six feet under, he's not able to do such a thing. Mizuki can handle herself, the Tojo Clan will do everything in its power to protect Akane, but is this something they can truly rely on forever?

The world is dangerous. Getting overly dependent on one thing is a sure way of dying a slow and painful death. The Tojo Clan and the Omi Alliance will not be here forever. Tatsu's contribution will not be forever remembered, and what then?

Tatsu pissed off a lot of people before his death, yakuza and supernatural races alike. He butted heads with the Church, Fallen Angels, and Devils. He made a lot of enemies, and even though most of them aren't stupid enough to poke the Tojo, there are the odd ones out who will do everything to hurt him.

And here was one example.

This is why he tried to convince Mizuki to get her daughter to train - why he plans to convince Mizuki to break the seal on her own powers, risks be damned. The world is changing, it's becoming more and more dangerous with every passing day, and if they're stuck like this, there's no chance they'll survive.

His gut told him that there's something brewing in the background, something big. Maybe it was just his paranoia talking, but his long years of working with the supernatural had taught him to trust his paranoia more often than not.

But even then, unlike the grinning Mad Dog next to him, Akiyama knows what moderation is. Akane, regardless of her growth, is still a beginner. She's not ready to face assassins or supernatural creatures just yet. For fuck's sake, she just started actual training just a few days ago.

For sure, the girl handled herself very well against a veteran, unleashing a highly-skilled spell that even Mizuki never learned like that wing spell. Not to mention the strange spatial magic with how she summoned that golden baseball bat.

But she's not ready. She's young, she's impulsive and naive, nowhere near powerful enough to fight off actual assassins.

When the battle started, Akiyama tried to rush in to save his niece, but he's not exactly strong enough to fight off the Mad Dog and his entire family. Not to mention, this little underground surveillance room isn't really an optimal place to fight in, especially not with his skillset.

Though it's not like he had a chance anyway.

Majima merely told him to "Shut the fuck up and watch."

"As much as I understand your point of view, I can't agree with it, Majima-san," Akiyama said. "She's not ready yet."

"And she'll never be ready if ya keep this shit up," He argued. "Shit's hitting the fan soon, Akiyama. Can't afford ta take it slow with Akane-chan anymore."

"So you gamble on her life?" Akiyama narrowed his eyes. "Risk to see if she's worthy or not? Is that how you do things?"

Majima remained silent.

"She's not part of your Family, Majima," Akane's uncle frowned deeply. "Don't treat her like she is."

"She ain't, cuz I know that she's worthy," Majima responded with a grin. "Ya just ain't seein' it."

"What?"

"What did ya see when ya watched the fight?" The Mad Dog asked suddenly.

"I…" Akiyama blinked, confused. "I'm not sure what you're trying to say."

"Look at this," He said, pointing at the screen as it zoomed into her face. "Whaddya see?"

Akiyama couldn't understand, but responded as best he could. "I see her scared out of her mind as she tries to fight for her life."

"That's why ya'd make for a lousy yakuza," Majima laughed. "Y'know what I see? I see Tatsu-chan."

The CEO of Sky Finance stopped, beginning to understand what the Majima Family Patriarch was trying to tell him.

"She's scared shitless, that's true, but her eyes are mighty fierce, more so than her pops," He said. "That's a look I've only seen on four people, Akiyama, and all of em' achieved great things."

"If shit gets too bad, I'll get involved," He shrugged. "I ain't unfair. I get that there are things she can't handle yet, but this? I expect her ta deal with it with her eyes closed."

"Is this one of Daigo's games?"

"Hehe, naw, this is all me," Majima chuckled. "Man, Mizuki-chan is gonna be pissed, ain't she?"

Akiyama turned to look at the screen again, the camera switching to the one near the abandoned church. He grimaced as he saw the wounded fallen get inside, likely alerting everything.

Apparently, Majima and the family knew already but decided to remain ignorant and passive so the Fallen could get bold with their plans. It's all part of the Mad Dog's 'training regimen' he prepared for his niece seemingly.

So then she'll have to deal with everything on her own here? This whole strange fiasco with Fallen Angels trying to for some reason kill random Sacred Gear users? What the hell is Azazel doing right now?

Regardless, Akiyama is not looking forward to the ass-kicking he'll be receiving once Mizuki hears about this.
