#245
(Rias)

Frankly, she had not expected that this would be how their first meeting would go. Here she was in the clubroom, trying to find a way to approach one of the heiresses without accidentally stepping on her toes, in a way that wouldn't make her look like she had an agenda.

Because she isn't! Rias doesn't only want to get on good terms with the girls because it's beneficial to her, but because she genuinely wants to know more about them. One of them is the foster daughter of a previous chairman, and the other has the blood of a yuki-onna, one of the rarest Yokai to ever exist. She'd love to learn what kind of lives they led up to this point.

Yes, she has the files on her, but those aren't detailed enough, and it's a lot better to hear it from her. Besides, there's a huge chance that the Yakuza fabricated a lot of the information on those.

So after drawing a blank, Rias decided to cut her losses for the day and go home, perhaps she'll think of a better plan tomorrow morning. Until she sensed a sudden spike of magic in the distance. At first, Akeno advised her to stay and wait it out, thinking that the Yakuza would handle it.

But then it became clear that whoever was using magic wanted to be sensed. They did not put a lid on the spells at all, making it obvious to sense by even the inexperienced bunch. This was some kind of a call for help, it had to be.

And in technicality, Kuoh temporarily belongs to the devils until they finish their education, so it was her responsibility to find out what was going on. The Yakuza don't have any reason to stop them considering the contract, so she took her whole peerage - minus one - and headed towards the dark streets.

Well, she doesn't quite know what 'dark' is, devils can see in the dark after all. She just assumed it was, as none of the lights were on for some reason. Perhaps the Fallen's doing to make it easier to escape.

And when they arrived, lo and behold, one of the heiresses was fighting for her life against an unknown assailant. Rias had a lot of questions when she saw the scene for the first time. Like, a lot.

Why is Amamiya fighting this mysterious assailant, and why is she using magic proficiently? Where are the Yakuza? What kind of enemy is that and why is he after the girl? Why does he have anti-magic technology, something exclusive to the Tojo Clan and Omi Alliance?

After they drove him off, unfortunately being unable to catch him, Rias invited the girl over for a quick debrief of what happened and called Sona over, now that the curtains are lifted. None of them need to hide who they are, and frankly, Rias prefers that.

And look at this, Akane already knows what they are, so they can cut to the chase.

Once they've made their way to the clubroom, Rias made sure to show the girl hospitality worthy of a duchess. Human or not, this is one of the most important figures in the supernatural world right now, especially with the Yakuza's rapid rise to power with their advanced technology.

Akane showed a neutral face, clearly cautious but not worried. As her Queen put a tray in front of the three heiresses, she bowed and gave the human girl a polite smile. Akane merely glanced at her silently before turning her gaze back to Rias.

She's anxious but not as anxious as Rias expected. More on guard rather than worried.

"I didn't expect our first meeting to be like this," Rias started, trying to ease the tension. "But I suppose anything can happen."

Sona grimaced as Akane stared at her silently for a few, painful seconds, then responded.

"You're not good at small talk, are you?"

Rias blushed in embarrassment at the blunt reply but managed to keep her cool. "I think this is a perfectly valid way of breaking the ice.."

"Let's just skip it and ask what you want to ask," The human girl sighed. "Don't make it painful for both of us."

Sona smiled a little and Akeno giggled in the background as Rias cleared her throat.

"Well, if you say so." She nodded. "What were you doing so late at night? How did you attract the attention of that man? And who is he?"

"Nothing much," Akane responded. "I was taking a walk before the guy jumped me. I don't know who he is or what I did to piss him off, but I had to defend myself."

"You were at the edge of town, taking a walk?" Sona raised a brow. "What brought you so far away from the center, where everything is?"

"As I said, I took a walk," Akane frowned. "Why would I try to seek out people who could hurt me? If I wanted to beat up somebody, I'd drag one of the idiots who think they're hot shit into an alley and kick their asses."

"That's, uh, oddly specific? But anyway, we only want to know why you were so far away. These parts of the city are dangerous." Rias pressed.

"To regular people, yeah," She crossed her arms, frown deepening a little. "I can handle myself."

"But-"

"This line of questioning isn't gonna help your case, Gremory," Akane cut her off harshly. "Drop it before you say something you regret."

Rias flinched at the hostility, not expecting such a response before she decided to forget it. Perhaps the girl was just nervous, it isn't wise to let something like this get to her head.

"Alright, very well," Sona dropped it for her. "Let's change the subject. Amamiya-san, I have a request."

Akane raised a brow, prompting her to continue.

"I'd like it if we are able to assist you in case such a thing happens again," Sona said. "Kuoh, while ultimately belonging to the Tojo Clan, is our grounds as well. It'd be irresponsible of us if we let anyone get hurt in it."

"Well, I'm not gonna refuse help," Akane shrugged. "Appreciated."

Success!

"But we'd like the same from you as well," The Gremory heiress pressed.

Sona stilled as she frantically glanced at her friend, but Rias knew what she was doing. The best way to get close to her is to fight by each other's side, right? Even two people hating each other can get over it if they fought together a few times.

"Since Kuoh technically belongs to all of us, I think we should all do our parts to protect it," Rias suggested. "And what better way than working together as a team?"

"Rias…" Sona warned quietly. "Don't push your luck."

"A team?" Akane parroted.

"Yes. All three of us are important to our respective factions," Rias nodded, ignoring her friend's warning. "Meaning assassins from all over the realms might come after us. Wouldn't it be logical to defend each other? Three are better than one after all."

The girl only stared at her, looking seemingly bewildered for a few seconds before uttering in confusion. "Uh, I-I'm sorry?"

"Eh?" Rias blinked in confusion.

"Please don't mind her," Sona quickly interjected. "She can be quite naive sometimes. Just ignore her."

"Sona?!"

"Right, I can see that," Akane responded, looking more annoyed, which only left the heiress puzzled. "Look, I get your offer, and I appreciate it, but I'd also appreciate it more if you kept your distance. That's all I'm asking."

"We understand and respect that." Sona nodded, giving Rias a scary glare as she tried to open her mouth to speak up again, quickly shutting her down. "We will not bother you in any way concerning the matter, but keep in mind that we will help as soon as you give us a call."

"Cool, so can I go now?" Akane said, standing up. "I promised someone I'd meet up with them soon."

"Of course," Sona nodded. "Would you like an escort?"

"No thanks. I know the way out."

"Very well. Always a pleasure to talk to you, Amamiya-san."

The human girl waved and gave Sona a tiny smile, the door closing behind her as she left the clubroom. As a few seconds passed, the Sitri heiress took off her glasses and rubbed the bridge of her nose as she leaned back.

Rias was confused at her friend's sudden change in character, and couldn't help but ask loudly. The redhead clearly had it. If Sona hadn't interrupted, then they could've gotten closer to her.

"You know, it's not like you to start brown-nosing," Rias spoke, a little more aggressive than she intended.

"Brown-nosing?" Sona uttered, then scowled. "For the love of Lucifer, Rias, you were this close to destroying any bridges we built with her!"

"Eh?"

"When will you realize that she is not our friend, she is not a random human we can converse with like this? She's one of the most important human figures in the Yakuza," Sona explained, looking frustrated. "She does not trust us, Rias, and we're on her turf. Anything you say can be used against you, and you decide to demand assistance from her?!"

"W-wha- I didn't demand anything!" Rias frowned deeply. "I've only suggested that we work together-"

"Context, Rias!" Sona cut her off with an uncharacteristic yell, making her flinch. "The context! Take a moment to consider where we are, who we are to her, and what the Devils did to her family!"

"Y-you're just being unreasonable," Rias scoffed. "Everyone knows that the Old Satans are at fault!"

"And you think she cares? For all she knows, all devils are the same. Being reasonable or not isn't the main concern, it's how we handle someone who we know has severe anger issues," Sona argued. "Talking to her is like walking around a minefield, and you decided to take a damned marathon. What the hell were you thinking?!"

"So what are we supposed to do?!" The redhead challenged. "Spend the whole time walking on eggshells, trying to appease her?!"

"What we're supposed to do is make sure she doesn't have a reason to distrust us, then try to be 'friends' with her," Sona deflected easily, making Rias flinch. "From her point of view, you might as well have demanded that she risk her own life for you in her own home."

Rias flinched as she realized what Sona was trying to get at, her scowl dropping as she tried to come up with an excuse. Was she really in the wrong? She just asked for assistance to try and get close to her that way, she didn't mean to push her way.

"But that's not what I-..." Rias faltered. "I-I just thought that…"

"Just do what she says and keep your distance," Sona sighed tiredly. "Your peerage too. Give her some time to adjust to Devils being in her school."

Rias frowned sadly and guiltily looked down, unable to form words of apology. She really screwed this up, didn't she? Not knowing what to say, the redhead decided to change the subject for now.

"W-what about the man who attacked her?" Rias questioned, calming herself down. "Do you reckon we should try to find them? They couldn't have gone far."

"Yes, as long as we don't send anyone to observe Akane, we can tighten security by using our peerages," Sona nodded, putting her glasses on once again. "I'll send a few to the spot where she was attacked. We're clearly missing something if the Yakuza never went to Akane's aid."

"Alright, I'll have Koneko accompany them," Rias said. "Let's hope we're able to intercept them. Knowing they have Anti-magic is concerning."

Sona nodded at her Queen, giving a silent order to tell the rest as Rias did the same with Akeno. The two Queens bowed respectfully and left the room, prompting Sona to stand up from her seat.

"I-I'm sorry," Rias muttered, stopping her best friend. "I-I guess I didn't really realize how different this is, compared to being regarded so highly in the underworld."

It was different; Rias is a Gremory, a ducal clan and one of the highest rankings in the underworld, so as an heiress, she has a lot of authority. It had never truly sunk in that such a title isn't much respected where she is right now, and in fact, might work against her.

It's a well-known fact what the Old Satans did to the Yakuza years ago, after conspiring with other parties to take out certain figures in the Tojo Clan and Omi Alliance. The incident ruined the New Satans' relationship with the human factions, making them incredibly hostile for three years straight.

Any devil that would set foot on the human world would get vaporized, and that's a best-case scenario. Earth itself became uninhabitable for devils because of it, and her brother did not want a war with the humans, because even if they won, they'd be too weak to handle the Fallen and Seraphim.

Thankfully, after some time, Daigo himself offered a truce, which they took. Most of the time since has been spent to mend their relationship after that incident, which then led to them acquiring Kuoh temporarily. Not everyone was happy about this, but it was something.

It was naive of her to think that everything was fine now that she reflects on it, but she didn't expect this much hostility and distrust from Akane. From what she knew, Sona was able to easily converse with her earlier, and she showed no signs of those feelings at all.

Sona's expression softened, seemingly unable to stay angry at Rias when she saw how genuinely remorseful she looked. Well, hopefully. She didn't look angry anymore, so it's safe to assume that she's fine now?

"That's alright, Rias. We all make mistakes." Sona said, showing a side that only Rias and her sister knew about. "Just keep in mind that we're indebted to the Yakuza, therefore to Akane, someone who very clearly distrusts us greatly. Anything you think is fine to say might come off as pretentious or arrogant."

"Does she even have the authority to kick us out?" Rias questioned genuinely. "From what I know, she has never been truly involved with the Tojo Clan personally."

"She can. The moment she feels unsafe or in danger around us, she can tell the chairman that she suspects treachery, which will not only end the deal but possibly worsen the relationship between the factions. We don't need any more animosity with her." Sona nodded, standing up. "I'll be going along with some of the girls to scout the area and make sure Kuoh is protected in case of another attack."

"Alright, good luck."

With that, Sona left the clubroom, leaving Rias on her own. The redhead sighed and brought her hands up to cover her face, finally getting her much-needed wake-up call. She shouldn't be too hasty, or close calls like this will keep happening, and she doesn't need stress for that right now with the upcoming wedding already making her feel terrible.

Damned devils and their stupid traditions.



(Akane)

I'm not gonna pretend to know a lot about politics. Frankly, I'm just lost when they start talking that stupid language, but I do know how people function, and from the looks of it, Devils are very similar to humans in that regard.

Every time I talk to somebody, I automatically hyperfocus on their body movement and tone. Some are easily able to hide it even from me, like my uncle or mother, for the most part, others… not so much. And I gotta say, I expected better from Sona.

Two: To remind them of who I fucking am, and how much they technically owe me.

Lying fuck.

Maybe they should work on that. I don't want to deal with idiot muggers every time I decide to take a walk at night.

Or assassins, or supernatural creatures.

Or both.

"What?" She freezes, looking at me in bewilderment.

"Yeah, weird. Thought they only looked after themselves, or that's what you said anyway," I shrug. "It turns out they actually care."

"I- well…" She sighs and shakes her head. "Doesn't matter, I'm just glad you're safe."

She embraces me again, this time not as rough as before, but she certainly takes her time. I don't know what to say exactly, still a little awkward from the fight we had yesterday, so I do what I do best and be blunt.

"Can you let go now?" I sigh.

"R-right." She says awkwardly, letting go of me. "Um, about what happened that night…"

"That's not what I-" She groans in frustration. "Can you please let me finish first?"

I give her a nod, gesturing for her to continue.

"I-I just wanna say I'm sorry," Mizuki says. "I shouldn't have. It wasn't right to do any of that."

I remain silent.

"But I just couldn't help it. I was so worried the whole time, I couldn't even think anymore." She looks away with a hurt expression. "Those looks you sometimes have bring back bad, bad memories, ones I don't want to ever remember, y'know? I felt something was wrong, I had to know if you had them too."

She pauses for a few seconds then answers. "Akane, you know we have yokai blood, but while yuki-onna aren't the kindest, my father's side of the family is… well, horrible, to put it simply."

"Horrible how? If they're something so much worse than yokai, why are we mostly human?"

I guess that implies that the Yokai heritage came from my grandmother's side. Good to know I guess.

I blink in surprise.

…What the fuck is my family tree?

"We come from a long line of sadistic, egotistical, and bloodthirsty monsters - they have killed thousands of people with smiles on their faces," My mother explains. "And admittedly, I was never able to get rid of the same disgusting urges that drove them. Even today, while I've learned how to fully control them, I still feel it whispering sometimes."

…Alright, that explains some stuff.

I trust you, Akane, with all my heart, I know you'd never be like them, but seeing that same look on your face scares me so much."

She looks ashamed, tears in the corners of her eyes as she admits that. Now I'm not particularly mad, more intrigued than anything. What kind of family did she come from? Yuki-No-Onna and now whatever that is. A strange combination.

Likely has to do with her past job as an assassin, and while I'd like to inquire more about it, I think I'm getting closer to the truth anyway. If I want to regain my AFF with her, I need to, unfortunately, play patient.

She's like a puppy, I swear.

I'm supposed to be the daughter here, so why am I being a mom right now?

"I'm sorry."

5 Affection with Mizuki Amamiya [95/100]

-10 Obedience with Mizuki Amamiya [50/100]

Though, to be honest, I'm not sure how that would help me either. With how high her affection is, I can probably get whatever I want from her anyway. Trying to up her obedience will probably be unnecessarily difficult with little to no reward. I'd likely get a perk similar to the one I got from the glasses idiot, and it doesn't look like it's worth the trouble.

We'll see. I have other things I need to deal with first.

Well shit. Busted.



(Issei)

He looked over the window in worry, still shaken up and unsure of exactly what had occurred earlier. Both of his parents were out, which he was thankful for because he wasn't ready to explain whatever the fuck went on down there, but he also didn't feel safe alone, even at home.

Kala-chan wanted to hurt him? She had wings, she could shoot light from her hands - she clearly wasn't human. But why? What did he do? Did he anger the wrong person somehow? Pissing people off isn't particularly difficult, but he kept most of the perverted tendencies in school, never out of it.

Honestly, he wasn't sure he'd survive that, but then his classmate came along, equally supernatural with her control over ice, and drove the big-titted winged girl out before the big bald man tried to shoot them.

That's a sentence he never thought was gonna form in his head, but here he is.

What the hell is going on here, and why do people want to kill him?

Maybe his mom was right. He should've stopped the perverted antics. First, it got his friends sent to the hospital - one with busted balls - got his ass handed to him, and now weird winged chicks with huge tits want to kill him.

The girl was crazy, but then she apologized to him later, so maybe she isn't that bad. To be fair, he and his friends were the ones who started it with their peeping.

Regardless, he didn't want to see her genuinely hurt. The bald man looked terrifying, and a part of Issei felt absolutely guilty for not trying to help her out. He's a guy, guys are supposed to protect girls, right?

Instead, he turned tail and ran, but what was he supposed to do in that situation? That psycho had a gun for fuck's sake. The police can handle it, right? He's sure they were gonna apprehend that fat bastard - Kuoh Police are fucking fierce.

He rubbed his eyes then turned over to look at his phone, grimacing as his parents still didn't read his message yet, prompting him to send another one. Where the hell did they go?

Issei gazed out of the window nervously and he saw his classmate standing at the front door, meeting his eyes and giving him a blank look. Issei blinked a few times then quickly made his way to her, opening the door for her.

Not knowing what to say, Issei spoke awkwardly. "H-hi?"

Akane snorted, ignoring his greeting. "I'm sure you have a lot of questions about what just happened."

"Yeah," He nodded, then quickly stepped aside. "Oh, uh, you can come in. My parents aren't home."

She came inside, still expressionless as Issei led her to the living room. For some reason, the air felt a little colder now, but that didn't come close to how awkward the atmosphere was, and how uncomfortable it felt.

He could feel her staring at him from behind, and it intimidated him a little too much. Issei cleared his throat and spoke up again, trying to clear the tension maybe.

"So um, would you like anything to drink or…?"

"No."

"Oh, okay."

Well, that didn't help. In fact, it just made everything worse. Might as well get to the point.

It seems she had a similar idea as she started explaining to him what that was all about, not even bothering to take a seat.

"Everything you saw back there was real. It's not a prank, a joke, or anything like that." She said, crossing her arms. "To make a long story short; most of the supernatural things you have heard about from stories exist. Devils, gods, magic, etcetera. Those things are real."

"Oh." Issei's eyes widened, unsure if he heard right. "I-I see."

Oh wow, okay. That was a bombshell if he had ever heard one. He figured that it might be something like that after what happened earlier, but to hear it stated as a fact was mind-blowing. And he had lived most of his life ignorant somehow?

Does the rest of the world know? From the looks of it, the supernatural things seem to be hidden, but that doesn't really explain why he was attacked.

"What you just saw, the girl with black wings, was a Fallen Angel." Akane elaborated. "Part of a relatively neutral organization led by a Fallen Angel."

"A- a Fallen Angel?" Issei parroted. "Kala-chan was an Angel?"

"You saw her wings, didn't you?" She raised a brow. "And I'm pretty sure you saw her use Light Magic. How is that hard to comprehend?"

"No, but I mean, an angel!" He said. "But wait, why did she try to kill me? Did I do something bad?"

"Fallen Angel, and it was because you have something within you," Akane responded. "The Fallen would never target a random pervert for no reason, but you're no random pervert. You have a Sacred Gear."

"Huh?" He uttered in confusion. "What is a Sacred Gear?"

"Superpowers given to selected humans upon birth," She explained. "You haven't awakened yours, so they wanted to kill you before you could."

"B-but why? I never even knew about any of this stuff before this!" This only served to confuse him more. "I-I would've lived my life not knowing anything at all- I would've never tried to interact with them!"

In all honesty, this frightened Issei a lot. He was targeted because of something he had no control over? If Akane hadn't arrived, he would've most definitely died, but seeing that he got away, does that mean they'll try again?

Will they target his family too? Do his parents have 'Sacred Gears' as well? Now he's not saying he's blaming Akane for this, of course not. He's eternally grateful that she actually risked her own life to save him, but now what? Is he gonna have to live in fear? Are they gonna try to kill him again?

"Calm down, it's not your fault," She said, "To be honest, it's a bit strange that they decided to kill you. The Fallen aren't usually anywhere near aggressive as this - they're more likely to try to recruit you than kill you."

"T-then why?"

"I don't know that either." Akane shrugged.

"What am I supposed to do then?" Issei questioned, desperate for an answer. "A-are they gonna hunt me down again?"

"Just relax, man." She groaned in frustration, making him flinch. "I saved you once, I'm not gonna let my efforts be in vain and have you killed the next day."

"Eh?" He blinked.

"What I just told you doesn't come close to being everything that's happening out there," She elaborated. "You have a Sacred Gear, so kiss living a normal life goodbye. If you want to live, then you need to know all about the supernatural world and how it works."

Issei didn't respond to that, opting to listen.

"Early tomorrow, before the sun rises, come over to the abandoned warehouse northwest of Kuoh," She told him, putting her hands in her coat's pockets. "Assuming you're interested in learning more about your power and the truth of the world you live in, of course. You're free to ignore me and go on about your business."

Issei nodded silently.

"I'll leave you to it then. You're probably overwhelmed enough as it is," She said, heading towards the door. "See ya."

"Wait," He stopped her. "Thank you for saving my life. I owe you."

She merely waved and exited through the front door, leaving Issei to his thoughts. He had a lot to think about, especially about her offer. He has superpowers he never knew about? That's reassuring - at least he's not completely defenseless against myths and legends that are apparently trying to kill him. Or, at least, he doesn't have to be.

He paused to think for a moment, a smile forming on his face.

…Does that mean his dream is possible?

Could Issei Hyoudou become the Harem King?

(Ichiban)

Last night had been strange, to say the least. His best friend was acting pretty weird all things considered, from being curious where Issei - someone who she said she disliked - lives, to not showing up when she said they could hang out together. It wasn't like her to go against her words like this, but he understood.

Unlike before in Kamurocho, where they had been relatively young, carefree, and had practically had nothing to do, she had responsibilities here. He didn't mind it, because at the very least she still texted him and apologized for not being able to make it. Ichiban won't hold it against her.

Though, then he got a weirder text message. A cryptic 'Come to the abandoned warehouse northwest of Kuoh' garnered his confusion. When he asked if there was something up, Akane told him that she had something important to tell him.

And Ichiban wasn't about to question it. If his friend didn't elaborate via text, then that meant she preferred to tell him in person. He didn't mind. Not like he had anything better to do. He would've appreciated it if she didn't tell him to come over so early in the morning though, but oh well. At least it would at least help him get used to his new routine of waking up early.

Fucking school.

Something did feel off, though. It felt a lot more serious than usual. He was no empath, but he sometimes could recognize different tones even in texts, so he had made sure to not waste any time and woke up early, passing by a convenience store on the way for breakfast, then jogging over to the designated place.

His training with his patriarch's captain made him feel the disturbance around him, feeling like he was being watched. Ichiban was no slouch, but he recognized the presence isn't something he could deal with, so he hurried over to the warehouse, worried that his friend might be in danger, even though the presence didn't quite feel malicious.

Something was pretty off about this place, and he wasn't sure he liked it.

With a quick glance behind, Ichiban knocked on the door as another hand ran through his afro, nervous sweat trailing down his cheek. "Yo, Akane, are you there?"

He heard something or someone inside, but couldn't make out what they said. After a few more seconds, the door opened slowly and a familiar face poked out. Akane's mother froze and stared at the boy for a bit as a wide smile appeared on her face.

"Mizuki-san?" Ichiban muttered.

Before he could even continue further, the older woman had both of her hands on his shoulders.

"No way, is that you, Icchan?" She asked before hugging him tightly. "It's been so long~! Look at you, all grown up~"

"Unfhf?!" His eyes widened, rapidly losing breath as she brought his head close to her chest, almost suffocating.

"What's with the afro? It's not the sixties, Icchan. You're too late for that kind of look," She said with a giggle, seemingly unaware that he's currently dying in a… nice way. "Ah well, I still think it looks good on you."

"C-can't breathe!" He managed to get out, face becoming beet red from lack of breath and embarrassment.

"Oh, oops," She quickly let go of him, scratching her cheek with a nervous chuckle. "Sorry, sometimes I forget about my own strength."

That's not the issue. He thought with a gasp as he tried to look anywhere that was not her chest.

"I-it's fine," He said, catching his breath. "It's nice to see you again, Mizuki-san."

"Likewise! Never thought I'd see you again in all honesty," She patted his head with a grin. "What are you doing in Kuoh anyway?"

"I, uh, got accepted into Kuoh Academy," He responded truthfully.

"For real?" She looked a little surprised before ruffling his hair. "Hehe, that's my Icchan. I knew you were pretty bright from the day I laid eyes on you. That's why I let you be friends with Akane."

He blushed at the compliment and rubbed his neck bashfully, not used to hearing such genuine kindness. "T-thanks, the entrance exam was pretty tough, but I got through it."

"That's good to hear." She nodded, stepping aside to let him in. "Come in, Akane is waiting for you inside."

"Do you know why she called me here?" Ichiban questioned in curiosity as he stepped inside.

"Nope, no idea. I just got here myself and I don't know why she's called me here either." Mizuki sighed, running a hand through her hair. "Wish I could go to bed. Barely had a wink last night."

Same. Ichiban smiled in sympathy.

Mizuki closed the door behind them, and Ichiban took his time to view his surroundings. Unlike the outside, where the warehouse looked abandoned from its cracked walls and rusted pipes, the inside was the complete opposite. It made him do a double-take, glancing around to see the walls and floors in pristine condition, multiple pieces of familiar gym equipment, and even some he has never seen before.

"Up, over here," Akane called out to him from above, prompting him to look up to see only an open second floor.

He couldn't exactly tell where she was, so he followed her mother up the stairs, seeing his best friend wearing her sportswear under a black track jacket, calmly sitting on a couch in front of a 4k TV with a steaming mug in her hand. On the other side of said couch was none other than Issei with just a simple red T-shirt and jeans. This confused him even more - why is Issei there? What is this place? What the hell is going on? Last he checked, Akane didn't like the pervert.

And between them was an adorable girl he didn't recognize. With blond hair and big green eyes, she wore a simple blue blouse and a white skirt, she looked like a foreigner. The girl looked a little nervous, eyes darting around before her gaze landed at him. She gave a small and shy smile, prompting him to do the same.

"Good morning," Akane said, putting her mug on the coffee table in front of her. "Sorry for dragging you out early like this."

"It's cool." He waved it off. "What's this place?"

"My secret hideout," Akane answered. "You look pretty confused."

"That's one way to put it." Ichiban smiled a little, scratching the back of his head as his gaze turned to the nervous-looking Issei. "Yo, how are you doing?"

"Huh? Oh, I'm good, thanks." Issei responded, clearly not expecting a civil greeting from him.

"How's the nose?" Ichiban asked cheekily, his smile turning mischievous.

Akane snorted in amusement as Issei sighed. "Still hurts, but better. Thanks for backing me up, by the way."

"It's cool, not like that's the first time I stopped her from doing something stupid."

Giving the blond one last glance, she silently responds with a nod, prompting us to rush out of the alleyway as we circle around the church, trying to find a backdoor or something. We avoid the stained glass to remain discreet as you're able to see through it easily, spotting one of the Fallen patrolling the area near the side, prompting us to immediately back away. It was the loli one, thankfully unaware of our presence.

Fortunately, she's on foot, likely thinking that flight could attract too much attention, which is perfect.

I quietly cast Ice Bullet, blanking its magical presence before aiming at her head. A single shot to the back of her skull is enough to kill her silently. We can drag the body somewhere else so nobody notices.

Ichi looks at me with a frown, then nods. He doesn't like it, but there's no other choice, and he knows that. Knocking her out is way too risky and could alert the others.

As soon as she is away from the stained glass, I shoot her in the back of the head, ending her life instantly and silently as the bullet penetrates her skull. She limply falls down, blood pouring on the ground beneath her.

Level up!

Issei flinches at the sight, then Ichiban puts a hand on his shoulder to calm him down.

"I know it's hard, but try to relax," Ichi whispers, trying to soothe him. "There isn't much we could've done."

Issei takes a moment to register what he said, still staring at the Fallen's corpse, but then nods slowly. He's taking it very well, I'm actually kind of impressed. Nonetheless, I do give him an extra moment to take it in, then I signal for them to get closer.

"Boost me up," I whisper. "We don't have much time until they notice something is off, but I can see some windows up on the walls of the hall - I'll try to get another shot from there. I'll give you a rough estimate of their numbers with a text, and as soon as you see one of them fall, rush them and destroy them. Remember, keep an eye out on that fat guy, he's really tough."

They nod seriously and listen to my orders. With Ichi's strength alongside my own, I'm able to jump very high and grab the ledge of the lower portion of the roof before pulling myself up. I crouch against the wall of the higher, central hall, peeking through the stained-glass window to get a better look.

I see around perhaps forty or fifty exorcists, the two other Fallen, and Ed all inside the place. All of them were disguised in casual outfits, likely to hide from the Yakuza in case they get too close, and they're completely ignorant of what just happened to one of their own, or what's about to happen now. It's almost funny really.

I texted Ichi what I saw, and once he relayed the info to Issei, he gave me a thumbs up. All set.

I aim another bullet at that Ed idiot, silently debating with myself whether I should risk it and shoot him instead of one of the other Fallen Angels, before changing my target. No, I know he's resistant to magic - it's not wise to try a sneak attack on him like that, especially seeing how much HP he has.

I aim at the healthier of the two - the only male Fallen in the group. The other one is still injured and her stats are pretty horrible all around. She's not really a threat at all - I could probably beat her without using any of my ice spells.

And once I take a deep breath.

I shoot.

The man falls down, blood and gray matter splattering on the walls as everyone inside was too shocked to react. However, my allies are quick to respond, shattering the stained glass as they leap through it. The enemy is too disoriented to react, panicking as they try to defend themselves from the two, but it doesn't help when I support Ichiban and Issei by raining down ice spells from above, slaughtering most of the Stray exorcists.

In mere seconds, their numbers were cut down to less than five. Only the big bastard and Kalawarner, who had her back against the wall as she watched the horrific scene unfold before her eyes.

I smirk widely. We got them good~

Level up! X4

Choose a new primary class!

Note: All EXP will be accumulated until you choose a new class

30 Reputation with Goro Majima [50/100]

Huh?

I shake the notification off and put my head back to the game.

Holy fuck.

…That was kinda anticlimactic. I know I told him to end it quickly, but he could've done something cool.

Ichi takes a step back before falling on his knees in exhaustion, letting go of the bat before letting out a deep sigh of relief. Ignoring the minor hiccup at the end, we completely crushed them. We didn't need help from the Yakuza or the Devils.

Just four of us lowly humans.

"What are you doing?"

"Don't worry about it."

Useless bastards.



(Akiyama)

Watching the battle on screen was… well, eye-opening for one. He knew his niece wasn't exactly the kindest of individuals, but to see her so ready to senselessly slaughter her enemies was pretty horrifying. He didn't really know what to think.

On one hand, it was the logical decision. They weren't powerful or equipped enough to be able to afford to spare every single one of their enemies, clearly not with that Saio Triad officer somehow acquiring advanced anti-magic technology.

But to see her not show even the slightest of emotions as she shot the Fallen girl in the head, not even a flinch or wince as she gazed at her bleeding corpse was one hell of a scene he could never get out of his mind.

He could understand Mizuki's concerns, she's really showing the same exact behavior those people do. Nowhere near as severe - she never grinned or laughed maniacally as she slaughtered them, only smirking in arrogance at worst, but if this kept going, then it would be pretty bad.

Not to mention, she awakened her heritage in the battle. As soon as they ambushed them, Akane's mana sharpened suddenly, and her pupils changed color, turning icy blue. What caused this? Did the adrenaline force it out of its dormant state? Could it be shock, but Akane just knew how to hide it? So many things happened in that fight, like Ichiban's awakening of the Boosted Gear.

So he simply pushed it to the back of his head for now, focusing on the actual battle. Of course, she made too many mistakes - one example being that she was incredibly impatient and quick to irritate.

She's very reckless, too. Had she retreated to regroup then formulated a new plan, they might've defeated the Saio Triad officer with relative ease, but instead, she pulled that dangerous stunt that barely even damaged him.

Of course, unlike him, the Mad Dog absolutely loved it, laughing and cheering for Tatsu's daughter, praising her name to high heaven. Hell, he forced the entire family to sing her praises just for that stunt alone.

However, that joyous moment was cut short as the officer began choking his niece. Akiyama was ready to endure the worst from the Majima Family if it meant he could fly away and assist his niece. He was this close from decking the Mad Dog in the face.

But his rage and worry couldn't be compared to the one tied up behind them.

Half of the underground facility was frozen in ice, although fortunately no one was hurt from the burst of magic. Shun could see his own breath, so could everyone else inside. Every Majima Family Yakuza backed as far away from the enraged mother as they could.

Shun turned around, seeing Mizuki with her head lowered, half of her hair pure white as she stressed the seal over her power. She was doing her utmost best to calm herself down, eyes closed and breathing steady.

The once-powerful seal used to stop her core from generating magic was now all worn out, weakened enough that mere stress is enough to destroy it. Seeing the battle on the giant screen almost did break it, her magic leaking in the process and causing the damage over the facility, but the unexpected ending gave her a moment to calm down before it did.

It clearly left a mark, though. Her magic was slowly returning, and everyone in the room could sense it. Shun didn't know if this was part of the Mad Dog's plan, but this could've ended up with the entirety of Kuoh frozen solid the instant Akane suffered a terrible injury.

However, the chair she was tied on was completely untouched, as were the chains used to tie her up, likely some sort of magical repellent or absorber. To withstand this much magic was impressive, but they all knew that Mizuki could've easily destroyed it if she had broken her seal completely.

"See?" Majima started, pointing at the half-frozen screen. "I told ya she could handle it, and she did better than any of us coulda expected."

"This was not the way to do it, Majima-san," Shun responded with a shake of his head. "Not even an ounce of assistance? One Yakuza to at least lead them?"

"Nah, that ain't gonna work. The girl is a natural-born leader, and she's a prideful one to boot." The Mad Dog waved it off. "Sendin' one of my men to boss 'em around would've pissed them off instead. Havin' them work together like this is better. This is good experience for them, ya see."

"Majima." He dropped the honorifics as he frowned, feeling his blood boiling. "What good is experience if you send her on a suicide mission? What good is experience if Akane had died?"

"She wouldn't have," Majima said with confidence, grinning at the girl who had her middle finger extended. "Someone like her ain't never dyin' like this, no way."

"How can you be so unreasonably sure about this?" He questioned.

"I told ya before, Akiyama." He shrugged. "Those're the eyes of someone who will never allow themselves ta lose. If a gaze could kill, then hers would've frozen the planet ten times over."

Having had enough, Shun grabbed the Mad Dog by his jacket and slammed him against the wall, an uncharacteristic snarl on his face as he glared at the smirking Yakuza Patriarch. Shun's red suit jacket lit on fire as he felt his Sacred Gear stirring, power coursing through his vein when his eyes glowed a fiery orange.

"I don't know what gave you authority to do any of this- To keep a mother from protecting her own daughter," Shun growled, gritting his teeth as he referred to the silent Mizuki, ignoring how every single Yakuza pointed their guns at him. "Don't force your delusional way of thinking onto us. As a guardian, your only job is to cut this stupid bullshit and protect her like you're told to."

"And hinder her potential in the process?" Majima's grin dropped, as did his Kansai accent. "I told you before; shielding her from conflict will do nothing but stunt her growth."

"There won't be growth if she's dead." Shun reiterated. "Look, I understand where you're coming from, but risking her life over assumptions? Thinking this is the only way she could grow?"

"They're not assumptions, they're facts, and both of us know that," Majima responded calmly. "She's like her dad; she grows exponentially under pressure. If one of us was around her, Akane would feel safe, and that stagnates her growth."

"She's not her dad."

"I know." Majima gripped Shun's hand tightly and effortlessly moved him away. "She's better."

He pushed Shun away, quickly reverting back to his Mad Dog persona as he shrugged, addressing the mother of Akane.

"Ya know Akane more than any of us, so ya know what I'm sayin' is true," Majima said. "Ain't that right, Mizuki-chan?"

Mizuki, who was silent the whole time, didn't give him an instant, heated reply like Shun expected her to do. She simply lifted her head up, hair back to what it used to be, and simply responded with the blankest voice he's ever heard her speak in.

"Can I see my daughter now?"

Majima blinked, and Shun didn't quite expect this. Not long ago, she was almost frothing at the mouth, cursing and promising torment. This was the complete opposite. However, Shun could detect the overwhelming rage she's currently feeling.

"Uh, yeah sure." Majima shrugged, waving to one of his men. "Get those chains off her."

"Yes, sir."

The subordinate quickly went behind Mizuki and began 'untying' the chains, using some sort of a strange wrench obviously magical in nature. Majima stepped towards her, seemingly unaware of her current desire to rip him apart, or simply not caring enough. Knowing him, it was the latter.

Majima wasn't even able to get a word in, because as soon as the chains dropped, Mizuki closed the distance in an instant and delivered a blow to his stomach, knocking the wind out of him and sending him smashing into the giant screen.

Mizuki simply blankly stared at him for a few seconds, not caring as guns were aimed at her, but all lowered their weapons when Majima raised his hand, a mixture of chuckling and coughing echoing in the facility.

She then just turned around and walked out of the door, but not before giving a warning that sent a chill down the spine of everyone in the room, even Shun, who's not involved in this at all.

"Majima."

They all froze and stared at her, her voice quiet and even, betraying the sheer overwhelming rage she's feeling.

"If you ever do something like that again."

Mizuki turned her head ever so slightly, eyes glowing blue as the ground under her feet began to freeze.

"I will bury the Tojo Clan."

And then she just left. Her steps could be heard as the entire place was dead silent until it was broken by Majima's sudden laughter.

"What a dangerous combination!" He giggled, wincing as he held his stomach in pain. "Tatsu-chan's tenacity and Mizuki-chan's viciousness. I wonder what Akane-chan will end up like?"

Shun sighed and left, going after Akane's mother. He knows the man means well in his own twisted way, but from the looks of it, they'll never agree on what method to go by.

He just hopes the Mad Dog doesn't take it too far again.

Now that the battle is over, Ichi and I took the fat bastard with us to meet up with Asia and a now-healed Issei before heading to the warehouse where Freed and Raynare are. Those two are still out cold from the looks of it, chained and bound together. Could they break the chains? Maybe, but by the time they wake up, they'd be too weak to do anything.

And unlike me, simply sitting on their asses won't heal their wounds. They need medical attention if they want to make a recovery. They won't be going anywhere, especially not with the four of us back. They're stuck there until one of the Yakuza bastards takes them.

I'd kill them, (for that sweet sweet EXP), but if I do that now, I'd have no excuse. More eyes would be kept on me, more attention that I don't want right now. If this evil nature of my weird assassin bloodline was a known thing in the Yakuza, then showing signs is gonna make them concerned.

It's already a pain in the ass with this new trait I've gotten.

[Sadistic] - Trait

The pain and suffering of others please you. Seeing someone groveling and begging for mercy will always put a smile on your face. Humiliating and hurting your opponents in every way will become a high priority, forcing you to prolong their suffering far more than necessary.

This trait is hard to overcome

It's gonna be a lot harder to keep myself under control with this. I've admittedly had some sadistic tendencies in the past, but I don't think they were worthy of being a trait on their own. This probably means that these tendencies are gonna be a lot, lot worse. I'm already having trouble keeping my anger in check, and this isn't helping.

I wonder, though. What triggered this? My sense of gratification when we crushed those Stray Exorcists? Or was it tied to this new bloodline power I got? I am related to this family of evil assassins after all, and according to my mother, sadism is part of who they are.

Weird. This bloodline power isn't related to them at all. It's my Yokai blood finally awakening. This brings me to this new perk, a very powerful one that'll help me catch up to the real monsters of DxD.

[Bloodline: Yuki No Onna] - Perk

You share the blood of the ambivalent Yuki No Onna, a very powerful and rare Yokai that is hidden from the world. While not pure, her blood runs strong within you, giving you abilities not seen in centuries. Use your powers wisely.

75% of any Ice Damage dealt to you will be converted to MP

Ice Magic Control's requirements for ranking up are cut by 50%

Refining and evolving spells are twice as easy, and you may learn one spell that is one rank above your current level

Ice Magic's effectiveness is increased by 50% and will ignore all resistances and immunities

You are more powerful in colder environments

You can absorb nearby natural snow or ice to increase your stats

This perk is incredible. The defensive and offensive capabilities of this perk, while specific, are amazing. I don't even need to match someone like Serafall in strength to defeat her with this. What's the point if she can barely do any damage to me anyway?

And the sheer increase in potential is insane. A cut by 50% for the requirements on top of that 25% for my Rising Star perk? I'll be able to rank up my Ice Magic Mastery like it's nothing. A single month focused solely on training is probably enough to reach the highest rank.

I also got another related perk that isn't as powerful as this one, but still very good.

[Shin Youjutsu] - Perk

Due to your powerful expression of the blood of a rare Yokai breed, you can inherently use the true form of Youjutsu, a far more powerful version than the false and weak imitation used by the current generation of Yokai.

MP cost of all spells is decreased by 15%

All Pure Magic spells' effectiveness are increased by 25%

Ki or Chi effectiveness is increased by 20%

Your emotions can influence the power of your magic

Certain Masteries will gain a bonus with this perk

This reminded me of the Ancient Youjutsu my mother talked about once, but it's named differently. Is it the same thing or is it something else entirely? She did say that emotions are the main power influence of it, but she never mentioned anything about Ki. Perhaps this is an even stronger variant?

I should ask her when I get the chance and get more info about Ki too. It's wise to have a backup source of power, seeing how some people have anti-magic tech. I knew going for a balanced build was a good idea. Eliminating all weaknesses is what anyone should do before they try to acquire more power. If I'd gone full mage, even if I've gotten a lot more powerful, it wouldn't matter much once I get hit by something like that magic disrupting smoke bomb.

Of course, that's not all the stuff I got. Two more stat milestone perks, a Cryomancy Spellbook, and a Rare Gacha Token. This beginning arc of DxD did more for me in a day than I got from training in safety for a week. I knew that sticking around Kuoh was only gonna accelerate my growth. The more danger I'm in, and the stronger the enemy, the more the levels and quests I'll get.

[Child of Magic] - Perk - 1000 WIS

Strange. Magic seems to look fondly upon your existence and lends its hand when needed, and you in turn enjoy its presence whenever it's around. You've somehow gained the favor of magic itself.

When your MP reaches 0, you will immediately absorb all ambient magic nearby to refill your reserves. Any given area has a finite amount of magic to draw on in this way.

[Intrinsic Knowledge] - Perk - 1000 INT

You know this isn't enough. You recognize that there's something waiting beyond these limiting walls of refinement. Your spells can be stronger, faster, and tougher than before. True temperament awaits.

All spells have their maximum refinement level increased by 5

I really do love the Gamer power. Just that instance of actual battle made me almost twice as strong as I was a day ago. As soon as I go back home, I don't think I'll be sleeping. I'll be in the dungeon all night testing my powers and ranking up my Ice Magic Control. With so many of the requirements being cut, I should rank up in a single night.

Then I can read the spellbooks and practice these new spells. Frost Cloak, Frozen Soldier, and the book I got from the quest, Cold Mist. There's also the Gacha Token I haven't used yet, but I'll do it when I'm training in the dungeon alone.

Honestly, at this point, I'm looking forward to Kokabiel showing himself. If weaklings like those Fallen and their squads of pathetic Stray Exorcists gave me so much, I wonder what a Cadre would do to my growth.

Of course, I'm not the only one who grew stronger. Like I predicted before, awakening a Sacred Gear does in fact increase one's natural power. Ichi went from 300-500 in his physicals to 500-700, least being DEX and most being STR.

It's good to have my close allies become powerful, but it's also a little threatening. Two boosts is enough for him to kill me before I realize what's happening. I know Ichiban would never do anything like that, but I still don't like it.

Perhaps it's just me being prideful, wanting to become the most powerful in our group or 'party' as Ichi likes to call it, or maybe I feel threatened. I honestly don't know. It's a weird, unpleasant feeling. I hate it.

I'll have to fix that. The problem with the Boosted Gear is that without it, the user is not powerful enough to handle actual threats. It makes you reliant on it, likely complacent too, as you only need to work on your stamina to use it to its full potential. Same with Divine Dividing, though that one is trickier to deal with.

If a Boosted Gear user focused on refining their 'base' form, then they could've conquered this world ages ago. Imagine someone like Sirzechs with it? How strong could a monster like him become after five or four boosts?

I glance at Ichiban, who has a satisfied smile on his face as he pats Issei on the back, saying how good of a job we did against the Fallen as they all sit on the ground in a circle, a couple of empty pizza boxes stacked on top of each other in the middle. Issei looks a little shaken up, likely from almost losing his life, but he's relieved. Even though she doesn't understand a lot, Asia looks a little happy too.

What I'm saying is simple. The best way to deal with a Boosted Gear user is to kill them before they get any chance to boost or unleash their Balance Breaker and to do that, I need more physical power. Dodging once is all they need to turn the tides against me, so I mustn't give them any window to do that.

Hell, growing physically is a must. Every 'mage' in DxD is fast enough to outpace regular bullets, and I'm pretty sure Sirzechs and the other Satans are way, way above that. They're the kind of people who'd think said bullets are frozen in time from how slow they are. A slap from them would be enough to turn me into a pile of gore.

I can't do much against that. I can't hit someone that I can't keep up with at all, so I must become as fast and as strong as they are to be able to match them. I have to eradicate every weakness I have so I can live in this world without fear.

I turn my head to the other side, looking at our prisoners. All of them are out cold, so I have no worries about them waking up and trying to escape. Even if they try to, Ichiban and I are more than powerful enough to knock them back on their asses without much effort. And if they're smart enough, they'll know that trying to run is futile. I won't hesitate to slaughter them if they do, because then I'd have an excuse to kill.

"Don't worry, I'll handle it if that's the case." I say.

"By the way, there's something I wanted to talk about." Ichiban crosses his legs, looking at me quizzically. "What was that weird power before? You pulled some weird sword out of thin air. How did you do that?"

I still for a few moments, internally debating whether I should lie or tell the truth. I can probably come up with a lie pretty easily, but this wouldn't help at all. He's talking about the inventory, and the inventory isn't exclusive to ice-based weaponry. So saying it's part of my ice magic isn't a wise idea. I'm gonna have to pull more bullshit out of there whenever I'm in a fight at some point.

Telling the truth will save me from explaining later, but I think the Yakuza are listening in on us here. That'll reveal the inventory not just to this group, but the entire Tojo Clan, or at least the higher-ranked members of it.

…Though, what about twisting the truth a little bit?

"It's some weird power I discovered around the same time I was able to use magic," I answer, prompting them to lean in to listen closely. "I can put stuff in it and pull it out whenever I want."

"Woah…" Issei's eyes widen. "That's so useful. What kind of stuff can you put in it?"

"Small things, usually crap that doesn't weigh over 25 Kilograms." I lie. "And I can't put more than three things at a time."

If I can't lie or tell the truth, then half of each should do the trick. The 'appear weak when you are strong' part of that Sun Tzu quote likely extends to certain powers as well. Downplay your strength so people gloss over you and don't give you as much attention as they should.

"Damn, that's a pretty great power to have." Ichi grins. "It's like your very own inventory space!"

I flinch slightly, quickly calming myself down and reminding myself that this moron is a video game addict, it's normal for him to think that way. For a second there I thought he figured out what it was, and that scared the hell out of me.

"Y-yeah. I guess that's true." I clear my throat and try to change the subject. "Anyway, you two can go home. I'll stay here and keep watch."

40 Reputation with Issei Hyoudou [90/100]

(Shun Akiyama)

He stood atop a pile of rubble, staring at the destroyed church, a cloud of smoke leaving his mouth as he exhaled. He took the lit cigarette and flicked it away as he looked around a little more. He arrived here before the Yakuza to see if there were any survivors, anyone he can at least save.

For questioning of course. While Shun does hate bloodshed, he's not naive and nice enough to save people who tried to kill his niece out of the goodness of his heart. He needs to know what the hell is going on with the Grigori and what could've pushed them to do something so drastic.

Using Suzaku's powers, Shun enhanced his senses to the max, eyes turning into a bright, fiery color. He scanned the empty battlefield, sensing two life forces in the distance, one very weak, and the other extremely powerful.

And far more malicious.

Shun rushed forward, fire exploding from his calves to propel himself. He almost recognized the evil presence, It was so familiar, it's at the tip of his tongue, and yet, it eludes him. What is that? What kind of supernatural creature is it? No, it can't be anything other than a human. It didn't feel like an Angel or a Devil, or anything of that sort. Not one bit.

He arrived almost instantaneously but spotted nobody. This evil and familiar presence had simply vanished as soon as he arrived. What the hell was that? He did sense someone here, but now they're gone. How did they escape so quickly?

Shun looked around and recognized the body of that blue-haired Fallen Angel. Blood poured from her forehead, a look of pure horror etched on her face. She was dead, but it wasn't the church collapsing that killed her.

Shun approached the corpse, crouching beside it to inspect it, grimacing at the bullet-shaped hole in her forehead. Was she what he just sensed? She'd been murdered by someone, that much is clear, likely by the same malicious presence who was just here before he arrived.

Who could it be? A Tojo Clan Yakuza? No, they wouldn't simply leave the corpse like this. They'd take it for examination before sending it back to the Grigori. What would they gain from this? Who could be powerful enough to do all of this without anybody noticing?

This isn't something the Majima Family can handle comfortably on their own. Something of this scale must be reported back to Daigo directly.

Whatever it was, Shun had a horrible feeling about it.

And for once in his life, he hoped he was wrong.

The battle gave me more exp than I expected. As soon as I chose the Swordmaster class, I jumped ten levels in an instant from all the accumulated level-ups. Yes, a sword class is pretty basic, but seeing how many magical swords are in this universe, it seems like a safe bet that it will pay off eventually.

Realistically, a spear class is probably much better as it gives you a reach advantage, but when people can shoot fire or ice out of their hands, reach doesn't really matter all that much.

Other than that, while I can probably get one easily, I don't have a spear in my inventory, but I do have a fire sword and an ice sword. One thing I noticed is that the Mastery Skill doesn't specify what kind of sword. A zweihander can't be used as a cutlass, for example, they require different skills, but for this? It means 'sword' in a general sense. So if I train exclusively using a katana and reach Master level in the Mastery Skill, I'll also be able to use a shortsword just as well. The wording of the skill is pretty literal in this case.

[Sword Proficiency: Adept] – Mastery Skill

Swords have been the common choice for a weapon in many different worlds. Hundreds of arts and variations were created for this weapon, making it one of the most versatile and flexible ever conceived.

You've become fairly proficient, nothing to write home about, but all around decent

Deal 75,000 Damage with Swords and create 3 Sword Skills to reach the next Rank. Progress to Journeyman Rank [24,052/75,000] [3/3]

If quality is off the table, then quantity is the way to go.
