"Then let's move," I say. "We don't have much time before we have to meet with Magnus."

With that, we split up in pairs, all of us going in different directions. Am I confident that one of us will find something that could tell us more about what's happening? Not really. It's likely that we won't find anything useful, not when my Spyders found nothing besides the Barracuda base. But as I told Issei, it's better that we try than twiddle our thumbs and do nothing.

Who knows? Maybe we will find something that my tech couldn't.

I'll try to keep my expectations low, but it doesn't hurt to hope.





– Kiba –

This was not quite the direction he'd expected this vacation to take, but admittedly, he didn't entirely dislike it. It felt a little exciting. Yuuto was intrigued. An adventure away from home? Some kind of conspiracy in Hawaii? Wasn't that fascinating?

Not to say what he'd been experiencing beforehand was boring or anything. He was loving his time in Hawaii. It was probably the most fun he'd had in years. During his time in the underworld and even in Kuoh, there had never been a lot of opportunities to let loose like this.

Most of his time was usually spent studying at school, training with the rest of the peerage, or general work as Rias' servant. However, Rias wasn't strict when it came to work and focused more on having fun with them than actually working. Even though Yuuto somewhat appreciated it— this normalcy he had never experienced, some days could get unbearably boring.

He never got to enjoy vacations because Rias never went on any. He had nothing against his King, but the magic of living in Japan had disappeared very quickly when doing schoolwork was expected of them.

Of course, he wasn't counting the conflicts they'd had since Akane had come to Kuoh. That girl was definitely a magnet for trouble, from the low-ranked fallen angels to Kokabiel to an entire invasion from the Old Satans. All of them in quick succession, too. Prior to that, they'd barely gotten in any trouble.

But he digressed. A vacation like this was something he most definitely needed. No responsibilities to concern himself with. Just him, his friends, and a good time. For a whole month in one of the nicest places on the planet.

It would've been even better had Rias and Akeno come with them, but his King seemed certain that whatever happened to Gasper wasn't the Dhampir's fault. That someone had somehow gotten involved.

He kept it to himself, not wanting to outwardly doubt Rias, but Yuuto didn't really think so. Even though Koneko and Akeno believed her, it just never really made sense to him. How and why would that happen? Who would have a grudge against Gasper of all people?

Even if he had enemies Yuuto didn't know about, how were they able to come to Kuoh undetected and get him to attack Akane and then disappear off the face of the earth? Hell, it happened after the Kokabiel incident, the only person who'd tried to cause a war between the devils and the yakuza.

Again, he never said anything out loud, as he didn't want to hurt his friends' feelings. And would it really hurt if Rias investigated? She'd be disappointed if she didn't find anything, but that'd be about it, right? He recalled her saying something about catching up to them once she was done, and thirty days was a lot of time. She was likely to finish before they left Hawaii.

Unless the CIA decided to kick them out, anyhow, and that seemed to be unlikely at the rate things are going. With Magnus Rose accepting their offer of assistance and all.

"Aw, man. This is the best." Issei said, ogling dozens of women in colorful swimsuits. "The women here are huge~!"

"Did you already forget why we're here?" Yuuto sighed. "Please focus, Issei-san."

"How can I? Are you even seeing what I'm seeing?" He replied. "This is heaven, man. We're in heaven."

He probably wouldn't agree, but Yuuto was starting to think that the placement for each pair was a little off.

"Issei-san, we're here for an important job." He reminded the human. "Pleasure can wait until later. You wouldn't want to disappoint Akane-san, right?"

Mentioning her name seemed to do the trick as Issei visibly hesitated, remembering who he was trying to impress. Probably. It didn't take a genius to realize he had the biggest crush on her. Yuuto found it a little pitiful seeing how she usually treated him. While she was never outright abusive to him, Akane liked using him as the butt of her jokes a lot of the time.

Besides, he'd never had a chance with her. Almost everyone but Issei had already noticed that Akane and Ichiban had gotten together, while Issei thought they were still love rivals. Nobody had the heart to tell him. Not even Koneko, who usually wouldn't waste a chance to tear into him.

But doing so would sting her as well, so that's probably why she held off on that. The poor thing.

"Ugh, you're right." He grunted, closing his eyes. "Innocent lives are at stake. I can't let myself be distracted."

"Good." Yuuto nodded. Then, he hummed in thought. "Though honestly, I'm not sure what we should be looking for exactly…"

Telling them to look for 'supernatural activity' was incredibly vague. Yuuto couldn't sense anything for miles; anything supernatural usually stayed away from populated areas like this. From Stray Devils to anything more significant. Then again, Koneko had told him that she and Akane had stumbled onto one of the Fallen Angels who had attacked Kuoh.

Raynare, if he recalled correctly. And according to them, she wasn't here to cause any trouble, seemingly enjoying a vacation herself. A strange coincidence for sure, but she wasn't really a threat now that Kokabiel was dead. If she were reporting to anyone, it'd be to Azazel, who was more or less an ally.

As for the Barracuda? Well, they'd found none, as if they'd disappeared entirely, which was surprising, to say the least. Yuuto was almost sure the gang would start patrolling the city looking for them, but they did not. Perhaps they were scared? That was the only logical explanation. Akane and Ichiban were very powerful— very few in the world could actually match them in strength, and the former's aura and killing intent were nothing short of terrifying.

Her power could still be felt even while in an idle or resting state. It reminded Yuuto that underneath all that haughty attitude and ego, Akane was a monster that could easily back up most of her arrogant claims, which was a rarity in this day and age.

"Hmm…" Yuuto scanned the beach again. "What do you think, Issei-san? Any ideas?"

"Holy shit, that one has to have the biggest rack I've ever seen." He whispered, staring at a woman sunbathing.

Yuuto facepalmed and sighed in exasperation.

"Issei-san."

"Uh, yeah. Yeah. Sorry." He cleared his throat. "We don't really have anything to start with, so how about the resort over there?"

He pointed at the luxury resort at the far right edge of the beach— Crystal Aloha Resort. A five-star resort with an outside bar, a huge pool, and several private booths.

"You think we'd find something there?"

"Well, no. Not really. But well…" Issei paused for a moment, coming up with a way to articulate his thoughts properly. "Okay, so I was thinking like this. We know how gangs and stuff typically have a leader, right?"

"Usually, yes." Yuuto nodded.

"And with the Barracuda being powerful enough to go on parades and bribe cops, then they gotta be well-off, right?" He rationalized, making Yuuto nod again. "Right. In that case, maybe their leader would want to use some of the money for personal pleasure and stay in the nicest place in Honolulu."

"I see." Yuuto hummed. "But we are talking about the leader of a supernatural faction. Usually, they'd try to be a lot more cautious than that."

"Yeah, that's why I'm not confident." Issei chuckled sheepishly. "It's worth a try, though. From what we saw, if the faction is mostly low-class humans, then maybe their leader is a human, too."

"And humans blend in with other humans effortlessly." Rias' Knight agreed, then smiled. "Your logic is very sound, Issei-san."

"You think so?" Issei rubbed his neck bashfully. "I just thought it kinda makes sense, y'know?"

"It does," Yuuto said, walking to the resort. "Let's go."

"But how are we gonna look for them?" His partner asked. "I don't think it'd make sense to check out every room there, right? It would take us ages."

"For sure." He nodded. "But we should try to stake out the building at least. Perhaps we could find a lead."

Assuming Issei was correct, then their leader should be in one of the suites, and only the highest three floors of the building had those. It still didn't help them all that much, but this was in case they needed someone to infiltrate.

Once the two made it to the resort's grounds, they stopped in their place as a pair of familiar faces walked out of the building, making Yuuto clench his fists and narrow his eyes. The two exorcists immediately noticed them, the blue-haired one glaring back at Rias' Knight in suspicion.

Those two again, huh? He'd heard from Akane and Issei that they'd met them at the waterpark, but what are the odds of meeting them again? The news of these Excalibur wielders being anywhere in Honolulu was annoying enough. Having to interact with them in any way? What a pain.

Xenovia seemed equally as irritated as he, being a 'filthy devil' and whatnot, but Yuuto didn't care what she thought about him. Not when she held that disgusting artifact everywhere she went.

Issei and Irina, however, didn't look like they shared those thoughts as their faces broke into big smiles upon seeing each other.

"Oh, Issei!" Irina waved, rushing toward them, with Xenovia following closely behind. "What a surprise! How'd you find us? I don't think I ever told you where we stayed."

"'Where you stayed'? Wait, you're staying at the resort?!" His eyes widened. "That's so cool!"

"Right? The church's paying for our expenses." Irina giggled. "But what are you doing here if you're not here to visit?"

"Oh, uh…" He glanced at Yuuto for help. "Well, it's kinda complicated."

Yuuto was trying his hardest not to challenge those two to a duel for their Excaliburs. To finally get a chance to destroy those vile artifacts once and for all. Disgusting blades used to ruin the lives of countless children.

Did these two not know the bloody history of what they carried on their backs? What sort of despicable acts have they been used in? And for them to call themselves servants of God. What a tasteless joke. The friends he had lost in that awful experiment…

Xenovia noticed his glare growing sharper, prompting her to scoff.

"Again, what are you staring at, Devil?" She said. "You've been doing this every chance you get. What do you want?"

To eliminate the relic that inflicted pain and suffering throughout his entire childhood. That claimed the lives of his friends. This was his greatest desire. However, as with every opportunity he had to voice his challenge, the moment was neither suitable nor appropriate.

So he held himself back—this time.

"It's nothing." He replied curtly. "Regardless, we were just about to leave. Let's go, Issei."

"Huh?" His partner blinked. "But we haven't really done anything yet."

Yuuto, who was about to insist as he didn't want to spend another minute around them, paused as Irina grabbed Issei by the hand.

"Aw, come on!" She said, pulling Issei closer to her. "Let's hang out a bit, at least!"

"Er, well…" Issei hesitated. "We were kinda in the middle of something important…"

"It can wait, can't it?" She persisted, wrapping her arms around his. "We're all on vacation. Let's enjoy ourselves and worry about other things later."

She was very persistent, Yuuto noticed. And Issei was rapidly folding to her demands, unfortunately, as he looked at Rias' Knight apologetically and pleadingly. Begging to be let go just this once.

…Well, someone had to distract them.

"Well, alright." Yuuto sighed. "I'll do it by myself."

Not like Issei was going to focus very well with someone like Irina attached to him like that anyway.

"Aw man, thank you so much!" Issei grinned. "Please don't tell Akane-san, alright?"

"I won't," Yuuto said. "I'll tell her you did your part very well."

"Thanks!"

"Eh?" Irina blinked. "What's this about Akane?"

"Where is she?" Xenovia asked expectantly.

"I don't know." Issei shrugged.

"Liar." She accused, pointing at him with her glare sharpening. "You have her number, don't you? Call and ask where she is."

"I am NOT going to do that." He refused. "She'd know I sent you, and I value my life. Thank you very much."

"Eeeeh? You have her number?" Irina pouted. "But you don't even have mine! That's so not fair."

"Er, well—"

Yuuto slowly walked away from them, thankfully slipping away before Xenovia noticed. He didn't think he'd be able to contain his temper if that one in particular were to bother him. She knew how to get on his nerves.

He'd get his chance eventually. And when he did, he'd break that sword right in front of her.





– Koneko –

"Found anything yet?" Ichi asked her as they strolled through the relatively empty streets of Little Tokyo.

For a packed city like Honolulu, they had thankfully been given the least crowded area to investigate. At least during this time of the day. The sun was just about to set, and most people were either having dinner or going to bars and clubs, most of which were on the western side.

Not that this side of the city was ever as crowded as anything else. There weren't many stores or places good for sightseeing besides maybe the shrine, which nobody cared about because of the creepy mascot loitering near it, and the park that wasn't even built yet.

So, for sightseeing, the northeast of Honolulu was a terrible place to be, comparatively speaking. But for a nice, quiet walk? It was the best. It didn't hurt that they were around the bar where they were supposed to meet the CIA agent.

Overall, a nice place. Koneko liked it a lot. If only this entire damned city didn't make her sweat like a pig, that was.

"Nope." She shook her head, trying her best to hide her discomfort.

It wasn't like her to care what others thought about her. If this were Rias she was walking around with, she'd be constantly bothering the redhead to stop dragging her everywhere and find a place to cool off. But she didn't want to sound whiny to Ichiban. Koneko was better than that.

As someone who had never had a chance to hang out alone with Ichi, Koneko was thrilled to finally have the opportunity to do so, even if they were on an important job. She wanted this moment to last as long as possible. Complaining might cut their time together short.

Most of the time, they'd interact with each other in school, and sometimes during training if their schedules aligned. And even then, Ichiban was in an entirely different league. Even without activating his Sacred Gear, he was already surpassing her in strength and speed.

Which she would barely make up with her superior skill and experience, but he was starting to catch up in those, too. So most of the time, he'd be training with Rias, Sona, and most commonly, Akane and the Tiger yakuza.

Koneko had noticed that they'd been interacting less and less ever since the tournament, and it made her feel terrible. Not to say she was entirely innocent. After all, she liked him. As in liked liked him. More than friends.

So seeing Akane kiss him and make a claim before she could during the finals hurt a lot. It admittedly made her avoid Ichi for a little while. But she knew it wasn't his fault. He wasn't aware of her feelings. And why should he be? It wasn't like she'd given him any hints.

She honestly didn't know when it had happened. Just that one day, she'd found him exceptionally cooler and more handsome than the day before. Was it her instincts as a Nekomata that made her attracted to his strength? Their shared interests? His kindness? All of that? She had no idea.

"For real? Hah…" Ichi groaned, not satisfied with her answer. "How long have we been walking around? The heat's killing me."

Koneko said nothing, but found some comfort in not being the only one affected by the weather.

"I really wasn't thinking it through when I agreed with Akane, huh?" He said, rubbing his neck. "I mean, what the hell are we even looking for, anyway?"

"Barracuda," Koneko responded.

"And where have they gone off to?" He questioned, glancing at her. "You'd think after we kicked their asses, they'd start looking for us for revenge."

"Ice Queen killed two of them." She answered. "She scared them off."

"Probably what happened, yeah." He sighed. "It's not like she made it pretty either. Beheading isn't usually what I would go for if I had to kill someone."

A violent method for sure. Personally speaking, Koneko would've maybe snapped their necks or stopped their hearts with a strong attack if she was forced to kill. Taking their heads was messy and way over the top.

But that's how things were with Ice Queen. Truthfully, despite how Koneko acted with Akane, she was a little scared of her. Being a Nekomata, she was extra sensitive to the presence of those around her, and Akane almost felt like she was always planning to kill someone.

It was bizarre and a bit worrying. Yes, someone that powerful in comparison would feel suffocating for someone like Koneko, but this wasn't just power. There was almost this weird anger that radiated off her, but it wasn't anger. Or at least, not hers. It was very odd.

It became hers whenever Koneko was around Ichiban, which was the biggest reason why she'd never tried to approach Ichi in a romantic or sexual way. Perhaps Akane herself didn't notice, but Koneko could feel her subtle glares drilling into the back of her skull.

Of course, that was just a part of it. There was also the insecurity that she couldn't possibly measure up to someone like Ice Queen when it came to looks. Really, who would take a small-looking girl like her over someone as beautiful and curvy as Akane? She was on par with Rias in terms of her body. Fit, voluptuous, and sexy.

Even if Ichi found Koneko attractive for some reason, the fear of rejection was still present. Generally, as a yokai and a devil, she didn't particularly care about sharing a man all that much. It was a common practice in both cultures, but the same couldn't be said for them. They were humans, and humans were primarily monogamous.

Assuming Ichi was an outlier and wanted a harem or something, Akane clearly wasn't. Not with how she'd glare daggers at Koneko each time she even glanced at Ichiban. Honestly, it was getting a little exhausting.

That wasn't to say Koneko hated Ice Queen. She quite liked her, if anything. She was fun to be around. Her antics and exaggerated sense of superiority were funny. Plus, they shared a dislike of Issei—that perverted little dick.

Besides, without Akane, Rias would've been married off, Kokabiel would've probably killed all of them, and the Old Satans might've just wiped out everyone. Arrogant Princess act aside, she was pretty much a hero to them.

At least it looked like the feeling was mutual whenever Ichi was out of the picture. She'd hate to be disliked by Akane, admittedly.

"Violent Ice Queen is violent," Koneko responded tonelessly. "Shocker."

Ichiban snorted.

"Yeah, fair." He said before pausing. "…To be honest, I'm not a fan of how casual she is about killing."

Koneko blinked.

"I mean, I get it. As much as I want to avoid it, sometimes, it needs to be done." He added. "But whenever she does it, she just feels…"

She waited for him to phrase his sentence. Ichi struggled for a few moments before he spoke.

"Disconnected, I guess?" He tried to soften the word he wanted to say. "Almost like she doesn't understand or care about the weight of her actions."

"You mean she's remorseless?" Koneko guessed his meaning, making him grimace in discomfort.

"Yeah…" He sighed. "I didn't wanna use that word, but yeah. Pretty much what it is."

Koneko took a moment to think about it. She understood where he was coming from— Ichi was very empathetic, even for a human. He never let it get in the way, but to show this level of compassion even to enemies was a beautiful quality. Not a lot of people could say the same.

Especially considering his upbringing. She didn't know a lot about his past, but she knew he was a person abandoned by his parents in a brothel of all places. Being this humane and caring despite everything that had happened to him showed a strength of character.

"What do you think?" He asked for her opinion. "Am I maybe overthinking it? I know the kind of person Akane is, but it's still jarring seeing her like that, y'know?"

After a couple of seconds, Koneko replied.

"I don't know." She shrugged. "Ice Queen's not the type to wear her emotions on her sleeves."

"Huh?" Ichiban blinked at her.

"Maybe it bothers her. Maybe it doesn't." She added. "But she's never gonna tell anyone regardless."

"Why do you think that?"

"I can tell Akane doesn't like to show vulnerability. I think that includes emotionally." Koneko clarified. "Maybe she doesn't want to worry anyone."

"That does sound like her…" Ichi agreed before shaking his head. "Yeah, you're probably right. Sorry for springing that on you out of nowhere, Koneko. Not like myself to start rambling about serious shit like this."

"Mhm, I don't mind." She responded with a small smile. "You're my friend."

"Heh. Yeah. Thanks." He smiled back at her brightly. "I guess you're just pretty easy to talk to."

Her heart fluttered at the genuine compliment, her face glowing a little. Ichiban noticed as he tilted his head at her, blinking in confusion.

"You alright? You look a little red."

"I'm okay." She said blankly. "It's just hot…"

"Right?" He agreed. "Let's stop for a little break. I'm sure the gang wouldn't mind if we stopped for some ice cream or something. If anything, they're probably doing the same."

Koneko nodded and followed along. As he took her to a nearby ice cream parlor, Koneko turned around as he picked and chose the flavors he wanted. Come to think of it, they hadn't run into anyone for a bit. The streets weren't crowded, but they hadn't exactly been this empty…

"What about you, Koneko?" Ichi asked, getting her attention. "Choose anything you'd like. It's my treat."

As she was about to respond, her eyes narrowed as she felt the intent to harm rapidly approaching them. The moment she heard the faint noise of something penetrating the air near them, Koneko moved, getting in front of Ichiban, and grabbed the end of a cane before it hit her partner.

Ichiban didn't waste a second, immediately realizing that they were under attack and striking the assailant in the chest, making them take a few steps back. These few brief seconds were more than enough to get a good look at him— it was an older man in a suit with slicked back dark brown hair and brown eyes.

From the pin he had on the right side of his suit, she could immediately tell he was a yakuza, but what did a yakuza want from them? Why had he attacked them? They were on the same side. Was he not from the Tojo clan?

Her questions were partially answered as Ichiban quickly recognized this individual.

"S-Sawashiro-san?!" He exclaimed.

Arakawa's captain? Koneko blinked.

"Sloppy, Ichi." He criticized, fixing his suit and tapping the cane on the ground. "If not for the girl, I would've splattered your brain across the pavement."

Ichiban clenched his jaw, quickly getting over his surprise.

"Yes, sir…" He nodded. "Sorry, sir."

Realizing this was some kind of a test, Koneko slowly relaxed her stance, but she still kept her glare, not appreciating his attitude or interruption one bit. The now-named Sawashiro noticed her glare and explained himself.

"Don't give me that look." He said coldly before staring back at Ichiban. "Someone has to keep this idiot on his toes. Just because you have the Boosted Gear doesn't mean you get to slack off."

"I wasn't," Ichiban replied. "I just… didn't think anyone would attack us in broad daylight like this, alright?"

"You think your enemies would care about time and place?" Arakawa's second in command scoffed. "You're either arrogant or the biggest dumbass in the world."

Ichi looked like he wanted to argue, but he kept his mouth shut and lowered his head, apologizing.

"Sorry."

"You're part of the family now." He added, tapping his cane on the ground. "Don't make mistakes like this again."

Koneko clicked her tongue, her fists clenching in annoyance at how rude this person was being to Ichi. Captain, patriarch, chairman— she didn't care who he was. He shouldn't talk to her friend like that.

But before she could tell him off, another, unfamiliar voice interjected.

"Enough, Sawashiro." He said. "You said you wanted to test him, not scold him."

The stranger approached them from behind Sawashiro. It was a boy their age with black hair and brown eyes, wearing a more colorful navy blue suit and matching navy blue pants. It wasn't dissimilar to a private school uniform rather than anything 'yakuza'. He also wore a pair of glasses.

Koneko could immediately tell that he was a rich kid of some kind. But instead of adding salt to the wound and insulting Ichiban, he smiled as one would when meeting a friend.

"It's been a while, Ichi." The strange boy said.

"Haha…" Ichiban chuckled in disbelief. "I almost couldn't recognize you, young master. Holy crap, what are the odds?"

Young master? Koneko blinked.

"You tell me. Never thought I'd meet you here, of all places," He replied before his eyes flickered to Koneko. "So are you going to introduce me to your friend?"

"Ah, right. This here is Koneko Toujou. She's a devil. One of Rias Gremory's peerage." Ichi said, prompting her to do a polite bow. "Koneko, this is Masato Arakawa. He's Masumi Arakawa's son."

"Don't introduce me like that. People are going to mistake me for a yakuza." He sighed in exasperation. "But a devil, huh? Interesting. It's a pleasure to meet you, Toujou-san."

This guy is a lot nicer than this Sawashiro jackass. Koneko thought, responding to him with a hum of acknowledgement.

"But what are you doing here?" Ichi asked. "I thought you were still studying in California."

"Still am. On a school trip right now." He explained. "Honestly, I could ask the same about you. What's your dumbass doing in Honolulu?"

"Dumbass? Heh. I'll have you know, I ranked eighth in Kuoh Academy." Ichi boasted, shocking him and the jackass captain as their eyes widened. "That's right! The age of idiot Ichiban has long passed. I'm now in my genius era."

Koneko snorted.

"Nothing funny about what I said." He told her.

"That so? What a surprise. That's great. Congrats, Ichi." Masato replied. "You must've worked hard."

"Well, I had help, to be honest." Ichi quickly admitted. "Say, young master, are you free right now? Whaddya say we catch up? It's been almost a whole year since we've seen each other, and I wanna introduce you to my girlfriend."

Hearing that stung her a bit.

"You have a girlfriend? Is the world about to end?" He teased before chuckling. "I'd love to, but I'm a little busy right now."

"Aw…"

"I'll give you a call later, though. When I have time." Masato added before waving. "See you soon."

"See you!"

With that, Masato and Sawashiro left, but not without the latter giving Ichiban one last glare. He became really quiet when the nicer guy showed up, but Koneko wouldn't complain. Honestly, she felt a little sidelined in their conversation. She didn't know what to say.

"Sorry. Must've been real awkward for you." Ichi quickly apologized, almost as if he'd read her mind.

"Er, it's okay." She said, surprised. "You seem very familiar with him."

"Heh. Yeah, we've known each other for a while." Ichi nodded. "When Arakawa-san accepted me, my first real job was to be a bodyguard to his son since Kamorucho was a shithole. Though, to be honest, he didn't need my help. He was way stronger than I was at the time."

"Mhm…" She hummed, waiting for Ichi to finish.

"Since he was the son of a known yakuza, he had trouble making friends his age, but we bonded pretty quickly." He continued. "Eventually, he left Japan to study abroad. He knows about the supernatural, but he didn't want to be involved in anything related to it. Yakuza included."

Koneko remained silent, watching them until they disappeared from her vision.

"Anyway, we should probably meet up with Rose-san," Ichiban said. "It's time."

"What about the ice cream?" Koneko asked, wanting her cold treat.

"Oh, right." Ichi snapped his fingers, turning toward the vendor. "As I was saying—"

But nobody was there.

"Eh?" He blinked. "Where'd he go?"

Koneko immediately realized and frowned. The funny interaction must've scared him off. Seeing two people fighting right in front of you in a way that did not look normal in any way would do that to anyone.

Koneko blinked, then jumped over the counter.

"What are you doing?" Ichiban curiously asked.

Nobody would notice a few scoops missing.





– Asia –

This investigation stuff was a lot simpler than Asia had thought it was gonna be. A lot less fruitful, too. Admittedly, she had no idea what she'd expected from this, but to just walk around looking for anything that looked off? In a city they barely knew? She wasn't one to complain about things like this, but this was starting to get a little boring.

Thankfully, she ultimately got to hang out with Akane, so maybe it's not all that bad.

Although Akane seemed focused on finding a lead rather than enjoying her time with Asia, the blond still found this pleasant. Delightful, even. Ever since they'd arrived at Honolulu, they'd been hanging out a lot more frequently than back in Japan. In Kuoh, Akane was usually too busy with schoolwork, tinkering, and/or training.

Coming here was the best thing that had ever happened. Ah, if only Mizuki were also here with them. Surely they'd have a lot more fun together. Just the three of them. Like the family she'd always dreamt of.

Asia had no idea why Mizuki didn't want to come with them, but she knew that something was bothering her. She wanted to ask the mother about it, but she hesitated, knowing that whatever it was, it was probably very personal. Regardless, she prayed that Mizuki would get through it fine.

Maybe if she was done with whatever it was, she could come and visit? After all, they were staying here for a whole month. That was plenty of time for her to join them eventually, right? Unless it was serious enough that she would need that much time.

If that was the case, then Asia felt terrible about going on vacation without first making sure that Mizuki was okay.

The blond shook her head, and with it, the bad thoughts. No, she couldn't be thinking like that. She was doing an important job and couldn't let these things distract her. Akane wouldn't let something like that happen to her, and neither should Asia.

"You look distracted." Akane suddenly said as they walked side by side, making her yelp. "What's gotten you so pensive?"

"Eh?" She blinked before sheepishly giggling. "Was it that obvious?"

"You seriously need to work on your poker face." Her older sister responded with a smirk. "Spill it. What were you thinking about?"

"Well…" Asia hesitated, then shook her head again. "It's nothing. I was just wondering what Mizuki-san is doing."

"She's fine. Knowing her, she's getting shitfaced somewhere." Akane said vulgarly. "She has a problem with alcohol."

"Yes, I've noticed." The blond nodded.

"Which is… fine, relatively speaking. She's superhuman. Her liver is probably made of titanium." Akane rolled her eyes. "The alternative is gambling addiction, and that's way worse. I wouldn't be as rich as I am today otherwise. Thank god she's stingy when it comes to spending money."

Something told Asia that Akane was a lot less worried about her mother and more about her own well-being. She didn't know if she believed in her mother that much or if she was just selfish, but Asia leaned toward the former, for both their sakes.

"Silver lining, I suppose?" Asia blinked.

"Silver lining." Akane agreed with a chuckle before checking her phone. "Anyway, we should probably go to Revolve right now. We're out of time."

"We are, aren't we…" She sighed. "And we haven't found any leads."

"Eh." Her sister shrugged.

At that, Asia paused. That wasn't the reaction she expected. Akane seemed like she didn't care about this one bit, even though this had been her idea. How odd. As temperamental as she was, even if Akane knew how to control herself, not to show even a sliver of frustration? That was unlike her.

"I thought you'd be a lot more disappointed." She noted.

"I would've been," Akane replied. "But you know what they say: Hope for the best, expect the worst."

"That sounds cynical," Asia frowned slightly.

"Maybe." The yakuza princess said. "But there's merit to it. That way, you're not as disappointed when things don't go your way."

That did make sense, but still…

"Besides," Akane added. "Chances of us finding anything were low. Like, 2% or below. I knew this was the case minutes after we set foot in Honolulu. Think about it: We've not found any of the Barracuda, even before we split up. That means they're doing their best to hide from us, and since we've not found their base yet, we don't know where to find them."

"I see…" Asia muttered. "But if that was the case, then why bother at all?"

"2% is still 2%. Chances are low, not nonexistent." Akane argued. "And like I said before, getting all of our information from Magnus might not be the smartest thing to do. We shouldn't trust him so quickly. Not when he hasn't given us a reason to trust him yet."

Asia didn't argue with that. Perhaps she was just naive, but Magnus Rose had seemed genuine when he talked about stopping the Barracuda from doing something dangerous. He didn't look like he had an ulterior motive. But Akane knew better than her. Trusting her sister's instincts was probably for the best.

As they approached the bar, Asia stopped when she heard the wails of a little child to her left. She turned in the direction of the sound, which was coming from the nearby orphanage. In front of it, there was a small yard where children were running and playing together, a scene reminiscent of what she had observed back at the church. It had brought back memories— good ones.

She'd passed by this orphanage once or twice before. Palekana Orphanage was apparently the only one in Honolulu. It was built and funded by a local religious group that went by the same name.

She scanned the yard and found the crying child next to a tree, having injured his knee after falling. Or what looked like it anyway. An old man — likely one of the caretakers — gently scolded him for doing something dangerous before comforting the boy.

"Asia?" Akane called her name, noticing that she'd stopped. "What's wrong?"

"Um." Asia hesitated. "Is it okay if I help that child, Akane-san? I know you told me not to show my powers to civilians unless it's necessary…"

"Seriously?" She frowned and looked at the child. "He's gonna be fine, Asia. A little boo-boo isn't going to get him killed."

"I know that, but…" The blond looked at her pleadingly. "Please? It's what I always wanted to use my powers for."

Akane clicked her tongue and crossed her arms, but then, eventually, she relented with a deep sigh.

"Fine." She said. "Just get it over with. We're gonna be late."

"Got it." Asia nodded with a smile. "Thank you, Akane-san."

With Akane right behind her, she approached the child, catching the caretaker's attention. Confusion flashed across his face as he turned to her. He appeared to be in his late sixties, with striking blue eyes and blond hair framed by a goatee. The old man wore a yellow shirt, white pants, and sandals. A unique pendant in the shape of three connected flames dangled around his neck.

"Ah…" The old man paused at her presence, glancing at the child, then back at her. "I am sorry. I hope his cries did not disturb you. It's just that he fell down and hurt himself."

"Oh, it's alright." Asia gave them a disarming smile. "I'm here to help."

"Oh, bless your kind heart. But you don't need to." He replied, thankful for her kindness. "It is nothing serious. A simple bruise is all it was."

"Even then, by the Lord's commands, I must help anyone in need." Asia insisted as she crouched next to them, a ring forming around her finger. "Please, allow me."

The caretaker looked at her curiously, and the boy's cries ceased as her Twilight Healing glowed a faint green, almost instantly healing the bruise on his knees. The boy and the old man both looked at her in awe, eyes wide in shock as well as recognition.

"Woah…" The boy breathed, looking at Asia with sparkling eyes. "You're like Lani."

"Huh?" Asia blinked. "Lani?"

"By Her grace… You are blessed as well." The old man added, gently taking her hand to observe the ring on her finger. "You have the power of restoration. Magnificent."

"You mean Twilight Healing?" Akane questioned. She was confused too. "You've seen it before?"

"Yeah!" The boy responded, grinning at Asia. "A girl here had the same ability! Her name is Lani Mililani! Do you know her, miss? What's your name? Do you live here?"

As the boy stood up, he continued to bombard her with questions, and Asia wasn't given the chance to answer any of them.

Though she was more preoccupied with the fact that there was someone else who had Twilight Healing, it wasn't unheard of— Twilight Healing was considered a low-level Sacred Gear, after all. Similar to something like Twice Critical, several people could have it at the same time.

But it still came as a shock. What were the odds? Was this meeting perhaps planned by the Lord?

"Easy, Tommy." The old man said, helping her up. "I apologize for him. As you heard, there used to be a girl who had the same power you have. He must've thought you were related to her. Though, unfortunately, she's been gone for a while."

"Gone?" Akane frowned.

"Kidnapped by a former staff member at the orphanage." He sighed wearily, making Asia gasp. "The police have been looking for them, but there's no news yet."

"Goodness, I'm so sorry," The blond responded.

"You have nothing to apologize for, miss." The old man shook his head before trying to change the subject. "Ah, where are my manners? My name is Bryce Fairchild, the Sage of Palekana. I own the orphanage."

"Ah. I am Asia Argento." She introduced herself. "And my friend here is Akane Amamiya. It's a pleasure meeting you, Mr. Fairchild."

Bryce blinked and glanced at Akane, who raised her eyebrow at him.

"Akane? What a coincidence." He said. "The one that took Lani away is also named Akane. Akane Kishida. Not that I mean anything by it."

"Eh. It is a common Japanese name." Akane shrugged.

"Is it? Sorry. I'm not very informed about Japan." Bryce said. "Please, why don't you come over for coffee or tea? I'd love to hear what you know about the power of restoration. Twilight Healing, you called it?"

"Well—"

Before Asia could give an answer, Akane took her hand and got in front of her.

"Sorry, we're busy right now. Maybe later." She told him before glancing at Asia. "Let's go. I just got a message from Ichi. They're waiting for us."

"Ah, right." Asia nodded, giving Bryce and the boy a smile. "Farewell. Please take care of yourselves."

They waved goodbye as the two girls walked away.

Wow. Another person with Twilight Healing was here? She was still surprised. Just what were the odds of Asia randomly stumbling on her? If she hadn't been kidnapped, then…
…

"Akane-san—"

"We'll look for Lani after we're done with Magnus," Akane replied, as if she'd read Asia's mind, giving the blond a smirk. "Can't have someone with my name go around kidnapping kids. Might end up hurting my credibility."

Asia smiled.

"Thank you."





– Akane –

As I expected, Asia and I haven't found anything despite searching for a few hours. Jobs like this should be done by the Spyders, but there's some guy out there that can detect and fry my tech, so fuck me, I guess.

Even the rest haven't found anything worth noting. Only that the Barracuda had vanished from every corner of the city. Also, apparently, Ichi randomly met Arakawa's son, so that's interesting, I guess. In case I ever wanted to get rid of him, I now have a way to lure him out somewhere.

Not that I plan to do such a thing anytime soon. If I ever want to dispose of Arakawa permanently, then it can't be by me directly. And there's a reason for that, of course. Simply put, I can't hide who I really am forever. It's neither possible nor appealing.

To hide under this guise of 'a good person'. Having to tiptoe around everything and everyone just for a crumb of progress. Doing everything I can to look 'good' in front of others. It pisses me off so much. Because why should I do all of that? I'm perfect the way I am. They should recognize that, too.

And by 'they', I mean those who can make me feel things. My 'property', so to speak. Ichi, my mother, Akiyama…

I want to show them the real me, eventually. But I know they'd never accept me for who I really am. Not when they're like… that. So sentimental and emotional. No. If I want them to join my side, then I need to take drastic measures.

And Ichi should be the easiest to deal with. If Arakawa died, then I'd be his sole emotional anchor. I'd be the one he relied on and loved the most. That way, I could try to convince him to see things my way, and he'd have no option but to agree.

But if he were to eventually know that I killed Arakawa, then he'd start despising me.

Even thinking about such a thing makes my stomach turn.

Which is why I have to orchestrate some kind of 'accident'. Make it so that Arakawa dies in a way that's not directly related to me. I can just do what I did to the Leviathan devil in prison, but that's not reliable enough for my taste.

But I digress.

The only interesting thing I found on my search was the old Palekana Sage. He's nothing special— his stats are low, his title revealed nothing of interest, and the 'thoughts about you' section was too vague for me to care.

However, his stats are low, yes, but that's in comparison to mine. They're actually higher than the average human by a ton. I'd even say around mid-class? For a human that old, that's pretty impressive. My first and best guess is that he has some kind of Sacred Gear that he has most definitely awakened.

Again, not that special, but a little interesting regardless. What's also a little interesting is that there's another Twilight Healing user running around. Anyway, I'd keep an eye on him with a Spyder, but…

Yeah.

I don't like the way he was looking at Asia, though. Felt a bit creepy.

We open the door to the bar, greeted by the rest of the group at the U-shaped booth seating directly to my left. Magnus is there too, but he's taken the stool in front of the counter, and behind it is another blond, caucasian man wearing sunglasses and cleaning a mug.

Using Observe on him tells me that he's another CIA agent. Way weaker than Magnus, though. High-class level.

"Took your sweet time." Magnus is the first to comment, not impressed with me.

"We were on the other side of the city. Sue me." I roll my eyes before addressing Asia. "Go sit with them."

"Okay."

As for me, I take the stool next to him. You know, being the leader and all that. I have to make an impression.

"So then—"

"Actually, before we start," I glance at the bartender. "One Mai Tai, please."

He raises an eyebrow at me.

"You're old enough to drink?"

"As a matter of fact—" I put down the totally real ID on the counter with a smirk. "I'm twenty-one years old."

The bartender doesn't look like he believes me, but says nothing.

"Seriously?" Ichi says, the rest of the group sharing his exasperation.

"You better shut your mouth." I glare at him. "I've been walking around in this heat for hours, and I deserve a drink for my efforts."

He looks like he wants to argue, but closes his mouth and scoffs. That's what I thought.

"Just give her what she wants," Magnus tells his CIA partner with a sigh.

As the Bartender goes to prepare my drink, Magnus takes a file out of his shirt and gives it to me. I flip through it, and the first picture I see is that of another old man, but this one looks wealthy. Gold chains around his neck, an expensive watch, and several rings. His most striking feature, though, was the stylized 'B' tattooed on the left side of his forehead.

"This is Dwight Mendez," Magnus explains. "The leader of the Barracuda."

Ah, so that's what he looks like. I knew his name, but none of the Spyders found him before they went kaboom. I hand the picture to the group as the CIA agent continues.

"A thorn in our side for years. He's been associated with the cartel and several other gangs before. Drug dealing, human trafficking— you name it, he's probably done it." He says. "The problem is, he has strong connections. Supernatural connections, which is how he's been evading us for years. Eventually, he settled here and made his own gang. The Barracuda."

"Is he strong?" Ichi asks.

Of course, that's his first question. Still valid, though. I'm curious too.

"Yes, but not as strong as most of us here." He answers. "You or Ms. Amamiya could probably easily beat him."

About Ultimate-class at most, then.

"Though it's not his strength that's worrying," Magnus adds. "In one of his previous gangs, he developed a dangerous drug that turned even the most fragile human into a powerhouse, comparatively. It's what his gang has been using."

As the chat goes on, the bartender serves me the glass of Mai Tai I asked for.

"'Powerhouse?' Really?" I chuckle, taking a sip from my drink. "Gimme a break."

Delicious~

"Compared to the average human cop?" He points out. Fair enough. "Regardless, they're not a big problem now, but my intel tells us that he's gradually improving this drug of his. Eventually, he'll be making an army of High-class minions. Maybe even stronger."

Sounds more like a blessing to me than a problem.

"Right. So he needs to be taken out." I nod. "Why haven't you done that already, then? I mean, I'm sure you have the resources to do something about him pretty easily."

"Yes. But that leads us to the bigger problem at hand." Magnus adds. "In the grand scheme of things, Dwight is nothing more than a minion himself, so if we take him out now, we could end up scaring away the real mastermind."

Oh? That's interesting.

"The Barracuda is only a third of Honolulu's underworld. There are two more organizations, and they're even more dangerous." He says. "The Ganzhe led by Wong Tou, and Yamai Syndicate led by Yutaka Yamai, a former Tojo yakuza. All of them answer to one person."

Right, the Ganzhe I knew about, but not the Yamai Syndicate. Former Tojo yakuza, huh? I should maybe ask Majima about him. He could have some info.

"You don't say?" I lean forward. "And who is this evil overlord we need to defeat?"

"That's the thing. We don't know." Magnus replies. "We only know that they're called the 'Overseer'. They rule Honolulu from the shadows, having even more authority than us, and they're planning to do something dangerous."

Overseer, huh? Could it be they who had been stalking me with whatever weird ability they might have? I thought it was Dwight at first, but that doesn't seem to be the case. I'm still lost on how they're able to do that.

And this leads me to another question: Is it them who spotted my spy tech? Someone working for them? One of these big gangs? Still don't know anything. It's frustrating, but hey, I am making some progress. That's cool.

"How dangerous?" Kiba questions.

"If we leave them unchecked, Hawaii might get wiped out at best." He answers. "At worst, the whole planet would be in danger."

Very interesting. Heh, would you look at that? We're finally facing our first world-ending threat. That's pretty damn exciting.

"Holy shit…" Issei breathed with a mixture of awe and fear. "For real?"

"The whole planet?" Ichi added. "You've gotta be exaggerating."

"I'm not. That's how serious this is." Magnus reiterates.

"How do you know that, though?" I raise an eyebrow. "I mean, what are we dealing with here? Is this Overseer that strong?"

I notice him hesitating for a split second before answering.

"We don't know how powerful they are as an individual." He says. "All we know is that they've found some weapon or artifact that they plan to use. We don't know what it is or where it is. We're lucky that he still hasn't found the key to use this artifact."

He's lying. Or rather, he's not telling the whole story. Hah. Knew we couldn't trust this bastard. And here I debated whether I should tell him about my ominous feeling that someone's watching me since coming here. Guess I'll keep that to myself.

Then again, I didn't feel it as much today. Rather, it felt… weaker, like it was looking at something or someone else. Someone near me.

"Right…" I drop it. I'd confront him about his lie, but I don't want him to suspect anything. Might as well make him feel he's in control. "So what are we supposed to do, then?"

"Right now, there's not much we can do," Magnus responds. "Dwight is hiding after what you did, so we'll need to lay low until he gets confident enough to come out."

"More waiting, huh?" I snort. "Forget it."

"Hmm?"

"I'm gonna start looking for Dwight myself," I tell him, getting off the stool. "Sooner we get rid of him and this 'Overseer', the sooner we can return to our vacation."

"And how do you plan on doing that, exactly?"

"I'll figure it out. I always do." I respond, finishing my drink, then looking at my group. "Let's go. We have a long night ahead of us."

"I thought we agreed to work together." Magnus narrows his eyes.

"We did, but I don't like your plan," I reply. "So I'm doing things my way. Don't get me wrong, though. We're still on the same side. I'll help you take out this Overseer."

He remains silent.

"See, I've learned that sitting around doing nothing rarely does us any good." I continue. "Think about it; if Dwight knows there are some super-strong people looking for him in Honolulu, then this Overseer probably does as well. He's gotta know who and where we are."

"Meaning Dwight likely won't come out until we leave Hawaii." Kiba nods, agreeing with me. "Akane-san is right. We need to act now."

"And like you said, this Overseer dude didn't find what he needed to use his artifact yet," Ichi adds. "So we gotta stop him before he does."

Magnus takes a moment to think it through before responding.

"And what do you suggest we can do?"

"Ideally, we try to lure them out." I shrug. "Dunno how, but give me an hour or so. I'll come up with something."

"…Alright." Magnus nods. "I'll try to figure something out on my end. I'll contact you soon."

"Sure thing." I wave, walking toward the exit with my friends in tow. "See you soon."

I honestly have no idea how I'm going to go about this, but it can't be that complicated. First, luring out the Barracuda or the other two organizations. Get to the leaders, beat them up for info, and kick the Overseer's ass. Simple.

I also need to figure out what this Overseer really wants. What this 'artifact' of theirs is supposed to do, and if I can have it for myself. What this 'key' looks like, and if I can get it before they can. Because color me intrigued.

Something that can possibly destroy the world… I already have one in my inventory, but it wouldn't hurt to get more firepower. After all, my world-ending artifact likes to nibble on my soul when I use it, and that's not very pleasant.

"So any ideas?" Ichiban asks.

"Nope."

"And you sounded so confident…"

"I am." I snort. "Trust me, this is gonna be easy."

Not really, but I'd have a much, much easier time using my Spyders.

Yes, I'm still very pissed that I can't use them. How could you tell?




– Yamai –

Staring at the photo in disinterest, his eyes flickered to his subordinate, who flinched under his gaze. Yamai didn't know what to do with him— he came running to his office, saying he'd found something that may interest his leader. But all he was given was the picture of a teenage girl with black hair and red eyes. Was this guy a pervert or something?

Yamai found this too reprehensible, even for him, but waited for the boy to explain himself. Everyone in his organization knew what type of woman he liked, and it was definitely not fucking teenagers.

"You call this interesting?" He said, his voice low and indifferent. His underling flinched again, making Yamai sigh. "What am I looking at, Kyo?"

"You don't recognize her?" Kyo questioned.

"Should I?"

"Er, no, it's just… It's Akane Amamiya, sir." He answered.

"Amamiya?" He raised an eyebrow.

"Yes. Daughter of Tatsu Amamiya of the Tojo clan." Kyo nodded. "She has an impressive resume for someone her age. Defeated a rogue cadre, killed the last of the Beelzebub bloodline, and was the MVP of a recent Rating Game tournament as a temporary piece."

Well, that was interesting, at least. As a former member of the Tojo clan, he was one of many who had looked up to the Immortal Dragon—a legend among legends. Even after being kicked out of the clan, he still greatly respected that man. One of his few regrets in life was never properly meeting the man before he passed away.

He would've loved to see the legend in action.

Then again, why should he care about his daughter? So what if she was in Hawaii? Was he supposed to do something about her? Why would he even bother with that? He might've considered kidnapping her or something had Tatsu been alive, but that was about it. With Tatsu dead, Yamai's interest had gone away with him.

…was what he thought until Kyo mentioned her achievements.

"Really now?" He hummed.

"Yes," Kyo confirmed with a nod. "The finals were livestreamed on Devilnet."

He picked up the picture again, inspecting it closely. It had been taken while she wasn't aware, but even from this still image, her posture wasn't that of an ordinary girl. Relaxed, sure, but most certainly not normal.

"I brought it up because I thought maybe we can use her against the Overseer," Kyo added. "Through her, we could get the Tojo clan involved."

That was one approach to handle that arrogant bastard, but what truly intrigued Yamai's interest was the prospect of discovering whether the daughter of the Immortal Dragon possessed the same fierce spirit as her legendary father.

…It wasn't like him to pick fights with teenage girls, but this time, he was willing to make an exception.
