– Akane –

I don't really get opportunities like this that often. Naturally, considering how 'unethical' the Devour skill actually is. To steal the essence of someone else, denying them reincarnation and an afterlife— such a fate should only be reserved for the scum of the earth. The worst of the worst criminals in the world.

But as I've already established a million times before, I frankly don't care what happens to those who oppose me. Why should I spare empathy for anyone, much less my enemies? It's nothing more than a ridiculous idea. Proof that compassion is a weakness and a leash that exists to stop you from reaching your true potential.

Had it really been in my power, I would have thrown away that weakness and become the strongest and best possible version of me. And what I'm saying isn't just metaphorical— I have actual, physical proof in the form of the Devour skill. Because really, what would they think of me if they saw me going around eating souls? They could barely stomach killing others in self-defense. It's senseless. Illogical. Utterly idiotic.

They are, first and foremost, still bound by human emotions, not logic, and unfortunately, I'm no different. I, of course, hold no remorse or regret for the terrible things I've done and will do in the future, despite full awareness. No, what truly holds me back is something else. Something arguably more illogical.

The fear of rejection by those I deem my confidants, the hesitation that I might just disappoint them if I do the wrong thing. It's nothing more than an ever-tightening noose around my neck. It's all so pitiful and pathetic, and each time I think about what I could do without these feelings, I feel nothing but overwhelming fury.

It's a hard limit that I can never break through until I find the strength to reject or break them first.

At the same time, though, it gives me these rare moments of freedom, when I can do whatever I desire— It's an indescribable taste that I just can't seem to get enough of. It's exciting, in a way. One tiny mistake can ruin it all. My friends, relationships, and position as a powerful political figure. All of it is practically hanging on a thread, supported by nothing but my own excellence.

And a small part of me hopes that said excellence fails me. It dreams of a day I make that mistake, because despite the pain that'll come with rejection, only then will I truly be free. Alas, my human side will never allow it. Not until I'm sure I won't lose anything from it.

I slice the arm off an incoming devil, thrusting my devouring claw through his chest.

"Love truly is nothing more than poison," I whisper at the dying devil with a smile, pulling his soul out of his body. "Don't you agree?"

As he falls over dead, I crush the soul in my hand and absorb its essence, increasing my stats further and making me shudder. This feeling is just so wonderful. This… buffet is everything I hoped it would be.

Slightly distracted by the indescribable feeling of feeding my own soul, I'm hit in the shoulder by a powerful blast of magic, making me stumble forward. I turn around and grin widely at the assailant, making them flinch. But what makes this all the more incredible to me is— What makes it so much sweeter…

"T-that was his soul… And you… You…" A yokai mumbles, walking backward. "You're a monster!"

…Is the overwhelming fear I strike into their hearts.

"Am I?" I giggle, twirling my sword and walking toward her. "Does it matter to you what happens to him? He's dead all the same, and you won't live long enough to grieve."

Her jaw clenches as her legs tremble, aiming both arms at me as magic gathers in her hands. I'm not worried, however, even as two more allies join her. A fallen angel and a vampire, casting their own spells and bombarding me with magic. Their powers are nothing to scoff at, with high-class strength that scratches the ceiling of ultimate.

I do not bother to dodge or defend myself in any way, simply walking into their attacks as a large cloud of dust and smoke covers the area. And as a relatively fragile human, even with my Satan-class power output, their attacks still hurt somewhat.

As they stop their onslaught of spells, I dash forward toward the yokai girl, piercing her chest with my blackened claws. She gasps in surprise, and as the vampire tries to help her, an ice sword flies out of the cloud and stabs him in the throat. The fallen angel, surprised by how quickly this is all going, panics and tries to cast another light spell before ice chains form around my arm and slither toward his leg faster than he can do anything, wrapping around it and slamming him into the ground.

My smirk widens as I take the girl's soul and crush it before her eyes, killing her instantly while my HP, MP, and SP go back to 100%.

Why worry about how much damage I might suffer when I can just heal right back up?

I pull the fallen angel with the chains, who panics harder and starts to scream, throwing more spells in hopes of saving himself. But nothing can save him. His life was forfeit the moment he saw me devouring the souls of his allies. Even if nobody would believe the words of a random convict over mine, even a rumor could pose a danger to me.

As a blade of light grazes my arm, shoulder, and even neck, my grin widens, and I pull the chains closer. Once he's close enough, I steal his soul as well, letting his empty corpse drop to the ground. I crush it, making all the wounds I've just suffered disappear in an instant.

"Hah…" A quiet moan leaves my mouth. "It's just too good~"

"Behind you, Akane," Lucifer warns.

"I know, I know~"

I casually side-step from a lethal attack, a blood spear aimed at my back, then turn around at the vampire, who has already regenerated, with a confident smile. He charges at me and swings a blade at my neck, but I effortlessly catch it with my hand before casually breaking it. Before he can recover and counterattack in any way, I wave my hand and turn him into an ice statue with a wave of frost before tearing his soul out of his body, taking his powers for myself.

This is everything I could've hoped for~

I bring up my stat page, unable to contain my laughter at what I'm seeing.

Name - Akane Amamiya

Level - 284

Title - Diligent Student

Primary Class - Juggernaut - LVL 84/100 [4%]

Secondary Class - Illusionist - LVL 71/100 [12%]

Race - Human

Rank - Mortal

Alignment - Neutral Evil

HP - 169,820 [19,408 per minute]

MP - 153,000 [56,532 per minute]

SP - 169,820 [19,408 per minute]

STR - 5551

END - 4852

DEX - 4361

INT - 5126

WIS - 4711

CHA - 3521

LUK – 2201

Over 1700ish points distributed across seven stats might not be much in the grand scheme of things, but it's still a marginal boost in power. My intelligence stat finally broke through the 5k mark, and while I didn't get a perk for it, that's still a huge milestone regardless, seeing how strong my magic already is.

I guess that settles it— I'm officially Satan-class. Not just in power output, but in everything. Speed, physical strength, etc. This isn't counting the new skills I got, like Light and Blood magic control, as well as a few perks that increased my HP, MP, and SP. Best of all, my Devour skill went up a level, and now I can steal more stats from my victims.

This feeling really is just the best~

And to think that my 'friends' are just right around the corner, that a single misstep would've exposed me to them. This was risky— EXTREMELY risky, but I just had to do it. Not only was I unwilling to waste this golden opportunity, but I just couldn't ignore it anymore. Those whispers in the back of my mind. My own soul demands to be fed. It had to be satiated.

I'm powerful enough to control these urges, but I can't deny that it gets more difficult every single day. I don't see myself ever losing control, of course. I'm too strong for that. And I'm sure if I ignore it long enough, it'll disappear on its own, but why should I do that when it benefits me to indulge?

Moreover, those idiots are too distracted by their own battles. They're too far away on the other side of the mall to really see what's going on here. They couldn't know what I've been doing, and anyone who saw me using Devour has already been devoured.

This was a free buffet. I barely had to try, and my power went up significantly.

Seeing me standing still in a semi-zen state, Lucifer speaks.

"Satisfied already, darling?"

I exhale and glance at him with an ever-present smirk.

"Satisfied? Please, Lucy. I'm a big girl. I need more than a couple of peanuts to feel satisfied." I reply playfully. "Then again, I also have to watch my figure. I can't indulge too much."

Lucifer chuckles.

"I suppose so. Too much could upset the stomach." He plays along, a hand on his chin as he sees my handiwork. i.e., the many corpses littering the floor. Of course, I made sure to desecrate them in very 'artistic' ways so the people cleaning up don't ask questions. "I must say this has been rather entertaining to watch. Reminds me of my old battles back when I was still alive. To stain the walls with the blood of my enemies, countless broken corpses lying beneath my feet. Ah, those were the days."

"I bet. I would've gone even harder if there wasn't a risk of being found out." I snicker. "But I'll settle with my peanuts for now."

I bring my devour-infused hand up and stare it with a satisfied look. I've noticed that it becomes more… evil-looking the more I level up the skill. Initially, it looked like my regular hand, but just as dark as the void. At level two, the hand became sharp claws. And now, the nails have become even sharper and longer, making it ever so slightly easier to rip out someone's soul.

And I gotta say, I like the aesthetic. It looks edgy. Threatening. Fits with the whole evil villain I'm planning to be. I wonder what it'll look like at max level.

Suddenly, the ground begins to shake, and I sense a relatively powerful energy signature approaching fast. A loud explosion followed by a noisy roar that echoes out in the mall, making me raise an eyebrow.

Wherever it is, it's attacking Xenovia and the rest. I'm guessing that's Patient Zero? Huh. It sort of feels like Ichi whenever he uses his Balance Breaker. I think that's what draconic energy is.

"And this must be that beast." Lucifer hums. "Hardly a challenge for you. How disappointing."

"I hoped I'd be surprised, but I wasn't counting on it being anything too powerful," I shrug, disabling the Devour skill as my hand returns to normal. "I'm just happy it's finally showing itself. About damn time."

I highly doubt I'll be able to devour it, but oh well. I think I've had enough souls.

As I'm about to go help them out, I pause as I accidentally hit something with my foot while walking, prompting me to look down at a small health potion. Then again, I was too busy devouring souls that I hadn't had a chance to loot anything…

…

I pick up the potion, grin, and look around for more stuff to take.

I'm sure they can handle themselves for a few minutes~




– Xenovia –

Deflecting an incoming fireball with Durandal, Xenovia charged forth toward her opponent— a dark elf, from the looks of it, who struggled to keep up with her. He cast more and more spells, trying to back away from the exorcist, but to no avail. She was faster, and with her holy blade, there was nothing she couldn't cut down.

Xenovia thrust her blade at the elf, who had backed away and avoided her strike by mere inches. She smirked, however, as Durandal suddenly shot a powerful blast of holy magic, piercing his chest and killing him almost instantly. The exorcist lowered her blade, observing the battlefield for a few moments.

Understandably, it was quite chaotic as waves of magic from numerous spellcasters coursed through the area, completely wrecking the black market. Xenovia guessed it had only been a few minutes, yet the place appeared entirely different. What had once been a neatly-arranged underground mall had turned into a scene of crumbling floors, with debris and rubble scattered in every direction.

Good. She thought.

Beyond the more pressing matters of finding Dwight's whereabouts, this was nothing more than cleanup duty, after all. These people were evildoers and deserved jail time for their crimes, and if they weren't willing to give up, then force would be used. And frankly, Xenovia couldn't care less if they had to be felled. Most of them were heretics, anyway.

Sensing an incoming attack, she twirled around and blocked the powerful swing of a mace from an ogre. Despite the green-skinned beast's much larger size, Xenovia quickly managed to overpower him, redirecting his mace to the side before slicing his belly open. Another heretic quickly attacked, this time a Lamia, hoping to catch her off-guard with her poison spit.

But Xenovia was no fool and avoided the monster's spell, charging toward her with far superior speed before effortlessly beheading the snake-like beast. Just then, two more heretics attacked the exorcist: a devil and a human magician.

And unlike many of the weaklings here, those two showed considerable strength as they managed to push back Xenovia. They didn't quite overwhelm her, but admittedly, being bombarded with many powerful elemental spells had her struggling. From weighty rock spears to sharp and precise ice blades, the exorcist gritted her teeth, suffering several scratches and bruises on her thighs, chest, and face.

Xenovia concentrated, sharpening her senses as she remained on the defensive. She blocked and deflected the various spells, finding a proper rhythm before starting her counter-attack. Even as they pushed her against the wall, she did not let it rattle her in any way and continued her focus until finally charging forward after getting used to their attacks.

With impressive adaptability, Xenovia turned the tables on her foes, targeting the devil first and slicing through every single spell he threw at her. From flaming javelins to demonic blasts, nothing stood a chance against the holy light of Durandal, dispersing the moment the spells made contact with it.

She weaved in between projectiles, keeping the human magician in her line of sight as she closed the distance with the devil, who had started to panic. As he tried to fly away, however, a pale blue line shot toward him and stabbed him in the side, stopping him in his tracks and giving Xenovia the opportunity to land a finishing blow.

At the same time, the human magician tried to stop her by throwing a massive fireball at her, which was thankfully stopped by Irina, who reflected it with an enlarged Excalibur Mimic, letting Xenovia cut down the devil with a single swing. The holy power immediately spread through his body, turning the two halves into ashes in mere moments.

Given a moment of respite, she sighed.

"Thank you," She said, looking at Issei.

He was looking worse for wear— bruises and wounds on his face, arms, and torso. They were minor injuries, however. He still looked able to continue fighting.

"No worries. I got your back." He threw her a thumbs-up.

"Not that I'm keeling over or anything any time soon—" Irina breathed, regrouping with them. "But I'm starting to feel tired."

"Yeah." Issei exhaled. "This is a lot harder than I thought it was gonna be."

Admittedly, Xenovia agreed. She could still fight for far longer and was used to much harsher training, but exhaustion could lead to mistakes, and one mistake could lead to death. And these criminals varied in strength, Xenovia noticed. Some were weak, some were quite formidable. All of those ice soldiers Akane had created were already destroyed, leaving the three to fend for themselves.

Speaking of—

"Where is Akane, anyway?" Irina asked, sharing her thoughts. "You'd think she would be here fighting with us, seeing how she wanted to be the leader."

Xenovia narrowed her eyes. For some reason, seconds after the battle began, the yakuza princess had suddenly disappeared and left them here to fight alone. Now, she wasn't saying Akane had run away— the girl looked way too arrogant to let something like this intimidate her. But it was strange how there hasn't been a trace of her since.

And with someone of her level of power, it was weirder that they couldn't even sense her. Yes, there was a lot of magic here messing with their sensory abilities, but she was bound to use a few spells that they'd be able to feel, right? Seriously, where had she gone, and what the hell was she doing?

"Maybe she found that Patient Zero thing?" Issei offered.

"Maybe." Irina hummed. "But then we'd know, right? If it's as strong as we're led to believe…"

"Regardless," Xenovia tightened her grip on Durandal as more enemies approached them. "Wherever she might be, Akane can take care of herself. Let's focus on—"

The blue-haired exorcist was quickly interrupted as the ground shook violently, nearly causing her and her allies to stumble and fall. Even their enemies paused their charge, curious and confused by whatever this was. Xenovia's frown deepened as she felt something coming from below, prompting her to grab Issei and Irina by their collars and leap away.

A sinkhole formed where they stood as a large… something smashed through, sending debris flying everywhere. Xenovia froze, her eyes widening in horror at what she saw. It was a half-naked horned man, with glowing slitted eyes and sharp teeth, attached to what looked like a giant, pulsating tumor.

"W-what the fuck is that?!" Issei cried out in horror.

The monster let out a roar, as its fleshy, vein-like, clawed tentacles lashed out at everything nearby, be it them or the criminals. It did not care who it hit, consumed by a monstrous urge to destroy everything in its path. But despite how powerful this thing was, Xenovia remained steadfast, deflecting one of the incoming tentacles with Durandal before backing away.

The criminals redirected their magic at the beast, showering it with a multitude of spells ranging from fire, light, ice, and wind. Blood and pus sprayed everywhere as it was wounded; however, it wasn't so easily slain as it responded in kind, its fleshy tentacles effortlessly tearing through some of the criminals like they were nothing but wet paper.

Moreover, all the injuries it suffered quickly healed, the tumor rapidly mending itself before their very eyes. It was a disgusting scene, Xenovia thought, but disgust wasn't going to keep her from doing the right thing and putting… whatever this monster was down.

The criminals had quickly realized that they stood no chance and promptly dispersed, running for their lives. This made the beast turn toward them, growling in anger and rage. Xenovia refused to run, and after taking a deep breath, she regripped her holy blade.

"Issei, Irina! With me!" She said, running toward it.

Although they hesitated, her two allies did not disappoint and charged forward with her. The beast roared, unleashing more of its tentacles toward them, but they were prepared, deflecting, blocking, or dodging its attacks. Despite its strength, these limbs were fragile, being easily cut apart by Excalibur and Durandal. Issei, on the other hand, used his Absorption Lines to limit the beast's movement, giving them a window to strike back.

Contrary to how it acted, the beast wasn't stupid and tried to keep its distance as countless tentacles shot toward them. Issei grunted as one of them slashed his leg, and Irina cried out in surprise. Another wrapped around her arm and tried to throw her away before Xenovia came to her friend's rescue, cleanly slicing through the weak flesh.

The speed was nothing to scoff at. Even she was struggling to defend herself as dozens— no, hundreds of tentacles shot toward her. Xenovia suffered more and more injuries as she tried to close the distance to a point where it began to affect her performance, and she eventually began to slow down. But she remained strong, letting out a battle cry before unleashing a wave of Durandal's holy power, taking out many of its tentacles at once.

The beast tried to get away, but with a cumbersome tumor and clumsy movement, as opposed to their decent teamwork and agility, they eventually caught up to it. Issei pierced its chest with an Absorption Line, and Irina swung her Excalibur upward, increasing its size several times over and nearly slicing the tumor in half. Xenovia, on the other hand, slashed its left arm right off as it tried to uselessly shield itself.

Xenovia glared at the beast, but now that they were close to it, she saw something she didn't expect. Beyond its mutilated body and the disgusting tumor it carried, tears ran down the beast's eyes as it looked at her pleadingly. For a moment, the blue-haired exorcist thought it was her imagination and decided to simply take its head off with a single swing of Durandal.

But then it spoke.

"H-help… Me…"

Xenovia hesitated, which gave the beast an opportunity as it smacked all three of them away with a newly created tentacle that looked much thicker than the rest. Xenovia, Irina, and Issei were all sent smashing into one of the few remaining marble pillars, causing more of the second floor to collapse onto the first one.

She coughed and hacked, pushing the debris off her and her friends before standing back up. Issei and Irina did so as well, getting into combat stances as the beast healed from all the damage they managed to inflict upon it.

Whatever that was just now… Xenovia huffed. It wasn't trying to trick me.

It truly needed help. But from what? Itself? That's what it felt like to Xenovia. Could this… 'Patient Zero' monster have been an unwilling test subject for these heretical criminals? But what for? What could it have that they'd need to do… this to it? To him?

If we can try to help him somehow…

"Ow…" Issei groaned, holding his arm in pain. "Damn it…"

"Are you okay?" Irina asked.

"Yeah, I think so." He replied with a nod as he kept staring at the beast. "Just what the hell is that thing?"

"I don't know. I've never seen anything like it before." Irina said. "Maybe this thing is Patient Zero?"

"Whatever it is, we gotta put it down before it causes the surface to collapse."

Xenovia admittedly hesitated, her expression turning into one of discomfort. She wanted to help him— she truly did, but Issei was right. But there was no guarantee they'd be able to in the first place, and with how powerful this poor thing was, it was a risk too great to take.

Damn it… She growled. To be an unwilling subject for someone's sick agendas is no sin. Why must one suffer like this?

The bastards who did this deserve to be sent to the deepest parts of hell.

Stumbling around, Patient Zero let out another roar, this time of anger and pain as he created more and more tentacles. But unlike those with a sharp, claw-like end, these ones glowed a fiery color at the tip.

"W-what the hell is it doing now—!" Irina started, and her eyes widened.

The glowing tips formed into powerful spheres of draconic energy before shooting toward them in a beam-like shape, at a much faster velocity than any of the other tentacles.

"Watch out!" Irina cried out as she quickly got in front of the two, enlarging the flat surface of her Excalibur and using it as a shield.

But her partner was quickly overwhelmed and was forced to let go of Excalibur Mimic, allowing the beast to land a finishing blow. Xenovia gripped Durandal and tried to deflect these beams, but there were too many of them, and as one of the beams soared toward Irina's heart, Issei pushed her away, taking the attack for her. Although it hadn't hit his heart, it still pierced his shoulder and left a large, smouldering hole, rendering him unconscious.

"ISSEI!" Irina screamed in horror.

"No! Damn it!" She hissed. "Irina, get him out of here and call for backup! Go!"

On the verge of panicking, Irina was immediately shaken out of her stupor by Xenovia's orders. As the grotesque monster charged several more of these beams, the blue-haired exorcist dropped Durandal and picked up Excalibur Mimic, doing what her partner had tried to do and blocking the beams with the sword's wide, flat surface.

"Now!" Xenovia urged.

Irina, with the unconscious Issei on her back, nodded and tried to run away, with Xenovia making sure to defend her partner with every fiber of her being. However, her eyes widened in horror as the titanic beast suddenly charged toward them, destroying whatever remained of the stores that stood in its path.

With the beams of draconic energy keeping pressure on her, Xenovia had no way of defending herself or her allies. All she could do now was pray, hoping that any of their other allies had sensed or heard the commotion and were on their way to help.

And thankfully, her prayers have been answered in the form of a gigantic ice pillar smashing into the beast and pushing it to the other side of the mall, causing the entire underground to shake. Fortunately, this seemingly forced the beast to stop the continuous stream of magical beams, and Xenovia's strained arms and hands made her drop Excalibur Mimic to the ground with a grunt.

She turned her head around and saw the yakuza princess casually walking toward them, and although her outfit looked worse for wear with a few cuts and tears, Akane herself seemed completely unharmed.

"I look away for a couple of minutes, and you're already buckling." She said with a mocking tone, and whether she was dead serious or only teasing, Xenovia wasn't sure. "It's pathetic. You people seriously can't do anything without me."

"Where the hell were you?" Xenovia questioned seriously, in no mood to joke around. "Issei's hurt. Badly."

"He'll be fine." Akane rolled her eyes as what looked like a potion appeared in her hand out of nowhere before she gave it to Irina. "Here. Found this lying around in one of the stores."

"Oh." Irina sighed in relief. "Thank you so much."

Akane stared at the exorcist with a raised eyebrow as she helped Issei drink from the potion.

"What, no mouth-to-mouth?" She snorted. "And here I thought you liked him for some reason."

"Huh?!" Irina's face went bright red. "U-um, well— I just—"

Xenovia found this scene to be very gross for whatever reason, so she was quite thankful that the beast decided now was the best time to interrupt them, throwing the ice pillar aside and casting several more draconic beams at them.

With a casual wave of her hand, Akane created a massive wall of ice that easily blocked the beast's attack. Then, with a snap of her fingers, the wall shattered into thousands of sharp ice shards before being flung into Patient Zero's direction, tearing it apart.

But Xenovia knew that this wasn't enough.

"I'm just teasing you~" Akane giggled. "Go on, get out of here. I'll handle this."

"R-right." Irina nodded, and with Issei on her back, she ran off. "Thank you so much, Akane!"

Once she left the two alone, Xenovia grabbed both Durandal and Excalibur Mimic, and as the beast quickly regenerated, Akane hummed in mild fascination.

"First time I ever fought someone with super regeneration." She said, smirking widely. "Wonder if it can outheal my DPS~"

Xenovia had no idea what 'DPS' meant, but she ignored it in favor of telling Akane what she knew.

"Akane, this Patient Zero—" She started, making Akane glance at her. "He needs our help."

"Hmm?" Akane raised an eyebrow.

Xenovia, Irina, and Issei may not be strong enough to take the risk, but Akane was far beyond them in strength, even combined. She could help him.

"He's lashing out because he's in pain. In a constant state of suffering." Xenovia explained. "He's not willingly trying to hurt anyone, so if you can—"

"I got it, I got it," Akane smirked, creating an ice sword before walking towards it. "I'll put it out of its misery."

"What? No, that's not what I'm trying to say!" Xenovia protested, but she was swiftly ignored as the beast attacked once more.

This time, a combination of energy blasts and tentacle claws shot toward the yakuza princesses, who effortlessly deflected everything with her sword. Not a single attack made it past her seemingly impenetrable defenses as Akane continued her advance toward the beast.

"God, you're so ugly." She said. "You deserve to be put down for daring to curse my eyes with your repulsive form."

"Akane, stop!" Xenovia said.

"Be quiet," Akane replied, glaring at her. Even without looking, she easily deflected everything coming her way. "I beat you in our duel, so you'll listen to everything I say. That's what we agreed on."

It was quickly becoming very clear that Akane had no intention of helping the poor man.

"If you're going to kill him, then at least make it quick," Xenovia growled.

"I told you to shut the fuck up. Can't you understand basic orders?" Akane responded, this time a lot more aggressively. "Now to do this world a favor…"

Xenovia gritted her teeth, but she did remain silent as Akane returned her focus to the beast.

Realizing he was severely outmatched, the monster roared and released hundreds more tentacles, each easily countered by Akane's ice sword and magic. It had gotten to a point where the monster started to back away from her, almost in fear.

Eventually, as Akane deflected one of the tentacle claws, it quickly recovered and wrapped around her arm. But the yakuza princess didn't even budge as the monster failed to throw her away.

"And here I thought you'd be a challenge."

Akane firmly grabbed the tentacle around her arm and swung the massive monster around, smashing it into the walls before yanking off the tentacle, letting it drop to the floor.

"Guess I was worried for nothing."

This battle was very quickly turning one-sided, and Xenovia knew that there was no saving that monster now. With Akane seemingly uninterested in helping it despite her words, all that was left for it was death.

And something told Xenovia it wouldn't be a quick one.





– Raynare –

For someone of her caliber, it was only expected that she'd be relegated to the less… direct missions. Things like scouting or undercover spying were more Raynare's forte, unlike, say, a real combatant or soldier. She was, after all, very weak compared to most of her colleagues back in the Grigori. Nothing more than fodder.

And she was okay with that. She didn't particularly care about gaining power and was hoping that one day she'd be given less dangerous responsibilities. Maybe a desk job or something. She may not be able to throw the most powerful light spears in the world, but she was pretty good with paperwork.

Unfortunately, Raynare was born unlucky, and with her lacking any real talent or power, she was very easy to intimidate, so when that asshole Kokabiel used her and a couple of others for his idiotic, warmongering plans, she couldn't do anything to stop him. She couldn't tell Lord Azazel or anyone else for fear of being killed.

Raynare was afraid of dying, naturally, and while what was waiting for her was reincarnation, she didn't hate herself enough to accept death so soon. She was too young to die. Still 134 years old, damn it. That's barely a young adult in fallen angel years.

But now there was no need to worry about that bastard anymore. She had been rescued, given an extended vacation in one of the most luxurious places in the human world, and left to her own devices, all her expenses taken care of by the Grigori. All because of the yakuza princess who had shown her mercy when she frankly hadn't deserved it.

The same couldn't be said for the other fallen angels, but they had been avenged by Akane, hadn't they? Yes, she was the one who'd actually killed them, but they weren't even supposed to be in Kuoh in the first place. Kokabiel had set them up for death when he'd provoked the yakuza. What choice had she had?

It was still mind-boggling to think about. Just how this young woman had suddenly found the strength to defeat someone like Kokabiel, even though she used to struggle to fight a couple of low-class combatants. Without a Sacred Gear or anything, somehow she was able to go toe-to-toe with and defeat a cadre, then proceed to kill one of the Old Satans' leaders.

And to think it only took her a few months to reach this level of power from a regular human. Raynare found it amazing. She thought Akane was incredible and was very much enchanted by both her power and achievements. She wasn't just a human— she was something more than that. Something better. Something for Raynare to idolize.

Raynare had gone from looking down on the yakuza princess to thinking she was the most remarkable living being that had graced this universe. She had everything, from strength to talent to charisma to near peerless beauty, and that was something Raynare idolized. She was infatuated with Akane, becoming her biggest fan.

Getting this chance to meet Akane again was like a dream come true. She almost couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the yakuza princess randomly walking around Honolulu, and she was ecstatic when her idol said that she'd put her grievances with Raynare behind her— letting bygones be bygones, as she'd said. That meant Akane didn't hate her, and that made Raynare hope to use this whole situation with the Overseer to get closer to her. Maybe they could even become friends?

Even the thought made it hard not to squeal in excitement. Being friends with her— what an honor! But did someone like low-class Raynare even deserve to be around someone as incredible as Akane, much less be her friend? Raynare didn't know, but that didn't mean she wasn't going to help her when asked.

Yes. You heard that right. The Akane Amamiya had asked Raynare for help. She couldn't believe it, either. Was this a dream or what? To survey the area as she and a couple of others went down to wipe out the underground mall may not be the most important mission of all time, but it still amounted to something. She had a purpose, and by god, she wasn't going to let Akane down.

…Though Raynare wished she wasn't stuck with her of all people.

In one of many cafes scattered around the southern section of Honolulu, Raynare dragged her eyes from the tableside window and glanced at the blond girl, who looked extremely nervous in her presence, making Raynare grimace.

She didn't know what Akane had been thinking when she'd paired them together — probably an idea so intellectual that Raynare couldn't hope to comprehend it — but she seriously didn't like this. Not when the devils and that Red Dragon Emperor boy each had their own places to monitor.

Raynare had nothing against Asia, of course. But considering their history, things were very awkward between them. Those feelings were shared by the nun, it seemed, as she refused to make eye contact with the fallen angel.

Her fingers drummed on the table as this atmosphere grew harder and harder to ignore, looking through the window again before Raynare decided to speak, hoping to maybe make this less tense.

"So… It's been a while." She started. "I see you integrated in Japan pretty well without us, huh?"

"Um, yes." Asia nodded. "Akane has been taking care of ever since… that incident."

Raynare frowned slightly.

"I see," Raynare replied. "And how's life there?"

"It's great!" The blond said, suddenly sounding excited. "I'm still not the best at the language, but Akane's been teaching me."

…

"So you've been enjoying yourself," Raynare stated, and although she outwardly remained composed, her heart burned with jealousy.

"Yes. Akane's so nice to me. She and her mother always treat me well and spoil me with gifts." Asia answered, holding her cross necklace. "I don't know what I did to deserve it, but they're like my family now, and I wish to repay their kindness one day. In any way I can."

Raynare's lips thinned.

What the hell was wrong with her? Why did she have to bring up Akane every time she spoke? Was she trying to brag about how close she was to Akane? Was she trying to ridicule Raynare? Was Raynare being mocked? Had nothing against her, scratch that, Raynare hated this bitch now.

"Good for you…" Raynare muttered quietly.

She was recently excommunicated and homeless, and now she's mooching off Akane's generosity. All because she was lucky enough to be rescued by her. What a joke. Why Akane would keep someone like Asia around was beyond her. She wasn't just weak, but a pushover and totally useless, too.

As the conversation died down, moments later, the ground beneath them suddenly shook, causing some of the civilians to stumble, drinks and plates of dessert to fall, and the lights to flicker.

"What's going on?" One of the cafe's patrons said with a concerned tone. "An earthquake?"

No. Raynare thought, sensing something below them. Looks like something big is happening down there.

"It's Akane," Asia muttered. "She's fighting someone."

"Or something." The fallen angel said, the ground shaking again. "And whatever it is she's fighting, they're being destructive."

"Oh, goodness." The blond looked worried. "I hope she's okay."

Raynare's eyes narrowed.

"Aren't you her friend?" She questioned a bit too confrontationally.

"Huh?" Asia blinked.

"Seriously, don't you have any faith in her?" Raynare added with a scoff. "It's Akane. There's no one in Hawaii, much less down there, who can beat her."

Although a little confused at first, the blond nodded.

"Yeah, you're right." She giggled awkwardly before looking out the window. "I guess I'm just being a worrywart."

So much for being friends. Raynare thought.

The ground shook once more, this time more violently. Panic began spreading among the nearby civilians in the cafe as they tried to hide beneath tables. Even the ones outside looked for safety, mistaking this for an earthquake. Hawaii wasn't new to those due to volcanic activities, after all.

"Hey, isn't that—" Asia started before her eyes widened. "It's Mr. Bryce!"

Following her line of sight, Raynare spotted the Sage of Palekana out on the other side of the road, simply struggling to stay standing each time the ground beneath them trembled. In his hands were bags of groceries, spilling out onto the sidewalk as he fell over.

"We have to help him," Asia said.

"Don't," Raynare replied. "Akane told us to stay here and keep watch."

"But what if he gets hurt?"

"He will be fine." The fallen angel insisted.

But as she said that, the ground shook a fourth time, this time hard enough to rupture the concrete road. Cracks and potholes began to appear as panic and fear intensified, with some believing this was going to be a major earthquake. What the hell was going on down there?

Seeing this, Asia made up her mind and dashed out of the store.

"Hey, wait!" Raynare exclaimed before hissing. "Idiot…"

She went after the blond, who quickly helped the old man get back on his feet. The fallen angel scowled in anger at Asia's insubordination.

"I told you not to run off like that!" Raynare scolded.

"I'm sorry, Ms. Raynare, but he needs my help." She responded, the conviction in her tone catching the fallen angel off guard. "Are you okay, Mr. Bryce?"

"Ms. Asia?" He mumbled, looking confused. "What are you doing here?"

"It's a long story." She replied. "Come on, let's get you out of here. It's too dangerous to—"

Before she could finish that sentence, the ground beneath them suddenly split open into a large sinkhole that quickly swallowed all three of them. Raynare reacted, her black-feathered wings sprouting off her back as she tried to fly away, but as she looked down and spotted Asia and the old man falling further and further, she clicked her tongue and dived down.

She quickly realized that the sinkhole led to the underground mall, which looked nothing like a mall in any meaningful way. If anything, the utter devastation made it look like a warzone. What the hell happened here?

That thought was cut short as she heard the guttural roars of a beast that sent shivers down her spine. She glimpsed a mass of flesh, eyes widening to the size of saucers as hundreds and hundreds of veiny tentacles swung around it, destroying everything in its path.

What the hell is that?! Raynare was terrified. No. Focus, Ray.

Right before they hit the ground, Raynare caught them both and quickly tried to get away through the same sinkhole, but she wasn't so lucky, as something pierced her right wing and nearly scratched her eye off, completely stopping her momentum and breaking her balance.

Crying out in pain, Raynare fell with the two humans in her arms, crashing into a pile of rocks and debris. She groaned and hissed, blood pouring out of the wound in her forehead as she got up on her feet. She coughed as she accidentally inhaled some dust, then she flapped her wings, thanking her lucky stars that the injury wasn't serious enough to prevent her from flying. It just hurt a bit.

But she could handle a little pain.

She looked around for the idiot nun who'd gotten them into this mess, spotting her sitting next to the unconscious body of the old man. He was bleeding from a gash on his head, likely from the fall, and an open wound across his chest and arm. Raynare thought it was a miracle he was still alive, even if he was hanging by a thread. But when had he gotten hit? Did the thing that attacked her also get to him?

"Mr. Bryce!" Asia yelled. "Oh, lord!"

As she called upon her Sacred Gear, a glowing green ring appeared on her finger. She hovered both hands above the downed Bryce, and Twilight Healing's soothing energy glowed a gentle light that seeped into his being, very quickly healing his life-threatening wounds.

Although he remained unconscious, he wasn't in critical condition anymore, prompting Asia to sigh in relief. When she noticed Raynare in the corner of her eyes, she gasped in surprise.

"You're hurt!" She said, approaching the fallen angel in hopes of healing her.

This made Raynare scowl angrily.

"And whose fault do you think it is?!" She yelled.

"Eh?" Asia blinked, stopping in her tracks.

"Seriously, are you an idiot? I told you not to run off!" She reiterated. "Look where your recklessness got us!"

"B-but I had to! Mr. Bryce would've gotten hurt!"

"That doesn't mean you can just do whatever you want!" Raynare argued as Asia's green eyes widened. "We had strict orders to—"

"Look out behind you!"

Raynare paused, becoming confused for just a moment until she felt the presence of death directly behind her. She turned around, seeing the mass of flesh attached to the body of a man looming over her, its tentacles lashing directly toward her.

"Ah…" Raynare uttered quietly, unable to move.

She couldn't move in time— she was nowhere near fast enough, even as everything slowed down. Her life flashed before her eyes while she wondered what she had done wrong to deserve this. Yes, maybe she hadn't lived the most fulfilling life of all time. Maybe she wasn't the nicest person around, either, but death?

Wasn't that too far? Raynare had done her best to follow Akane's orders. She hadn't let anything distract her from doing her job. She didn't think she deserved to die because the blond idiot next to her had decided to ignore said orders.

All because she wanted to help some random old man who looked like he was three months away from dying anyway. Why did Raynare have to pay the price for Asia's stupidity? She should've just flown away without them. She should've left them to die here.

As the tentacles were mere inches away from reaching her, her black-haired savior appeared in front of her and froze the tentacles solid before pushing the grotesque monster back with a battering ram of ice.

The fallen angel fell on her rear, her eyes glued on Akane's magnificent form. Her majestic crystal wings spread wide, tiny snowflakes gliding down as her overwhelming aura engulfed all that was around them. Raynare could see her own breath from how cold it was, and yet, she was utterly mesmerized.

Although her clothes were a little torn, Akane seemed utterly undamaged, having effortlessly pushed back a beast thousands and thousands of times more powerful than Raynare could ever hope to be.

She'd seen her defeat that former yakuza agent, so she had somewhat of an idea of how powerful she truly was, but this? This was different. Like an entirely different league. Simply feeling this power nearly choking Raynare was…

Beautiful. She thought. She's beautiful.

Akane glanced back at them, shimmering light blue pupils within sharp red irises. She seemed somewhat displeased, but mostly confused.

"What the hell are you doing here?" She asked, her voice calm and even.

"Huh? Ah— I— I mean, we—"

But all Raynare could do was stammer in a high-pitched voice, with her face becoming crimson red.

"Akane, it's Mr. Bryce!" Asia answered, pointing at the old man. "A sinkhole appeared and swallowed all of us!"

Akane's eyes widened in surprise as she spotted the Sage of Palekana, but her expression quickly shifted into one of thought as she gazed at the sinkhole, then back at Asia.

"I see. I guess I wasn't being very careful while dealing with this disgusting abomination. My fault." She hummed. "Then again, throwing something ten times my size around like a ragdoll was pretty fun."

The roar of the beast made Raynare cover her ears from how loud it was, but naturally, Akane was entirely unaffected. Even as it charged at the yakuza princess with its lashing tentacles at a speed Raynare couldn't hope to conceive, Akane simply raised one hand where magic began gathering in her palm.

"I probably should end it before this gets out of hand." She muttered to herself as a perfect, smooth sphere formed in her hand.

Once it reached its desired size, Akane closed her hand into a fist, crushing the sphere. Reduced to nothing but particles, she threw the spell at the beast, which proceeded to freeze it solid. It was stopped almost immediately, its tentacles halting just a hair away from the yakuza princess.

A beast that large and that powerful, turned into a glittering statue of ice in less than a second…

"Your healing factor might've proved troublesome to others, but me?" Akane smirked, creating a gigantic baseball bat made of her ice. "My ice magic is cold enough to freeze atoms in an instant. You never stood a chance."

She regripped the bat and swung it at the monster, shattering it into a million pieces. As Xenovia approached them with a displeased frown, Akane dispelled her weapon and stretched her back with a satisfied groan.

"If you had the ability to kill him so easily, then was this necessary?" The blue-haired exorcist growled. "Torturing him like that—"

"No, but it was fun." Akane shrugged, utterly unapologetic. "And it was a monster hellbent on killing us. I'm not going to spare any sympathy for it."

"And your 'fun' was all that mattered, wasn't it?" Xenovia argued, growing more frustrated. "Because of you dragging this fight for the sake of your own pleasure, someone got hurt."

"Well, maybe you should've kept your mouth shut," Akane replied. "But you just had to talk bullshit about it wanting to be saved. As if your opinion ever mattered to me."

Something about this made Xenovia's eyes widen.

"What did you say?" Her expression rapidly went from shocked to angry. "Spite? You did this— tortured that poor man out of SPITE?! Are you out of your—"

Akane cut Xenovia off by grabbing her by the neck, glaring at her with a sneer. The exorcist gasped, either of surprise or fear, Raynare didn't know.

"You still don't seem to understand. But with a skull as thick as yours, I'm not surprised," She started with a low tone, the air around them growing colder by the second. "So let me make it crystal clear for you: I make the rules. I say what we can and can't do. It's my right as the strongest, and as the one who defeated you in a duel, and until I ask you for your input, you'll stay silent and follow my orders without question."

Xenovia said nothing, and although she looked quite anxious, she was brave enough to stare at Akane defiantly. Both Raynare and Asia were tense, utterly quiet, not sure what to do or say in a situation like this.

"We're not friends, and I certainly don't care what you think of me. You're nothing to me other than a mildly powerful ally, and you're only getting involved in this mess because I was kind enough to allow you to." The yakuza princess said. "So, unless you want to be sent back to Italy in a box, Ambassador, keep that in mind next time you try to order ME around, got it?"

Xenovia said nothing, but Akane took her silence as obedience and eventually let her go. The blue-haired exorcist ran a hand over her neck, nervous sweat rolling down her cheeks.

"Now, let's get out of here," Akane said, addressing everyone, walking past Xenovia. "Before the authorities show up. We don't want to be seen, so we're leaving through the tunnels. Follow me."

With that, she took the lead, and everyone followed. All the while, Raynare couldn't take her eyes off Akane's back. She was utterly bewitched by the girl in front of her. Everything about her was dignified. Her proud attitude, her well-placed confidence, her unbelievable power and skill— it was as if she were actual royalty. No, she was more than that.

She was Divine.

It was there, and then that Raynare silently decided that none deserved her undying loyalty more than her. Not the cadres. Not the Grigori. Not Azazel.

But Lady Akane Amamiya.




– Akane –

Soon after utterly wrecking the black market, I informed the rest to retreat to the resort so I could share everything I learned. With Xenovia, Asia, and Raynare in tow, we managed to slip by without anyone from the authorities noticing us. We used the military tunnels we came through, which led us to the other side of town. Away from the cops.

Now, I'm not really concerned about them or anything finding the market down there, because it's going to be very swiftly cleaned up and hidden by the US government, but I am worried that we caused enough racket for said government to get involved more thoroughly. You know, besides sending Magnus.

Speaking of which, apparently, he's not done with his investigation into the Ganzhe and Wong Tou, and I doubt we'll be hearing from him for a bit. He likes to use more… meticulous methods, rather than just bulldozing his way through whatever stands in his way. Even though I've already proven that my methods are a lot more effective.

Not like it matters. We're gonna have to lay low for a while, anyway.

"So Dwight wasn't there after all…" Ichi sighed. "Kinda hoped he'd be. I mean, what safer place to hide in other than a market filled with countless superpowered criminals, right?"

"It's too obvious." I shrug. "I doubt he'd put himself at risk, seeing how the CIA wants him. Better a place than nobody knows about."

I'm not really surprised that we didn't find a trace of him there, but I wasn't entirely counting on it, in all honesty. What mattered more to me was getting to increase my stats via Devour and looting the fuck out of the place. Of which, I got to do both. I may not have grown leagues more powerful than I was, but it's a significant boost regardless.

As for the loot, well, to be honest, a lot of it is useless shit you could find anywhere. I thought I'd get things like weapons or artifacts, but most of what I found was stuff like expensive brand clothes made out of endangered mythical beasts, a couple of pieces of enchanted jewelry, potions, lots and lots of drugs of both natural and supernatural origins. You know, useless stuff for the most part.

I did find some useful loot, too, though. Phenex Tears, supernatural materials like Mithril, Orichalcum, and Adamantine, monster parts from griffins, wyverns, and hydras, some magic crystals of various elements, and most importantly, a large chunk of Agreasite.

Yup. The crystal I've been salivating over ever since Lucy first told me about it. A whole chunk of it, and while it's of low quality according to the Devil God, it's more than enough to begin the project I've been holding off on. I'm VERY excited to start working on it.

I had a feeling I was going to find some here, as you can only legally acquire it from the Agares pillar. That doesn't mean I'm canceling my plans to raid their little floating island, though. I still need more. Way more, vastly better quality Agreasite if I want to build strong armor.

"Even though he had that Patient Zero thing in his back pocket?" Issei questioned, having woken up and recovered.

Irina sat close next to him, still throwing him concerned glances every once in a while, even though he had been healed by Asia after we came back. Sheesh, talk about madly in love.

Terrible standards, though.

"That thing clearly couldn't be controlled. He'd put himself at risk standing anywhere near it." I argue. "And if that really is the case, then Dwight has to be way weaker than I thought."

That thing wasn't even a challenge. I was messing around with it because I was bored, and because the blue bitch kept bothering me. I literally could've ended it whenever I wanted, and only thought to see if regular ice spells could overwhelm its healing factor. You know, using it as a test dummy. I even made a couple of new spells to test out, because the dungeon monsters immediately die if I so much as glare in their general direction.

Can't really train much over there anymore.

On the bright side, I'm very close to unlocking the third-tier dungeon. I'm level 286 — I leveled up twice when I killed Patient Zero — and I need to reach level 300 for it to open. I'm very excited, as I jumped in power significantly in the past two dungeons, so I'm hoping this will give me a similar boost. Also, the next one is a dragon dungeon. Isn't that cool?

A Dragonslayer title is a lot cooler than 'Diligent Student'. Even if it's admittedly pretty useful to have.

"So we're back to square one, huh?" Ichi says, leaning back on his chair. "Killing his trump card must've spooked him. I doubt he's going to show his ugly mug any time soon."

"He doesn't have to," I smirk, drawing everyone's attention. "I have this, after all~"

I take the scientist's phone out of my inventory and wave it for everyone to see.

"This phone has Dwight's number in it." I elaborate before anyone asks.

Although everyone immediately understands where I'm going with this, Xenovia, being the dipshit she is, simply has to ask.

"So?"

"So, I'm going to dox his ass," I answer. "Even if he wises up and gets a new phone number and a new device, we'll still know his last hiding spot. There's literally nowhere he could run now that I have this."

"So you're saying he's completely fucked?" Issei asks with a smile.

"In every conceivable way." My grin widens. "I bet he's scrambling for a solution now that we've wiped his entire operation off the face of the earth."

I'm not the only one happy about this, as the rest — except Xenovia, who's still sore about how I scolded her for being an arrogant moron — celebrate. See? My genius is unparalleled.

"Oh, he's so done. He has nobody to protect him." Ichi says. "You're amazing, Akane. Seriously."

"Of course, I am." I giggle. "I'm me, after all."

"How long would it take you to locate him?" Kiba asks a valid question.

"Not very," I answer a little ambiguously. "Should have it figured out by tomorrow morning at the latest."

"So he barely even has a chance to hide somewhere else," Irina concludes. "And that's assuming he knows you can dox him in the first place."

"He probably doesn't," Koneko says.

"He's dead dead." I reiterate. "There's no place in Hawaii that he can hide in anymore."

I guess he might come to the conclusion that the CIA's going to dox him, not me, but it doesn't really matter. Even if he does, as Irina said, he doesn't have enough time to hide anywhere.

"Then we strike the moment Akane gets his location," Ichi said. "Everyone cool with that?"

"I doubt we need so much firepower to put him down." I slightly disagree. "Either you or I would be enough for him."

"Then—"

"And I call dibs." I beat him to it.

"Aw, come on! Really?!" Ichi complains. "Why do you get all the fun stuff?"

"You'll be fine, you big baby." I tease him. "I doubt he's even half as strong as you, so there's no reason for you to want this fight. And unlike you, Ichi, I like bullying enemies weaker than me."

Everyone looks at me with exasperation after my very casual confession.

"Hearing you say that so casually makes me a little concerned about what you plan on doing to him," Irina mutters.

"I guess I can't argue with that? Ignoring the weird but unsurprising admission of sadism from you." Ichi sighs. "But next time someone strong shows up—"

"It'll be your turn to fight them. Sure." I nod. I don't like this battle-junkie trait of his, but I'm willing to give him a pass. He's lucky I love him. "Besides, you're too nice to get information out of him. I, on the other hand, can be very convincing."

"That's fair, I think." He says. "You're a lot scarier than me."

And willing to do way more to get what I want, but let's leave it at who's scarier.

"Then it's settled," I say, getting off my chair. "You should all rest for now. In the meantime, I'll be busy tracking his location."

Which, again, shouldn't take too long. Probably less than a couple of minutes, but nobody here is as tech-savvy as me, so I can take my sweet time. Why would I do that, seeing how getting to Dwight is a priority? Because there's something else I need to worry about. Something a lot more important.

And it's figuring out how the hell Bryce got dragged into our mess. How did he stumble on Asia and Raynare like that? Asia said she found him randomly, seemingly on his way to the orphanage with groceries.

…But I refuse to believe that. My gut is telling me something different.

Not to worry, though. I had a Spyder on him the entire time, so I just need to go back to my secret base and watch its recording. So I didn't just corner Dwight now that I have his location, but now I have concrete proof that Bryce is the Overseer.

My genius really is unrivaled~



– Lucifer –

Alongside his potential successor, they watched the footage recorded by the Spyder she left with Bryce, the girl's eyes wide in utter shock as they saw what neither of them had admittedly expected.

It was nothing. Absolute nothing. Nothing suspicious or incriminating. Nothing that could prove his identity as the Overseer. Nothing that even hinted at the mere idea that they could be the same person in any way.

Akane rewound the video to the beginning, her magic slowly bubbling with rage at what she had seen. She was almost in disbelief.

The video began with Bryce in his office, alone and seemingly reading the christian bible. A little odd, but this proved nothing. This was nothing more than an old religious man interested in another religion.

Then, someone knocked on the door.

"Come in." He said.

The door opened, and an adult woman of Hawaiian descent walked in.

"Mr. Bryce? I don't want to interrupt you, but we're running low on groceries." She said. "The others and I are busy with the kids, so I'm sorry to ask, but could you—"

"Of course, Angela. I'm happy to help," He responded with a light chuckle, closing the bible, putting it in the shelf, then approaching her. "Do you have a grocery list, or do you need me to write one?"

"Ah, thank you so much, sir." She nodded, handing him a piece of paper. Again, nothing incriminating. It was not a secret message or anything. A simple grocery list, nothing more and nothing less. "Here. It's not much, so it shouldn't take long."

"I was hoping otherwise." He admitted. "My doctor has been telling me I should walk more often, and I've been slacking. Perhaps I should take a detour."

This was something that raised a few flags upon first watch. Both had thought he was going to his base or something, but no. As Bryce left the orphanage, he didn't go anywhere suspicious. He simply took the long way to the supermarket, going around the town.

"You've gotta be fucking kidding me…" Akane whispered to herself.

And when he arrived, he acted like any other civilian. He simply filled his cart with the items he wanted. Vegetables, frozen meat, canned food. Once again, nothing incriminating. He was a human doing human things.

When he had left the supermarket, on his way back to the orphanage, it happened. The ground beneath him began to shake. Asia and Raynare arrived to help, and the sinkhole appeared, swallowing all three.

And that was when the footage was cut off.

Yes, cut off.

It appeared that the Spyder was destroyed in the crossfire.

"…Well, then." Lucifer started, stepping back and grinning. "I suppose you were wrong, after all."

As the veins in her forehead throbbed, Akane bared her teeth and clenched her fists, rage swirling inside her. Lucifer watched, interested and amused at her reaction, knowing full well she didn't believe anything she saw in that footage.

"Bullshit." She growled. "This is fucking bullshit! There's no way I'm wrong!"

"Oh? How so?"

"You're telling me all of this was just a coincidence?!" Akane whipped her head at the Devil God, forgetting who she was talking to. "Are you out of your fucking mind?! There isn't a snowball's chance in hell that he's that lucky! It's insane— He had to have planned this!"

"But you had him recorded this entire time, no?" Lucifer argued. "And the footage showed nothing out of the ordinary."

Truthfully, Lucifer actually agreed with her. This was way too convenient. Things perfectly fell in place just for him to avoid Akane's surveillance through her Spyder. Too perfectly. So, unless he had the luck of the entire universe on his side, he must've known where he was going.

"Because anything out of the ordinary would've already revealed him to us!" Akane said, once again rewinding the footage until he fell into the sinkhole. "He knew he was being tracked. He knew we were watching. This bastard KNEW and figured out a way to get rid of the Spyder. No, not just that. He knew exactly where it was, too."

"And the evidence being?"

She played the footage again, this time frame by frame, up until the Spyder was destroyed.

"Because I installed danger detectors in the Spyders. They would've gone out of harm's way even while on him." She said. "But look at this— The tentacle directly hit the Spyder because he moved his arm right before he got hit. He knew where it was and used Patient Zero's attack to destroy the Spyder before it could move out of the way."

True to her words, from what they could see of the footage, Bryce had seemingly positioned his arm in a way where the tentacle that was going to hit him also took out the Spyder. Less than half a second before the attack actually landed, so the Spyder couldn't reasonably avoid it. Perfectly executed plan.

"All of this… He knew all of this was going to happen. He played me like a fool!" Akane seethed, smashing her fist into the screen. "GODDAMNIT!"

She huffed, backing away from the broken screen. She stared at it with a deep snarl, but then she took a deep breath, trying to calm her nerves as she rubbed her temples.

"What of it?" Lucifer eventually questioned. "I don't quite understand what angers you so. Doesn't this prove his identity?"

"Don't you understand?" She hissed, glaring at Lucifer. "He wasn't just trying to save himself or protect his identity. This bastard is mocking me. He thinks he's better than ME."

'By using my own short-sightedness' was left unsaid. After all, none of this would've happened had she immediately killed Patient Zero. But she was blinded by her own arrogance, high on the souls she devoured, and full of spite for that blue-haired exorcist. All of this led to Bryce falling into that sinkhole and getting the Spyder destroyed in this 'accident'.

This was a mistake of her own making. But it was one she wasn't willing to admit.

Despite that, Lucifer's smirk widened. He found this to be endlessly amusing.

"So it seems~" He chuckled. "And what are you going to do?"

Although still utterly enraged, Akane managed to recompose herself, and with a cold tone, she answered.

"I'm going to make an example out of the Overseer." She swore. "And once I've broken him in mind and spirit, I'll rend his soul in two."

The Devil God couldn't help but quietly laugh.

She truly is the perfect successor.
Writing arrogant edgelords crashing out is fun as fuck
