Edited by: Priapus, Marethyu, Maple



Right after dealing with Dwight, I, as well as everyone else except Magnus, who's still on his part of the investigation, return to the resort to discuss what happened. It was straightforward enough, I suppose. I did leave out the part where I killed Dwight, though. I doubt we'd see him again, and I can easily blame the Palekana for killing him after they 'rescued' him.

I highly doubt anyone would ask about Dwight, anyway. He seemed the sort to be immediately forgotten after death. A nameless NPC mob who thought he was bigger than he actually was.

Glancing at the TV from the corner of my eye, I can't help but grin in mild amusement. 'Terrorist Attack in Crystal Aloha Resort'? Really? Is that the best explanation they could come up with? Well, I guess it happened too suddenly to really define it properly, but I highly doubt anyone would believe this.

Being honest, humanity would be stupid enough. They tend to believe anything they see on TV. Or, well, anything that suits the narrative they've built up in their heads, regardless of the evidence presented in front of them. Any other day, I'd be ashamed to be part of this worthless species, but this implies a problem of self-hatred. A problem someone as great as I doesn't have.

I suppose they do have redeeming qualities, however. After all, ignoring my yokai heritage, they've given me existence, so perhaps humanity does deserve salvation. Perhaps a hand to guide them. A leader they can look up to. A real savior and the subject of their worship. And they'll get one soon enough.

But I digress.

Although there were no casualties and only a few dozen injuries, this and what happened that night with the sinkholes are obvious indications of supernatural activity for those in the know, and that's not good for me right now, because the Yakuza will get involved soon. After all, they can't risk their precious princess getting hurt.

And that's why I'm going to stop them from doing that. I can't let them interfere, not when I'm this close to catching that Bryce bastard and possibly devouring the soul of a god. Even if their support could be invaluable here, I know I don't need it. I don't need them. I've proven my own strength time and time again.

How am I going to stop them, you ask? Simply by changing their priorities from 'Protect Akane' to 'Catch the motherfucker hacking our systems'. I have all the tools I need to pull it off. It's really just a matter of time.

But that's for later. I still have a date to get ready for.

"A man-made mirror realm, huh…" Ichiban hums. "I guess that explains how no one caught him yet. I bet something like that is tough to find."

"Try impossible," Irina says with a resigned sigh. "I mean, mirror realms aren't like dimensions like the Underworld or something. They're really complicated to locate. Like a needle in a haystack, except the haystack is the size of infinity."

"Still, it's a step in the right direction," Issei replies. "We know where he isn't right now."

"Does that even help?" Irina mumbles, not confident in our odds.

"Of course it does," I respond. "Because right now, all we have to do is trick him into opening another portal there."

Because, as I've proven already, I can open doorways between dimensions. If one of my Spyders or even Bronze Spheres manages to enter that mirror realm, then we practically win. Yes, these people don't know I actually have a whole portal machine working, but they don't have to.

I can simply make another machine, maybe a dimension breacher rather than an actual portal maker. It shouldn't be too hard to build, nor should it take too much time with Nemesis' assistance. A couple of hours, maybe. If not, then perhaps a way to help either Koneko or Kiba cast a teleportation spell directly to wherever that realm is.

That's how terrible my portal machine is in hindsight. Simple demonic spells can replicate anything that machine can do. Then again, it always was a placeholder until I got my hands on that devil chick's portal magic. Instantaneous, doesn't need stupid magic circles, can be used in combat. That's the real deal.

"Simply analyzing the portal will get us to wherever he's hiding," I add before Irina can bring down the mood with her shitty attitude. "We didn't win the battle this time, yeah, but as long as he doesn't find Lani before we find him, then we win the war."

And while I couldn't get Dwight's soul, I killed him and got some EXP. Still frustrating as fuck, but I'll take the little wins where I can get them. Eventually, they add up.

"I guess…" Irina mumbles, making me frown.

What the hell is wrong with her? Why is she being such a downer? Doesn't she understand that we're pretty much winning right now?

"What's wrong?" I feel curious enough to ask. "What are you so concerned about?"

Irina hesitates for a split second before answering.

"I don't know, don't you think that things have been a little too easy?" She says. "The Barracuda roping you into this in the first place, Yamai randomly showing up to attack you, everything with Dwight and the Black Market— all of it has been conveniently going our way."

I wait for her to finish.

"Yamai told us that he has a way to somehow see and predict everything we do and plan, and sure, Yamai might just be easy to figure out, but what if that's not the case? What if the Overseer has some sort of power that lets him do these things?" She continues. "What if all this was him lulling us into a false sense of security, and then, when we least expect it, dupe us and get away with what he's doing?"

Irina's suggestion somewhat resonates with the rest of the group, as I can almost sense their confidence dwindling the longer they think about it. Me? Oh, I pretty much knew this a while ago. I'm honestly a little impressed by Irina. I didn't expect her to notice it either.

It's easy to ignore these things when it genuinely feels like you're getting closer and closer to your goal. It makes you short-sighted, and short-sightedness makes you very easy to manipulate.

…I know this firsthand.

"Hold on, even if that's the case, how is that going to help him?" Ichi is the first to argue. "He wants Lani, not us, and we're here to stop him."

"He's hoping we find her for him," I explain, drawing everyone's attention. "With the Bronze Spheres scouring all of Hawaii, it's only a matter of time before we find her, and the moment we do, he gets what he wants."

"Then you've noticed it too, haven't you?" Irina asks.

"Of course I have." I scoff. I noticed way more than just that. "I know we're walking straight into a trap."

She blinks as the rest look at me in confusion.

"What do you mean?"

"He wants Lani because whatever she has, it can be used to revive his goddess. She's essential to his goals," I remind them. "And he knows that we're his best chance at finding her. We have the resources and means to do so, while he's stuck in Honolulu in fear of attracting the wrong crowd."

i.e., factions that can wipe him out in seconds. He's nigh-invincible in his turf, but not outside of it.

"The moment we find her, I can guarantee you that all this secrecy and tip-toeing bullshit he's doing will immediately stop. He won't rest until he gets her hands on her, even if that means torching Honolulu to the ground." I add. "But that's where he fucks up, because the Overseer has no idea who he's messing with."

"How?" Irina questions. "If he gets Lani, doesn't he win?"

"That's true, but who told you we're just going to let him do that?" I respond with a grin. "He's going to try as hard as he can to get her, and eventually, he will slip, and that's exactly our time to strike."

With whatever possible clairvoyance spell he's using to see me specifically blocked off by my bond with Excelsis, Bryce is most likely very cautious around me. However, he still doesn't know what I'm really planning, and neither will any of my friends, because that's just a window into my mind, and I can't have that. Plus, by peering into their minds, he'd be fed false information, which gives me the advantage.

Even if it's the actual future he's seeing, my fate, therefore, what I intend on doing, remains concealed. Would that also be enough to indirectly hide the fates of everyone else as a side effect? Maybe, maybe not. It's still a risk, but at this point, it's my best chance.

At the same time, wherever Lani is, she's outside of his range, so when I find Lani, I'll have secured a way to his realm, because Lani is my Trojan Horse. When Bryce catches her, she'll have several Spyders on her that will immediately scatter when they've infiltrated the mirror realm. Through them, I'll very easily locate the dimension he's hiding in.

Letting her get caught by Bryce has another purpose since she has what he needs to revive Pele. Something tells me it runs the risk of Lani losing her life, but that's a risk I'd gladly take. Politically, she's a nobody, and to me, her worth is nothing more than a speck of dirt.

Her death serves a grander purpose, so really, she should be honored.

"So far, none of his little minions posed a threat to any of us, so it's safe to assume that we're far more powerful than anything he could throw our way." I continue. Not counting Pele. "So as long as we stay around Lani, then it's doubtful he could even lay a finger on her."

"I don't know…" Irina remains unconvinced. "I still don't like this."

My smile drops as I grow tired of her demoralizing attitude.

"Oh, I'm sorry my idea isn't to your liking," I ask with a sharp tone. "Do you have a plan?"

"N-not really…" She replies with a wince, detecting my frustration.

"Then why the hell are you questioning me?" I snap. "If you're going to shit over anything I suggest, you better have an alternative. Otherwise, shut the fuck up, you patronizing bitch."

Irina's eyes widen, startled at my venomous response. Everyone else looks equally surprised, seemingly unsure where this was coming from. They shouldn't be. She's being annoying.

"Woah, calm down." Ichi is the first to speak. "That's a bit too much, Akane. What the hell was that about? Irina's just understandably concerned."

"Concerned is one thing, but she's plain unhelpful," I argue. "Her criticism doesn't even amount to anything beyond 'feeling bad.' How the hell is this going to help any of us?"

"Even then, at the very least, that's not how you should talk to someone who is only worried about the innocent lives at stake." He remains firm. "Telling her off just because she's not sure about what we're doing is not necessary."

"So, what? I should comfort her? Get real. If she has zero faith in herself or those around her, then she should put down the sword and stay here until we handle this." I scoff. "I don't want an indecisive crybaby dragging us down because her tummy felt bad."

With tears gathering in the corner of her eyes, Irina looks down and away from me but remains quiet.

"How dare you talk to Irina like that?!" Xenovia scowls at me, standing up all of a sudden. "Whether we agreed to follow your orders or not, you're in no position to treat her or anyone else here badly!"

"Follow my orders? You idiots can't even keep your worthless opinions to yourselves." I sneer. "Everything I say and tell you to do just has to be met with a retort, and I'm frankly getting really sick of you."

Xenovia bares her teeth at me as her hand hovers over her sword, but doesn't do anything else, because both of us know how this would end. If she tries drawing her little stick, she loses her hand.

"Akane!" Asia snaps at me, looking uncharacteristically upset.

"I wish you even had something smart to say. All I ever hear from you morons is pointless and asinine jabbering by someone who can barely function outside of hitting something with a sword," My stare sharply switches to Irina. "And a defeatist who would rather stay here with her thumbs shoved firmly up her ass than do anything else."

"That's enough!" Ichiban yells, becoming increasingly annoyed. "Knock it off!"

Instead of tripling down, I hold my tongue out of regard for the only one here who even deserves my respect. I cross my arms and keep my glare on the two exorcists. The blue idiot looks at me with an expression of anger and, surprisingly, mild distress, while Irina avoids eye contact entirely.

The tension grows heavier by the second until, eventually, Xenovia's scowl drops as she glances at Irina before quickly switching back to me. Although still enraged by my insults, she holds almost impressive control over her emotions as her sword arm drops to her side.

"I see. If that's how you feel." Xenovia says. "I suppose I was wrong about you. Come on, Irina. We're going."

As the blue idiot helps up her mildly confused partner, I raise an eyebrow, admittedly feeling curious enough to ask.

"Wrong about me?" I mutter in askance, tilting my head to the side. "What's that supposed to mean?"

Xenovia visibly pauses before answering.

"I thought you were more reasonable. That's all." She says. "Someone with your incredible skill, great courage, and excellent leadership— you made me think you were someone I could admire."

I frown, but don't say anything as she continues.

"Those traits made me blind to who you truly are. There were signs, but I ignored them." She adds. "Because how could that be when you surround yourself by wonderful people? It didn't make sense."

"Get to the point." I roll my eyes.

Xenovia looks at me directly, fearless as the day I met her.

"You're really nothing but a bully and a narcissist." She claims. "You tend to joke about it, but you do think you're always right. Someone who is above criticism. You believe Irina and I are beneath you. That's why you treat us this way."

I remain quiet.

"I can't work with or for someone like you." Xenovia's eyes narrow as her hand over Irina tightens. "And I certainly won't allow such disrespect for my partner to slide, so we're taking our leave."

"But—" Issei starts, trying to stop them.

"This decision is final." Xenovia cuts him off. "We're grateful for everything you've done for us, but we will tolerate this no longer."

She drags her partner toward the front door, as no one else tries to stop them, either respecting her decision or lacking the courage to do so. As Xenovia stops by the front door, she looks back at us and says her goodbyes.

"Take care."

And with that, the massive pain in my ass finally leaves me the fuck alone. God, I should've done this a long time ago. Can't believe telling her what I actually thought would be enough to get her to piss off. I should be more honest more often.

"Alright, back to what we're talking about—"

I'm immediately interrupted by Issei slamming his hands on the table and glaring at me for some reason.

"What's wrong with you?!" He raises his voice at me. Oh wow, that's a first. "Why would you say that to them?!"

"Say what? The truth?" I raise an eyebrow, unfazed by whatever tantrum he's throwing.

"The truth?!" He looks at me like I said something crazy. "Calling them worthless and idiots— that's not truthful at all! You're just being a bitch!"

"Watch your fucking tone, Issei," I scowl, the air becoming several degrees colder. Who the hell does this moron think he is? "Unless you want to be thrown out with them, you'd keep it to yourself."

"What's gotten into you?!" Asia calls out, utterly shocked and appalled. "Why are you suddenly so mean?! Irina was just worried and— and you just said all those terrible things about them!"

"Jerk," Koneko mumbled under her breath.

Kiba is the only one who says nothing, but even he looks conflicted.

What's going on? I glance at Ichiban for some support, and he gives me a disappointed stare that hurts a lot more than I'd like to admit.

"I get that you might be frustrated with them," He says. "But that was really uncalled for, you know?"

What the hell is happening? Why am I the bad guy all of a sudden? Yes, I was mean, but how the hell is this my fault when that defeatist bitch decided to get all uppity with me? I addressed her concerns, and she was still all mopey about it. Either she had something worth saying, or she stayed quiet.

But I'm the one in the wrong?

Overwhelming fury begins to bubble in my chest as I get up from my seat. On the verge of blowing up and accidentally freezing the entire private resort, I bare my teeth and clench my fists, just barely containing it.

"Why the hell are all of you taking their side?!" I roar. "What's wrong with you all?!"

"Nothing's wrong with us, Akane," Ichi replies firmly, not intimidated in the least. "We're saying you just went off on them for literally no reason."

"But—"

"I understand that it's annoying when others aren't being helpful, but Irina didn't do anything wrong by making her concerns known." He explains. "You realize what's at stake here, right?"

"I literally addressed said concerns, but that wasn't enough for her either," I argue with a hiss, reminding him how bitchmade she was. "My idea not being good enough for her is one thing, but she had nothing planned!"

"And that made you resort to name-calling?!" He snaps, becoming more annoyed. "All you had to do was shrug your shoulders and leave it there. It was that easy to avoid a confrontation and let two of our friends walk away!"

"I—"

"Instead, you thought you'd kick the 'defeatist' down even more. And for what?" Ichi adds. "When did that ever help?"

I say nothing. Seeing this, Ichiban visibly relaxes.

"I know 'being mean' is your thing. I know you never mean most of the things you say, but I just don't understand why you'd do something like that." He says, his tone a lot softer. "That wasn't like you at all."

My closed fists tighten even more as I lower my head, just barely containing my fury. I can feel my heart beating faster and faster, my throat closing up uncomfortably while I do my absolute damndest not to lose control.

That's fucking precious. 'Not like me,' he says, as if he knows who I really am. But what does he know beyond this fake little persona I put on for him? This blissful ignorance of his— I used to think it was funny and adorable at first. But now, hearing him so confident about himself as he fucking dares to admonish me when I did nothing wrong?

It makes me so sick I want to puke. It makes me want to show him who I am and how wrong he is. It makes me want to see this hero wannabe feel so disgusted with himself for associating with someone as truly evil and irredeemable as me.

Seeing him staring at me like that makes me want to break him by showing that everything between us is built on a lie I maintain for HIS sake.

But I know I shouldn't do that.

My hands relax as I manage to calm my overwhelming rage just enough for my rationality to make my decisions for me. I exhale and break eye contact, looking away.

…I can't do that.

"Akane," Ichi says my name, his earlier annoyance turning into concern as he puts a hand on my shoulder. "If there's anything wrong—"

"Don't touch me." I shove him off me as I walk away. "I've got things to do, and I want none of you to bother me."

I exit the main building and, after rubbing my eyes, I walk toward the outside shed. I close the door behind me and lock it, then hop into the teleporter and arrive at my secret hideout in an instant.

Moments later, Lucifer materializes near me.

"…Seems you've gotten yourself in an unexpected dilemma." He says after a while as I pick up the blowtorch. "Would you like to talk about it?"

"No," I respond curtly.

"As you wish." Lucifer leaves it there.

…

…Ridiculous.





– Lucifer –

Observing his potential successor tinkering with what clearly looked like a suit of armor, Lucifer's gaze lingered on her back as he wondered whether he should pity her after witnessing such an unsightly reaction or feel disgusted for trying to pretend to be something she was not.

Naturally, Lucifer did not care for those two exorcists and considered them utterly useless. Although crass and excessively confrontational, Akane's words rang true, and he fully agreed with her. They offered nothing of value beyond their status as meatshields, and it made no marginal difference whether they stayed or left.

At the same time, it was an utterly pointless argument, serving no purpose. Causing tension between your allies for… what, exactly?

And that was what Lucifer found utterly pitiful and somewhat even humorous. It was why she felt the need to start an altercation. After all, her one-sided battle with Dwight wasn't enough— she needed something else to massage her fragile ego. And with her less-than-favorable view of the two exorcists, they felt like very acceptable targets.

Blinded by her own rage after what she perceived as humiliation by the Overseer, and unable to see just how short-sighted she was, all culminated in her doing what she could to reaffirm her self-importance. The funniest thing about this? Her complete and utter ignorance of how she would be viewed by her allies and friends after doing such a thing.

She expected them to applaud and take her side, but why should they? Even ignoring their seemingly more humane reasons for opposing her, Akane had, in practical terms, driven away two allies because one of them dared to question her. Like some despot drunk on her own power.

What disgusted him was what had happened afterward. The accusations and hurt feelings. How juvenile. Such a human way to react, but Lucifer always had to remind himself that she was human, and no matter how she pretended to be otherwise, that didn't change.

Not yet. He thought as his glance flickered to the armor. But perhaps sooner than later.

"This suit of armor you're building…" Lucifer eventually stated. "It seems remarkably similar to the one you're building for Nemesis to pilot."

With the black and red theme she had chosen, it was a suit of armor that matched the cloaking gauntlet. A sleek and elegant-looking design that covered the whole body, and although the armor didn't look very different from what she had designed for her AI assistant, its most unique feature was the jagged-looking mask. Three thin, red visor rows that were divided in the middle, resembling three pairs of eyes. Almost made with the intent to intimidate, rather than protect.

In contrast, the helmet she'd built for Nemesis was more practical, covering the whole head with a simple, large black visor.

Though I suppose the helmet is the head in that case. He thought to himself.

"With the resources I have right now, I can't afford an upgrade. But I won't settle for an inferior product, either." She replied. "Besides, I have a theme, and I intend on keeping it."

"Fair enough, I suppose." He hummed. "I imagine you'll leave room to improve it once you've made your breakthrough with the Agreasite crystals?"

"Obviously," Akane said. "I wouldn't call this a prototype. More like the foundation for my perfect weapon. Aside from Nemesis."

Lucifer waited for her to finish.

"With every tool and armor I make, I get better at creating things. I haven't hit a wall yet, and I don't see one getting in my way any time soon." She continued, putting her tools down and stepping back. "Eventually, this thing will be unstoppable. No devil or god would be able to put a dent in it."

"And what about now?"

"Now, it's just a glorified costume." She sighed. "The alloys I used for it are of excellent quality, but without a proper energy core, it can't even go past 1% of its real power. Still, this is more than enough for now."

He watched as she took her gauntlet and put it on. Akane pressed a few buttons, prompting the suit of armor to open up. For a moment, he expected her to inspect the armor's insides, but instead, she got inside as it closed around her. Akane picked up the mask on the table and put it on before it created a holographic hood over her head.

"Ah…" Lucifer smiled as realization hit him. "I see. So it's time, then?"

He didn't think she would do this so early. From what he remembered, Akane was planning to make her grand reveal after her little date with the dragon boy.

I suppose that's delayed, then. He thought in amusement.

"I'd rather not waste any time." She said. "Not when I'm ready."

"And what of your friends?" He reminded her as she opened a portal to Japan. "Are you not worried they might try to approach you?"

"I made it clear to them that I don't want to be bothered. And I locked the door." She replied, referring to the shed within the resort's parameters as she activated the cloaking device. "But even if any of them tries to, I have Nemesis there to handle it. He has my voice."

"I see." He dropped it there. "Then I suppose all I can do now is wish you good luck."

"I don't need luck." She scoffed playfully as she stepped through the portal. "I'm beyond that."

"So you are." Lucifer chuckled. "Do be careful, Empyrean~"

Once the portal closed behind her, Akane leaped from building to building, stealthily making her way to the main headquarters of the Tojo clan. Lucifer still found this incredibly delightful. To turn on her own allies so readily… it was entertaining to watch.

She truly was deplorable. Irredeemable. And she knew that as well.

…But she was still human, as much as she wanted to deny it.

Because real monsters were ready to cast everything away for the sake of their ambitions.

Akane was not.

But as what had already been established, she had the potential to be the same monster he was. No, even more than that. Perhaps months, years, or decades later, Lucifer knew that if the circumstances were just right, she could not only keep the devil god's legacy alive…

She might very well surpass him.

And Lucifer could hardly wait.




– Daigo –

Just when things had started to calm down, just when he'd thought he could keep his guard down and relax for a little while, some shit just had to happen. At this point, Daigo was starting to think rest wasn't on the table until Christmas. Because, believe it or not, a lot of factions, terroristic or otherwise, respected that holiday in particular. Some unwritten rule where none may cause trouble until after New Year's Eve.

But December was a long way off, and the days had started to feel longer and longer. There wasn't much he could do but push on until then. When would it end, he wondered? Not long ago, the peace conference was the most stressful thing he had prepared for in a while, and now?

First, it was the strange white-haired child that Akiyama had told them to keep an eye out for. Then whoever it was that had decided to wipe out random gangs in their territory, apparently having 'successfully guessed' that God was dead, and now, some random and obviously supernaturally-motivated attacks in Hawaii. The place where Tatsu's girl had decided to spend her summer vacation.

Really, sinkholes randomly appearing in Honolulu, then the most prominent hotel randomly getting blown up? He wasn't an idiot. That definitely was not a coincidence. What was a coincidence, however, was that Akane somehow, someway, most likely got involved in whatever that was. Because of course, she was. A trouble magnet, just like her father.

Daigo would've honestly found it really funny if it wasn't so incredibly stressful. Confident in her power as he may be, he also knew that the girl was just as headstrong as Tatsu and might wind up in too much trouble, where even they could not bail her out. If that were to happen…

Well, he would rather not think about it.

Thankfully, the solution to that problem was simple enough. As long as he sent someone to stay around the girl and keep her safe in case shit hit the fan, then it'd be highly unlikely she'd get hurt. Again, Akane was monstrously strong and could easily take care of herself if things came down to it, but why risk it?

He had many a strong yakuza standing around not doing anything in Japan, and some tended to get irritable when there was nothing to do, so Daigo might as well send them off to blow off some steam. While that's happening, the rest could figure out what was going on with this terrorist showing up.

Because something told Daigo that whoever this person was, he wasn't a delusional madman spouting nonsense.

"That is rather concerning," Sirzechs said as he, Daigo, and Azazel were on a call. "But are we certain that they know?"

"It's a possibility." Daigo nodded. "They haven't attacked directly yet, but they've proven that they're more than efficient enough to pose a threat."

"Moreover, the timing is undeniable," Azazel added, looking uncharacteristically serious. "Right after the conference, an attack in Japan where said conference took place."

"Are you saying they've somehow managed to eavesdrop on us?" Sirzechs questioned.

"Yes, that's what I believe as well." Daigo agreed with the Grigori leader. "Either that, or there's a mole."

But if that's the case, that mole must be a yakuza or a yokai. The three biblical factions had kept the knowledge of god's death concealed for centuries, only for some random psychopath to go painting it on the walls at the same moment the yakuza had the information and were begged to keep it a secret? This reflected poorly on them.

"This is troubling news," Sirzechs said. "If this terrorist truly knew about his death, then they could do untold harm."

"I doubt that they'll be taken seriously by other factions. As threatening as they may seem on the surface, they've done nothing to warrant it. Efficient, yes. A reliable source of information? I don't think so." Daigo said. "I'll run a thorough investigation here and see if we do have a mole on our hands."

"Please do, Daigo-san." The Satan Lucifer urged. "We can't let someone like that gain notoriety and earn support from our enemies."

Daigo's gaze flickered toward Azazel, who had a thoughtful expression on his face.

"Azazel-san?" The Tojo Clan chairman called. "Is something wrong?"

"…It just feels like we're missing something here. Something important." He admitted. "But for the life of me, I can't figure it out."

"Missing something?" Daigo parroted. "Could you explain?"

But before he could, the call suddenly froze. His and Sirzechs' faces contorted while their voices kept getting cut off, almost as if the internet suddenly stopped working properly. Daigo blinked, wondering if the site was the problem until the lights in his office kept flickering.

His monitor went black as his computer shut down on its own. Daigo frowned and got off his chair, backing away from his computer as the lights kept flickering on and off. As he pulled out his phone and went to make a call, he realized it had stopped working as well. The screen was completely black.

Until three pairs of glowing red lines appeared with the sentence 'God is Dead' below them.

"What the hell…?" Daigo muttered to himself.

Moments later, the door of his office burst open as a panicking yakuza walked in.

"Chairman!" He cried out. "Our systems have been compromised!"

"By who?"

"I-I don't know!" He replied. "But our cameras caught something on the roof before they were shut off!"

Daigo nodded and ran past his subordinate. He, alongside several yakuza, quickly headed toward the exit. He spotted Mine walking beside him, and on their way, they exchanged a few words.

"What's the situation?" Daigo asked.

"Seems the bastard is a lot bolder than we gave them credit for." His captain answered. "Attacking us directly like this— either they have a death wish—"

"Or their confidence is well-earned," Saejima said as he caught up with them. "If they can easily compromise all our systems like this, then they ain't a joke."

"Amon?" Mine wondered out loud.

"I… I'm not sure." Daigo shook his head. "Out of everything I've heard about them from Mizuki-san, this doesn't seem like the way Amon operates at all."

His closest confidants remained quiet; once they left the building, they turned around and saw them. In a dark, tattered cloak over black and red armor, the terrorist stood tall above the main Tojo Clan building, staring down at them behind their mask.

Daigo couldn't sense their presence directly— he couldn't tell if they were even human or otherwise, but there was this… pressure they exuded that brought a sense of dread he wasn't used to feeling. Something told him this individual wasn't normal in the least.

Even as hundreds of yakuza surrounded them with their guns aimed their way, the individual remained unfazed, keeping their gaze on Daigo, Mine, and Saejima. The White Tiger activated his Sacred Gear, but Daigo quickly put an arm out, silently ordering him to stand down. Not yet.

Whoever this was, Daigo should at least know their motives before attacking.

"Who are you?" He called out. "And what do you want from us?"

The stranger shifted their position, and Daigo felt their gaze piercing his soul.

"You stand before the true savior and salvation of mankind." They said, speaking in perfect English. "And I've come to deliver one final warning to the wicked."

"A warning?" Daigo narrowed his eyes, understanding them well enough.

"Hear my voice and tremble in fear, you who have called yourselves the bastion of humanity." They boomed in a deep, guttural voice, throwing their arms. "Your choice to side with those who treat you like cattle over your own is treason. Your continued aid to those who call themselves holy yet preserve a lie to save their own hides speaks volumes about your cowardice. Your inaction to the kind who nearly started a war on your soil makes you unfit to be the protectors you claim to be."

That settles it… Daigo thought. They know.

This was far more specific than some madman's delusions. Either it was a mole, or someone had infiltrated and spied on the conference. And something told Daigo it was the latter. Not even their developmental tech could do what this person's tools have done.

"You've been corrupted. Taken over by the filth that has continued to violate the sanctity of our beautiful world time and time again." They continued their speech. "And I refuse to stand by and let this go on any longer."

Once again, Daigo said nothing as he, Saejima, and Mine waited for an opportunity to catch them by surprise.

"I am Empyrean! And I swear to cleanse this world of those who desire to defile it!" They promised. "You will join me on my righteous crusade against the enemies of humanity, or you will stand beside evil and be crushed beneath boots!"

Saejima's gaze met Daigo's as the two knew this speech of theirs was nearing its end.

"You have been warned," Empyrean said. "May you see the light before you meet your end by my hands."

"Now!" Daigo ordered, prompting Saejima to act.

With a roar, the White Tiger unleashed an immensely powerful gust of wind that would surely tear apart a mountain with utter ease. Empyrean did not attempt to dodge or block the attack and simply stood there as the fierce wind harmlessly passed through them, making Daigo's eyes widen.

"The hell?!" Even Saejima was surprised.

"Farewell," Empyrean said before disappearing.

"It's a hologram!" Mine concluded, then turned to the countless yakuza surrounding the building. "The real one could still be around here. Look for them!"

The troops obeyed, surveying the parameters in search of this 'Empyrean'. Daigo didn't know if they were some bastard with delusions of grandeur, an idiot who had no idea what they were talking about, or a fool who wanted an excuse to start a fight.

But what he did know was that they were a terrorist who knew too much and should be taken down as soon as possible.

…Daigo had a terrible feeling about this.




– Akane –

Watching the Yakuza running around like headless chickens looking for me, I can't help but laugh quietly. So much for the technological juggernauts of the world. Tricking them was as easy as taking candy from a baby.

I can maybe forgive their bafflingly shitty defenses, seeing that they didn't expect the so-called random terrorist to compromise their entire systems with the same effort it would take to yawn, but that's exactly why I'd rather not be associated with them forever. Ultimately, they're a liability, and I've proven my superiority.

I inspect the USB stick between my fingers, my smile growing wider. While they were distracted by the hologram delivering its speech, I slipped in and headed straight to their data centers, killing and devouring the souls of the yakuza who stood in the way. You know, as a little treat to have while on the job. Also made sure to store the corpses in my inventory. Y'know, to clean up after me.

I try to be a good member of society.

Now, why exactly did I do this when I could've probably had Nemesis scrape their date without me ever having to get close? Well, I weighed the pros and cons of both methods and decided my approach was more thorough. Plus, significantly more frightening to them. While also VERY fun for me.

First, as much as I hate to admit it, actually hacking their database was surprisingly a lot more difficult than I thought. They had impressive security systems I did not expect, given they're the only faction, aside from the Amon, that primarily works with technology. I mean, why would they need that when most factions can barely operate a regular computer?

I'm guessing their security systems were actually recent, though. Despite its strength, I did notice a few weaknesses that Nemesis and I could easily exploit. It is a risk because I wasn't sure I could actually squeeze their database for all it was worth before I was kicked out.

So I went with a more direct method. First, a special device similar to an EMP bomb that only temporarily disabled their technology. Then the hologram tech I positioned up there, created by nearly microscopic drones, and finally a simple USB stick of my own making that can hold the entire internet in bytes as of 2018.

Said USB drive contained Nemesis, and once I plugged it into one of the ports, my wonderful AI assistant took just over a minute to get everything. I was tempted to then destroy everything just for the hell of it, but that seemed a bit counterproductive. Inferior or not, they're still my allies.

I did, however, leave a little present there. A malware that will delete every single file and brick their systems permanently. It's dormant, though, and will only activate whenever I desire. So once they've outlived their usefulness to me, then bye-bye, Tojo Clan. I almost feel sad for doing this. After all, they pretty much raised and nurtured my father, and I bet he wouldn't approve.

Too bad he's dead, huh?

Giving the scrambling yakuza one last look, I turn away as a portal leading to my base opens up. I go through it, take off my mask, and exhale lightly. My armor then opens up, prompting me to get out of it, feeling like a million dollars. Mission accomplished~

"See?" I glance at the amused Devil God as I sit on my chair. "Told you it was gonna be easy~"

"To be quite honest, I wasn't sure what you did back there." He says, a hand on his chin.

"You don't have to worry about that." I wave it off and show him the USB stick. "What you have to know is that I've got everything I need and more right here."

I plug the stick into my computer as it automatically downloads everything.

"And I can't wait to see what's in there," I add with an excited giggle. "Oh, this is going to be so good. Nemesis, open up the blueprint files for the generators the Tojo Clan uses."

Without my having to do anything, the desired files open, revealing the blueprint. A detailed guide explaining exactly how and what the generators are. What sort of coding language they use, what script makes them work, and even their terminology.

"Huh. They call it Radiant Energy?" I hum. "RE for short. Doesn't sound very catchy…"

Not like that matters, because I can use this as the base for my own energy, and mine is going to be the perfected version of whatever the hell this is. Their amateurish method of creating a fully tech-based magical power. Credit where credit's due, though. They did invent it and gave me the inspiration to invent something even better.

Because, unlike them, I'm using Agreasite for it. And I'm also a vastly better engineer.

"Do you believe it is possible now?" Lucifer asks.

"Yes." I nod, reading the blueprint. "It's very doable. I was just going about it the wrong way."

"How so?"

I pause and glance at Lucy. I doubt he'd understand half of what I'm going to say…

"Well, to make a long and complicated story short…" I reply, simplifying it. "The scripts I used acted closer to banging two rocks together over an empty campsite, hoping the sparks would catch it on fire."

Lucy hums.

"Whenever Agreasite crystals lit up during my experiments, they would immediately lose power, but that's because in my method, there were no 'shavings' for the 'sparks' to get a campfire going," I add, pointing at the screen. "This explains how to apply these shavings. However, unlike a campfire, it keeps the generator in a nigh-endless feedback loop, thus creating a usable power source."

"Fascinating…"

"Very fascinating." I nod in agreement. "The main issue is how restricted their generators are. Its output has a hard limit that it can't go past, no matter what."

"And you're certain this will work with the Agreasite crystals?" He questions.

"It should. Probably even better than what they have." I reply with a smile. "Besides, now that I know how it works, I can provide even better scripts. Their 'Radiant Energy' would be nothing compared to what I can make."

If a tiny generator made with worse qualities was that strong, then just what the hell will the Agreasite be capable of once a proper genius engineer refines it into a power core? Holy shit, I can't wait. I really want to—

My train of thought is quickly interrupted as Nemesis suddenly warns me.

"Alert: Ichiban Kasuga is approaching the Teleporter Zone."

The AI follows up by bringing up the video feed of the hidden cameras I installed on the shed, showing Ichi walking toward it. My smile switches to an annoyed frown, and while I'm still pissed at him for taking their side, I feel a little… anxious? Glad? It's a weird emotion I'm not very used to.

I almost order Nemesis to take care of it by using my voice to tell him to fuck off, but I hesitate and think about it longer. I don't want to see him after he turned on me like that, but…

…Well, it's good that he'd chosen now to bother me and not when I was busy. I might as well go check and see what he wants.

"…Right…"

Lucy says nothing, but I can almost feel him judging me behind that neutral look on his face as I step into the teleporter. I don't know what he's thinking, but having to go through this in front of him feels humiliating.

I seriously hate being human.
We're drawing ever closer to the end of part 1 of this fic. Yes, this fic is separated into two parts.

– Ichiban –

Lying on his bed, he stared at the ceiling, thinking back on what had transpired during their meeting. Things sort of happened way too quickly. He was still trying to understand why it went the way it did, and Ichi couldn't help but blame himself a little for not de-escalating the situation when he probably could've.

Not to say he was at fault. Ichiban knew that wasn't the case, and it was his girlfriend who had become aggressive out of nowhere. Sure, Akane was always pretty damn aggressive, but it was the kind that made her fierce, assertive, and bold without ever making her outright malicious. Those traits Ichi found very attractive.

Whatever that was, it wasn't the Akane he knew. What was worse was that it came out of left field and left them all too stunned to temper the growing tensions between her and the two exorcists. Now, Ichi was fully aware that his girlfriend did not like Xenovia by any means, and could see her doing or saying something like that to her, but as far as he was concerned, Irina was blameless.

Akane seemed to enjoy her company, even. Why she would suddenly turn on Irina like that left Ichiban utterly bewildered. Did something happen in between them that he didn't know about? Perhaps during their raid on the underground black market? It didn't feel like it. They all came out of it looking ultimately victorious, ignoring their injuries.

Well, Xenovia did seem upset, but that was it. Irina was much more concerned about Issei getting hurt and was relieved when he recovered. So this still didn't explain his girlfriend's random hostility.

In a way, Ichi understood where she was coming from. Having her plans doubted and criticized despite her proving herself time and time again must be incredibly frustrating, especially when the one criticizing her wasn't offering any better alternatives, but it definitely didn't warrant that reaction. Resorting to petty and personal attacks over something like that was childish.

…Then again, Akane was sort of childish, wasn't she?

Ichiban loved his girlfriend with all his heart, but he wasn't blind to the flaws she would probably insist didn't exist. While he was sure she mostly joked around, he knew that she did think a bit too highly of herself. She was arrogant and had an enormous ego, and sometimes it got in the way of her being honest with others and even with herself.

And that's precisely why Ichi knew that something was bothering her.

Before this incident, Akane had had these brief moments when she suddenly looked uncharacteristically serious. With a scary-looking frown on her face, she would be deep in thought while coldly calculating every move she would make. It was always unsettling to see it, as if she were devoid of all emotion, but, as Ichiban came to understand, it meant she was either anxious or upset. Possibly both.

Akane almost always masked it with her usual overconfident demeanor, so nobody really noticed anything wrong with her, but Ichi had spent a lot of time around his girlfriend and had learned to pick up on these cues relatively quickly. Even before they'd started dating.

It was as Koneko said, too. Akane was someone who kept her true feelings to herself and never wore them on her sleeve. So he knew that her overly confrontational reaction was a symptom of a bigger problem. It didn't feel like something she would do because it wasn't.

Maybe this whole thing was affecting her a lot more than we thought. Ichiban frowned. And none of us noticed it.

This was the only explanation that made sense, and it was why he felt bad about it. Had he seen the signs earlier, this wouldn't have happened.

And I just promised Mizuki-san to take care of her. He sighed. Way to go, proving her wrong. Great boyfriend material, you are.

But this wasn't the time to kick himself down. Now that he had noticed the problem, he needed to fix it.

'Scold her when she does something wrong', huh? He thought, remembering what Mizuki asked of him.

First, he had to check up on her. The scolding could come afterward.

He glanced at the digital clock on the nightstand next to the bed, noticing it had been about two hours since the incident, then promptly got out of bed and left the room. That should be enough time for her to cool off, right?

He closed the door behind him and walked toward the exit when Asia, who was alone in the living room, noticed him and approached.

"Where are you going, Ichi?" She asked.

"Gonna go check up on Akane." He told her as he opened the front door.

"I see." She breathed a sigh of relief, making him blink. "I thought you were going to leave like Issei."

"Issei left?"

"Yes." She nodded. "He said he was going after Irina and Xenovia, but he didn't say if he was coming back. I'm a little worried about him…"

Ichi remained silent for a few moments before replying.

"I doubt he's leaving leaving." He reassured her with a smile. "Knowing him, he's probably gonna try to convince them to come back."

"I hope so," Asia said. "May I come with you? I want to see if Akane is okay, too."

"I don't think that's a good idea, Asia." He responded, being honest. "After what happened, we don't want to overwhelm her. Let me talk to her alone first, alright?"

At first, Asia wanted to argue, but quickly relented with a sigh.

"Alright."

He gave her a nod of appreciation before leaving the building, walking toward the shed Akane called a 'makeshift workshop.' Tinkering with her machinery in their bedroom was a bit too loud for Ichiban to get any sleep, and she liked working in the middle of the night for whatever reason, so she moved her stuff over there.

Truthfully, Ichiban didn't know what he was supposed to say, assuming she gave him the time of day, but he would probably figure it out. Hopefully, she did calm down enough to have a proper discussion about what happened back then rather than turning it into a shouting match. Anger issues or not, Akane was pretty reasonable most of the time.

Strangely, he didn't hear anything inside the shed. He expected the loud whirring of an electric screwdriver or the hammering of nails, but it was eerily quiet. Still, that didn't deter Ichiban, who knocked on the door.

"Akane, it's me." He said.

No response, and after a while of standing still waiting for it, he tried to open the door himself to no avail. She'd left it locked, and Ichiban took this as a sign to give her more space. Clearly, she wasn't in the mood, and he couldn't force her to talk to him. Not when she'd actually teared up after he chastised her the first time.

But then, as he was turning around to leave, the door unlocked and slowly creaked open, with his girlfriend peeking out of it. Despite her cold glare that would surely intimidate anyone else, Ichiban couldn't help but think it made her look endearing in a weird way. She looked like a cat that was deeply annoyed.

That thought passing through his mind made it hard not to crack a smile and piss her off even more.

"I told you I didn't want to be bothered." She said harshly. "What do you want?"

"I just want to talk." He replied, raising his hands.

He saw her visibly contemplating whether to listen to him or tell him to shove it, and thankfully, she chose the former, fully opening the door for him and backing away. Ichiban entered the shed and closed the door behind him, taking a look around.

As he thought, tools and gadgets filled his field of vision. Near every wall and corner was one of her machines. Inactive Bronze Spheres, her new bronze armor, and many devices he had never seen before. What caught his eye was the strange circular pad beneath a curtain. That looked important.

He ignored it for now, however. His curiosity could wait.

"How are you feeling?" He started.

"Just get to the point." She rolled her eyes. "I have work to do, if you haven't noticed."

"That is the point." He replied, already feeling exasperated.

Akane blinked and crossed her arms.

"Really? You're here because you want to know how I feel? Cute." She scoffed. "Stop wasting my time, Ichiban. Either you say something important, or you fuck off."

That made it clear her emotions were still running hot, so Ichiban remained composed because one of them had to be mature if they were going to make any progress.

"Akane—"

"Just get out." She huffed.

"There's no one here but me," He told her, his tone still soft. "You can talk to me."

"I said leave."

He sighed.

"Acting stubborn won't help either of us," He said. "I know something's bothering you. You don't need to hide it."

"Of course, there's something bothering me!" She snapped, scowling at him. "You turned on me! You picked their side over mine!"

He backed off slightly, not expecting her heated response. Whether he said the right or wrong thing, Ichiban wasn't sure, but at least she was willing to engage.

"It's not about picking sides."

"Yes, it is! And you're supposed to be on mine!" She strongly disagreed, pausing before composing herself. "All of you were. So what if I was mean? That stupid bitch started it by pointlessly criticizing my approach, even though she couldn't think of anything else. How the hell was I supposed to react to that? Be nice? Get real."

Ichiban said nothing for a bit.

"I express my thoughts once, and suddenly I'm the bad guy. It's like you were just waiting for the opportunity to gang up on me." She said, then crossed her arms and looked away. "And you know what? I would've been okay if the others did that. Not like I care what they think about me. But you?"

She gave him a quick look, and even though she appeared angry on the surface, Ichi could tell she was really hurting beneath the surface.

"You of all people should've known better." She muttered in a much quieter tone.

He picked up the underlying meaning of what she said. After all, he was her boyfriend, so it was his job and responsibility to support her and always take her side. And she was right, but the same was true of all his friends. What kind of a person would he be otherwise? He didn't blame her for feeling that he had betrayed her, but he had to call out even those closest to him if he thought they had done something wrong.

That's what a real friend would do.

"Again, it's not about whose side I'm taking." He replied, and thankfully, she waited for him to continue this time. "If anything, I am on your side."

"Then you should've told them off."

"It doesn't work that way." He told her. "I get it, Irina wasn't being very helpful, and Xenovia can be a little annoying, but blowing up on them like that wasn't right."

"But she—"

"Irina was just worried, Akane. And for good reason." He said. "Would you really want me to agree with you even though you're in the wrong?"

She hesitated and didn't answer immediately.

"…Yes." She muttered weakly, most definitely not meaning it.

"Well, I can't do that." He spoke. "And I'm sure you wouldn't like it, either. Otherwise, I wouldn't be me anymore."

She remained silent for a moment, almost as if she had conceded, but then she spoke again.

"I thought you said you loved me." She said.

"I do love you. That's why I'm doing this." He replied. "That's why I'm relying on you to call me out if I'm in the wrong."

She opened her mouth to retort, but promptly closed it as Ichiban continued talking.

"If I see you randomly walking off a cliff, I'd pull you back and ask what you're doing, not walk off with you. And I expect you to do the same." He added. "I'm with you until the end, and I'm sure you feel the same way about me, but that's why we have to keep each other grounded. It's a responsibility we both share."

"I…"

However, she was without argument as she looked down uncomfortably. Despite how she was, Akane was usually a rational person. More logical than emotional, but even someone like her could feel overwhelmed.

"The thing is, I thought about it, and I think I know where this is coming from." He stated. "Just like Irina, you're worried, too, right? That's why you reacted that way."

She paused, her frown deepening as she stared back at him.

"What do you mean?"

"This stuff with Lani, the Palekana, the Overseer, and Pele…" He clarified, getting closer. "You pretend it's not affecting you, but I can tell it's making you very anxious."

Akane's expression turned into one of shock, almost in disbelief, and although she said nothing to prove or disprove his claim, her silent reaction was all the evidence he needed to know he was right.

The look of dread, quickly replaced by an empty look, told him she was doing it again. The stiff expression returned as she began analyzing her surroundings, and Ichiban didn't know what she was afraid of, but he went to reassure her anyway.

"I was really stunned that you were so aggressive with Irina. I mean, it didn't feel like you at all, but that back then was just stress getting to you, wasn't it? And it's not wrong to feel that way. Not when you're practically spearheading the whole thing," He gently took her hands, holding them in his. "I'm here for you, okay? You don't have to do this alone. If there's anything you want to tell me, I'll always be here to listen."

Akane said nothing for a while, but for the first time, as she turned her head away, she seemed a little vulnerable. Ichiban couldn't tell what to make of the flash of guilt that passed through her face, and assumed his words were getting to her.

"…Maybe it is a little stressful…" She murmured under her breath.

She said nothing else, however, but getting her to admit that was something. Progress was progress. Besides, Ichiban wasn't counting on her to tell him anything in the first place. Akane was far too stubborn for a few words to make her pour out her heart to him, but as long as he made it clear he was available if she wanted to talk, he was satisfied. Forcing her would have the opposite effect.

"And that's fine." He insisted. "Feeling stressed out knowing the things we do is only normal. Blowing up as you have is normal, too. It's a mistake, but we're humans. We make mistakes all the time. It's who we are."

Her face scrunched into a grimace, as if she were being reminded of something she would rather forget. Ichiban knew she was just feeling uncomfortable. It was not surprising. Akane wasn't usually confronted with her own issues.

His girlfriend was ultra spoiled, but he loved her anyway.

"That's why, sometimes, we have to take a step back and reflect." He said. "It's how we can grow and be better."

In a failed attempt to brush him off, Akane huffed.

"Look at you trying to be so understanding." She muttered. "Since when did you take the role of the wise counselor?"

"I had a pretty good mentor teaching me these things." Nonetheless, Ichiban gave her a grin. "Thought you could use some of it, too."

His 'kill her with kindness' approach seemed to have worked, as after a pause, Akane actually smiled back. But that smile quickly faded, and he felt her hands gripping his as she looked down at her feet.

"…I guess I was a little too mean." She admitted uncomfortably, her tone far too quiet but just loud enough for him to hear. "I'm mature enough to accept that."

"Well, you're still gonna have to apologize," He reminded her.

"Hah! As if." She disagreed, her haughty attitude returning. "Neither of them deserves to be in my presence, much less receive my apology. Why the hell would I do that?"

"Akane…"

"I already said I was being mean." She complained, retracting her hands away. "Isn't that enough?"

"Admitting your mistake is just the first step." He coolly replied. "This isn't over until you confront the real issue. You know that too."

"But I…" She struggled to form an argument, and as Ichiban gave her a mildly stern look, she huffed again and rolled her eyes. She was so adorably childish. "…Fine."

"Awesome. I knew you had it in you." He said, his wide smile returning as he patted her on the head. "I'm proud of you, Akane."

Telling her that provoked a self-satisfied smirk from her, which quickly dropped into a deep scowl before she slapped his hand away.

"Why am I being treated like a child?" She growled. "Are you mocking me? Are you asking for a beating, you bastard?"

"I don't know what you're talking about." He replied, shrugging his shoulders. "You're always asking me for praise, so when I saw you doing a good thing, I praised you. I'm doing what you ordered me to do."

"How dare you use my own words against me, you asshole. You know you're not supposed to do that," Akane told him off, crossing her arms. "The only reason I'm not kicking your ass right now is because I'm that forgiving. You'd better thank me for going easy on you."

Ichiban couldn't help but chuckle at that. Which seemed to lighten the mood as Akane's posture relaxed further.

"Knock it off. It's not funny," She said, her tone conveying mild amusement instead of annoyance.

"Then why are you grinning?" He responded, pointing out the smile playing at her lips.

"Because it—" She stopped, struggling to stop herself from giggling. "Why am I even explaining myself to you?"

"Good question." He said. "I guess the haughty Goddess loses all that pride and confidence when she's around her humble peasant."

"Oh, you really are asking for a beating," This time, Akane giggled as she shoved him away toward the exit. "Get outta here before I turn you into a popsicle, dragon boy. You already know how busy I am."

"Alright, alright," Ichiban laughed. "I'll leave you to it."

Ichiban grabbed the door handle, and moments before he left, his girlfriend spoke up again.

"Hey."

He turned his head to look at her and saw a mildly remorseful expression on her face. She visibly hesitated and seemed on the verge of changing her mind, but she said it regardless.

"I'm… sorry if I was being difficult." She apologized. "I know you're just trying to help."

Ichiban blinked, a little surprised to hear this from her. Akane barely ever apologized, and he definitely didn't expect this level of awareness from her. She was pretty bad at this sort of thing.

"No worries!" He replied with a wink. "Doesn't matter how easy or difficult you are. I'd never give up on you."

His heartfelt response elicited a blush from her, paired with one of the sweetest smiles he'd ever seen on her. A rare combination, if Ichi had to say. And one he would never grow bored of seeing.

Under all that bratty smugness and mildly endearing arrogance, Akane was still his princess.

He truly was lucky to have her.

Sometimes, I'm not sure if she's tamed you… Ddraig quipped as he exited the shed. Or if it's the other way around.

Ichiban liked to believe it went both ways.




– Akane –

As minutes pass after Ichi left the shed, I stand in the middle of it, almost motionless, as my hands tremble uncontrollably. A pit forms in my stomach, making me exhale as I stare at the door, still utterly baffled by what happened.

At first, I felt comforted in his presence. Hearing how he'll always be there for me, how he'll lend me his ear if I want to say something, how he'll be on my side no matter what. The reassurance felt nice. Calming. For once since that incident with Overseer, I felt at ease. Looking at his big dumb smile made it seem like everything was going to be okay.

But when he left, so did that feeling of comfort, replaced by overwhelming dread as the implications of everything that had happened came crashing down on me like a bag of bricks.

I can't believe I'm even thinking this, but I fucking hate myself for this. For how meek I was in front of him. At the same time, I just don't understand. I'm still processing this, even. Seriously, how? Just how? It doesn't make sense. None of it does. I know I was in the right this whole time.

They started it, and I ended it. They questioned my authority as the leader, and I put them in their places as anyone else in my position would do. I'm not wrong, not in a million years. I am not wrong.

So how in the hell did I let him talk me into this? And why am I not as angry about it as I'm supposed to be? I should be pissed the fuck off hearing him say all that sappy bullshit and making it sound like I'm at fault, but I'm not. I'm… weirdly okay with it.

Even when I try to force myself to be mad at what just happened, it doesn't work. I feel strangely at peace, and although the idea of apologizing to those two idiots makes me want to puke, I'm still fucking considering it.

Every time I try to argue, every time I try to tell him and convince him that I'm in the right, I take one look at his face, at how understanding and kind he appears, and it's like I forget all the words I want to say. I just stand there listening to him. Not out of fear or anything, but it's like… knowing he's right and I'm not.

And it's not true. I know it isn't true. That's not normal. This isn't me. What the fuck did Ichiban do to make me feel that way? How is he making me doubt myself? Is he so skilled in some form of witchcraft that it ignores both Excelsis' defenses and Gamer's Mind?

Most importantly, how did he just… know that I'm uneasy? I said nothing about this to anyone, not even to Lucifer, and I always made sure to appear confident so no one would question me and think I'm weak. Yet he somehow knew. He knew what I was thinking, what I was feeling.

It's terrifying. He shouldn't know that. I don't want him to know that. Ichiban of all people should know nothing about what I'm really thinking. Because what if he knows more than he lets on? What if Ichi knows I'm not who I try to appear to be? What if he knows I'm not a good person?

If he does know that, then does he also know what I've been doing behind his back? Will he report me to the yakuza after everything I've done? Will he turn on me for real and stab me in the back when I don't expect it? Will he hate me?

I don't want that. I don't want him to hate me. He can't hate me. I'll never let that happen. But what am I supposed to do? If he knows, then how can I—how am I supposed to convince him that what I'm doing is right too? Ichiban is understanding, but he's too good-natured. He wouldn't let that slide.

I look down at my trembling hands, dread slowly eating away at me as I try to calm myself. I clench my fists, close my eyes, and exhale again as I force myself to think rationally while sitting in my chair.

Calm down. Ichi doesn't know. He couldn't know. If he did, he would've confronted me about it already. That's the kind of person he is. He's decisive when he needs to be and won't ever just stand there and let things he thinks are wrong happen. It's why he approached me in the first place. Ichi lets his feelings dictate his actions more than logic, so he would've told me off had he known.

He might've known I was nervous, but that was just a lucky guess. There's no way in hell he knows about Empyrean or my soul-devouring ability. Not when I've made it my whole mission to keep it away from him until I'm ready to reveal it.

"How bizarre." Lucifer suddenly says, seeing me in this embarrassing state. "Just now, you were swooning over the dragon boy, and now…"

I say nothing as my grimace deepens.

"Now you seem deathly frightened." The Devil God adds, giving me a wide grin. "Of what, I wonder?"

"Shut up," I growl out.

Instead of shutting up, Lucifer takes a step toward me.

"Do you fear the boy knowing who you are?" He guesses, making me tighten my fists even more. "Do you fear him hating that person you wish to be?"

"I told you to shut up," I reiterate.

"Or is it the guilt creeping up after what you've done only moments ago?" He ignores me, leaning closer. "But if that's what it is… then what is there to be guilty of?"

I grow more and more infuriated as the bastard of a devil continues to interrogate me.

"Belittling those who are beneath you? Taking what's rightfully yours? Come now…" He chuckles. "And I thought you were better than that."

"Don't you fucking question me!" I spring forth from my chair, carelessly approaching the Devil God as he quickly backs off. "I don't care who or what you are! I'm not some weakling you can push around for your own amusement, understand?!"

Lucifer's grin only widens at that. I quickly compose myself, but my scowl doesn't change.

"How I feel about things is none of your goddamn business," I add. "You're here and not rotting away in some divine-guarded cell because you're still useful to me, so unless I specifically ask for it, keep your pointless counsel to yourself, Lucy."

Neither intimidated nor offended by my outburst, Lucifer chuckles again.

"Questioning you? My my, is that what it sounded like?" He puts a hand over his mouth. "That was not my intention, not at all. I was only trying to tease you and lighten up the mood, seeing how tense you were. But I see now I've only made things worse. My apologies, darling."

Like fucking hell that was your intention, but keep acting coy, you demonic son of a bitch.

I exhale for the umpteenth time and calm my nerves. Whatever. This whole thing is only making me more cautious. This isn't the end of the world, and now that I've gotten a real glimpse of where things might lead if I'm careless, I know to prepare better.

I can't let him know.

No matter the atrocity I must commit. No matter who I have to kill. Empyrean must remain a secret until I'm ready to disclose it to him. Until I feel comfortable enough to do so. Until I know he'll pick my side over anyone else's.

Ichiban must never know who I am. He must never know what I'm doing. He must never come to hate me.

My hands begin to tremble again as an uncomfortable truth passes through my mind.

Otherwise, Ichiban will die by my hands.





– Magnus –

It was pretty obvious even before he came to Hawaii to start his investigation, but Ganzhe was significantly more competent than either the Barracuda or the Yamai Syndicate. Where one thought he owned the damn place and the other didn't give two fucks about where he was, Wong Tou knew what he was doing. He knew who his enemies were and prepared accordingly.

This, naturally, could just be the CIA's splinter group helping him with information and resources so their little project could remain uninterrupted, but credit where credit's due: this guy was pretty damn smart. He spy-proofed the hell out of his base.

So, as expected, staking out Nirvana Hotel was a lot more complicated than it would appear. Because there weren't just cameras Magnus could very easily disable or hack with his Unknown Dictator, but also scrying wards all over the damn building. Magic he couldn't sabotage with his Sacred Gear.

This led to many problems. First, he didn't know how many people were in there that had nothing to do with Wong or the Overseer. Nirvana Hotel was still an actual establishment, and not entirely a front. Recklessly charging into the place, as the kids had done to Dwight's underground market, would put many innocent people in danger, and Magnus didn't want that weighing on his conscience.

Second, he didn't actually know much about the Ganzhe. Notable members, possible weapons, underground experiments like Patient Zero— none of that. They were the most secretive bunch, and Magnus only knew their leader due to his prior investigation and Wong Tou's old files and criminal record.

Third, he had no idea where Wong Tou actually hid. The safest bet was to say that he stayed on the highest floor, but was there a secret office or room? A secret path that led him in and out of said room? He didn't know, and at this point he wondered if it was even possible to get the jump on someone as prepared as he was.

How was Magnus supposed to catch him? If he tried to hack the cameras, the scrying wards would detect it because of the energy he'd have to release to use his Sacred Gear. If he tried to sneak into Nirvana, he knew for damn sure that he couldn't get past the hundreds, if not thousands, of cameras around and inside the building.

And alerting his only possible lead to the Overseer was the last thing he needed.

Besides, the Overseer probably knows it, too. He thought, observing the hotel from a distance. Meaning he'll be closely guarded by the Palekana. Maybe even the traitors.

Aside from the splinter group, the mysterious group trying to revive Pele was a much bigger problem. They probably had many powerful combatants in their ranks, so even a bulldozing approach might not be as effective here as it had been for Dwight's underground market.

How are we supposed to infiltrate their defenses without alerting Wong Tou? Magnus wondered, humming to himself. …Something to think about and share with the rest.

Magnus had been in this game for decades. So damn long that he'd been thinking about retiring, in fact. So he knew when it was time to retreat and ask for a second opinion. Sure, his current allies were a bunch of kids.

But, dubious or not, the yakuza princess was pretty resourceful.

Akane's edgy 'Machiavellian' mindset getting one-shot by her himbo's pure shonen spirit had been incredibly fun to write.

Proof that she can very easily complete a redemption arc if she wanted to, but will she? That's the real question.
