Gathered in the living room with the rest of those who stayed behind, I can tell that things still feel awkward after my fight with the two exorcists. Even though I'm still right and they should've taken my side, but whatever. It's not worth going over it a second time. I've gotten over it, and it's not like I care what these idiots think, either.

That includes Issei. Why would I want that useless sack of shit here anyway? If he wants to hang out with two equally useless morons instead, then let him leave. One less annoying gnat to worry about. He exists to drag us down.

As a memory of what happened in the shed flashes in my mind, I barely resist the urge to frown. I can't believe I let that happen. Even though I'm in the right. I can't believe I let Ichiban talk me into apologizing to that bitch. I should've told him to fuck off, too.

Too bad I'm apparently too much of a pushover to do something as simple as that.

No, no. Stop that. I said I'm over it. That wouldn't be the case if I kept thinking about it. Also, so what if I have to apologize? It's not like I mean it; I'll make sure to be as condescending as I possibly can so she knows that, too, so it doesn't count.

"So, uh…" Ichiban starts after a while, clearly feeling the growing tension. "Any word on Rose-san?"

…Just focus on the situation at hand, Akane.

"He said he's on his way," I answer. "He's found where Wong Tou is hiding, so I'm guessing he wants to plan an attack with us before infiltrating on his own."

Which would imply that Wong and his organization are much more dangerous than what we've been dealing with at the moment, but the CIA is kind of bitchmade, from what I've seen. Way too careful.

…Then again, being careful wouldn't have put me in a place where the Overseer could've tricked me.

I blame Xenovia. She made me do it.

"I imagine he'd want to know what we figured out on our side, as well," Kiba says.

"Probably." I nod. "Hopefully, with everyone on the same page, the rest of this investigation will be easy. Or easier than it already is, anyway."

"You just had to say that…" Ichiban sighs. "I guess that still leaves finding Lani. She's the final piece of the puzzle."

"The spheres are still searching," I remind them. "And by now, they've covered about 80% of the region. It's only a matter of time before we find her, and once we do, the Overseer is done for."

The real question is how am I going to kill and devour Pele? If he needs Lani to revive her, then I don't think it'd be possible for me to do so. Once he gets his hands on her, we'll be able to follow them into his mirror realm and prevent him from sacrificing her.

This, of course, means I need to somehow give him Lani without anyone else suspecting a thing. All I can think of to pull this off is by feigning ignorance/weakness one way or another, and that's not going to be very easy when my reputation around here is the 'extremely dependable leader'.

What a pain in the ass. Suffering from success, that is.

"Then we'll need to prepare our final assault on the Overseer's dimension," Kiba adds. "He will more than likely be very prepared for us. I assume there would be an army at his beck and call, and if they're anything like that warrior that rescued Dwight…"

Right, that Pele's 'Chosen' or whatever. I guess gods can have their own champions. Perhaps I can use him?

"Then we'll have one hell of a fight on our hands, huh?" Ichiban smirks. "Finally. It's been way too long since I had some action. I've been practicing a lot of techniques before we came here, and I've been itching to use them in real combat."

"What kind of techniques?" I ask with a mildly interested hum.

"You'll just have to wait and see." He says vaguely. "Let's just say that with Ddraig and Saejima-san's help, I'm no one-trick pony anymore."

Now I'm really curious.

Our chat is interrupted by a knock at the door, prompting Asia to get up from her chair to answer it. She opens the door, and Magnus gives her an appreciative smile as he enters the building, looking at us with a serious frown.

"About time," I say as he takes a seat.

"Sorry. My side of things took a lot longer than I initially thought." He replies before pausing, looking around the table. "…And I see we're still missing a few. Where's the rest?"

My mood sours as he mentions it, and the rest shuffle awkwardly, but I don't let it distract me.

"Don't worry about it. It's not important right now." I wave it off, and as nobody objects, I continue. "So what did you learn?"

"Right. I've found where Wong Tou and his Ganzhe are hiding." He nods. "Somewhere in Nirvana Hotel."

"That's the big one just outside of Honolulu, right?" Ichiban asks, making sure.

"Correct. Seems like he owns the building. Legally, it's in someone else's name, likely to protect his anonymity, but I've found swathes of his men standing guard in and out of it." Magnus explains. "And not only is the place littered with security cameras, but I've noticed countless scrying wards in its perimeters. He's most definitely hiding there."

"That settles it, then," I say. "That's the next place we're hitting. Shouldn't be too different from Dwight's."

"I'm afraid it's not that simple." The CIA agent disagrees. "Unlike the underground black market, Nirvana Hotel is a legitimate business."

"So?" I raise an eyebrow.

"So there's going to be a lot of innocent people there, Akane-san," Kiba tells me. "Humans or otherwise. If we recklessly rush in without a good plan, then there's no telling how many would be put at risk."

Right. Almost slipped there.

"You're right. I forgot about that." I cross my arms. "So there's no easy way to do this, huh?"

Nemesis could easily infiltrate, but again, I haven't found the bastard who hacked my Spyder yet, and until I get rid of them, they're not leaving my base. I'm not willing to risk my, or I guess Empyrean's, technology getting reverse-engineered.

"Not this time," Magnus says grimly. "Our best bet at the moment would be to lure him out."

"Which we can't do until we find Lani and Akane-san," Ichi replies, making me raise an eyebrow at the random honorific after my name before I remember he's talking about the other Akane. Still feels weird to hear that from him. I don't think I like it. "Talk about getting stuck between a rock and a hard place…"

"I hate waiting games…" Koneko mutters.

"You and me both." I snort.

Almost immediately after, my ring suddenly starts buzzing loudly enough for everyone in the room to hear, making us pause. Although none of them understand what this is about, a wide grin stretches across my face. Perfect timing~

"The good thing is that we won't be playing." I continue, raising my hand to show them the ring. "Because I just found Lani~"

"Really?!" Asia asks, smiling hopefully.

"Alright!" Ichi grins, a lot more excited. "Amazing work, Akane! Those things really came in handy after all."

Magnus says and does nothing, but I feel a sense of suspicion coming from him as he stares at me. What's his problem? He's been acting that way ever since we met for some reason. His 'Thoughts about you' section, when I use Observe, even confirms that he's suspicious of me.

But why? What does he know?

…I don't like it.

"Ice queen is reliable." Koneko compliments, mumbling her second sentence. "Still a jerk, though."

"Was there any doubt?" I shrug as I pretend not to hear the second part, pressing a tiny button on the ring to bring up a blue holographic screen. "Let's see…"

The screen shows a tiny remote island far south of the mainland. Surprisingly, it's inhabited by a small community, barely a hundred people. And I don't mean some uncontacted tribe nobody ever heard about, but a civilized group with its own tiny port and marketplace.

As for our targets? A small child with short brown hair and an old lady in her sixties with gray hair. Both are hiding in some kind of warehouse. Though it's clear that they're taken care of by the locals.

"That's them," I say, looking up what the spheres have analyzed. "A place called Rich Island, south of here. Seems anything but rich to me."

Pretty dingy, to be honest. Civilized, but dingy.

"That's where we have to go, then," Ichiban adds before pausing.

I notice him slightly fixated on the older woman, his stare lingering for a couple of seconds, making me blink.

"What's wrong?" I ask.

"Uh, no, it's nothing." He quickly shakes his head. "She just looks kinda familiar."

"Right…" I drop the subject. That was weird, but I don't think he's into older women. "Anyway, now we know where they are. We just need to grab them and let them stay here for safety."

"But aren't they safe where they are?" Kiba argues. "If the Overseer couldn't locate them there, wouldn't taking them to your resort increase the risks? Especially seeing how close it is to Honolulu, where we know he operates."

"This hinges solely on the assumption that the Overseer wouldn't find them on his own eventually," Magnus answers before I can. "And with his resources, it's only a matter of when. We're lucky we found them first."

"First, it's not luck; it's pure talent and excellence." I point out. "Second, now that we know her location, the risk is there regardless. We'll eventually need to go to Honolulu again, and the Overseer will do whatever mind spells he does to get that information out of us."

"I suppose…" Kiba hums.

"I thought you didn't believe Yamai when he mentioned the stuff about mind magic," Ichi says with a blink, making me shrug.

"I don't. Not entirely," I personally think it's future sight. Lucifer thinks so, too. "But it's worth taking into consideration regardless."

"How are we going to get to Rich Island?" Asia asks, having been quiet most of the time.

"I'll fly there. It shouldn't take me longer than a couple of minutes to get them here." I answer, getting up from my chair. "Once that's done, we can discuss what we'll do next."

"I'm coming with you," Ichiban says.

"We don't need two people for something so easy," I tell him. "Stay here."

"Screw that! Ever since we came here, you had all the fun. You fought Yamai, infiltrated the black market, fought Patient Zero, and beat up Dwight." He argues. "I barely got to do anything. I'm bored as fuck."

"As if this is going to be a fun experience," I roll my eyes. "It's a boring rescue mission. I doubt it'd take more than five minutes at most."

"I don't care." He insists. "So I'm coming, whether you want me or not."

I sigh. Yeah, he's not letting this go.

"Fine." I reluctantly accept, glancing at Magnus. "Text me in case something happens here."

"Got it." He nods.

With this, Ichi and I leave the resort and step onto the beach outside. Crystal wings of ice sprout out of my back, and as I offer Ichi a hand, he grins and activates his Balance Breaker. The red cape appears on his shoulder, fluttering as he slowly floats above the sand.

"I can fly too, y'know." He says.

"And here I thought you wanted to be lovingly held by your beloved girlfriend." I retract my hand as I match his elevation. "Your loss."

"Yeah, yeah," He scoffs playfully. "So, where are we going?"

"This way." I point at the horizon. "Follow me."

With Ichiban sticking closely behind me, we fly south of the resort. This idiot Overseer thinks he's playing us. He thinks we're practically bringing Lani to him, and you know what? He's right. That's exactly what I'm doing. After all, I want Pele revived, too.

Because if there's one way to thoroughly crush him in mind and spirit, it's to devour his beloved goddess right in front of him.

He shouldn't have picked a fight with me.




Landing on the docks bridge of the island with Ichi close behind me, I dispel my crystal wings and walk forward. Again, the place is incredibly small, with a couple of stores near the docks and a path leading straight from the beach to a thick forest, where the warehouse is.

Seeing how late it was, nobody was here, understandably. I doubt this place even has any law enforcement. Probably, whatever problem the island faces is handled by the locals. They'd be fucked if they got in a fight with pirates, though. I think. Are there even pirates in Hawaii? I know pirates still exist in general, but I don't know if there are any here.

Actually, back when pirates were more prominent, were some of them aware of the supernatural? I'd imagine legends like Blackbeard probably had some sort of powers. And if King Arthur existed, does that mean Davy Jones was a thing, too? Yeah, they did not sail these seas specifically, but it's interesting to think about. I wonder what actually happened to them?

"Whew, it's weirdly chilly in here," Ichi says with a shudder. "That's not your doing, is it?"

"No?" I raise an eyebrow. "Why would it be me?"

"I dunno, you seem kinda mad." He replies. "The air gets cold when you're mad."

"That's my thinking face." I point at myself. "Not the angry face. You should know these things."

"I guess." He snorts. "What are you thinking about, then? Aside from finding Lani and Akane-san."

"I was wondering if there are pirates around," I tell him as we make our way toward the warehouse. "Like actual supernatural pirates. Imagine if Davy Jones was out there somewhere?"

"Ooh…" Ichi grows excited at the prospect as his eyes start twinkling. "That's so cool. You think there are some sea monsters, too? Like the kraken? Giant sea serpents?"

"Dragons and hydras exist, so probably."

"Aw man, I wonder if we'll ever get to see one." He says with a grin. "It'd be a shame if we didn't before we're back in Japan."

"Hmm…" I pause and think about it for a moment. "Do you think kraken calamari would taste better than regular squid calamari?"

"That's the first thing that came to your mind?" He questions before thinking about it. "…Now I'm wondering, too."

"I mean, neither of us has had dinner yet, so…" I shrug. "Maybe we should start looking for giant sea monsters to eat."

"Haha, that'd be awesome." Ichiban laughs. "If only we knew where to look."

If anything, I'm starving. I haven't had anything to eat since breakfast, and ever since that little funny incident with Irina and Xenovia, I was in too bad a mood to really eat. Well, I guess I did have a few souls in the Tojo Clan HQ, but those don't really count toward actual food.

My stomach's filled up on energy drinks, and it's starting to be a little upsetting. I guess even being super durable doesn't stop a terrible diet from fucking you up. I'm really glad I got that perfect body perk a while ago. Made keeping my figure totally effortless.

Still, I'm hungry. I hope there's a nice restaurant around here somewhere. We could grab a bite before we make it back to the resort. Assuming there's anything open this late in this corner of the earth.

With an irritated frown, I shoo away the annoying, flying bugs with my hands. The deeper we make it into the thickets, the more mosquitoes, flies, and moth flies around our faces. Ugh, this is why I hate the wilderness. I'd torch this entire island to the ground if it meant getting rid of them permanently.

"I fucking hate bugs…" I complain.

"Who doesn't?" Ichi replies before suddenly pointing at something. "LOOK OUT, A COCKROACH!"

"KYAA?!" I squeak out in surprise, reflexively jumping away and holding onto him for dear life. "Where?! Get rid of it! Get rid of it!"

However, Ichiban bursts out laughing instead. It takes me a couple of seconds to realize he was just messing with me, and I growl.

"That's not funny!" I shove him away.

"But it is." He disagrees in between chuckles. "Aw man, this shit always gets me. Behold the invincible and almighty Akane Amamiya, capable of destroying countries with a flick of her wrist, yet ever so frightened by a tiny bug."

"Knock it off." I click my tongue. "Do you know how many diseases those things carry? You'd be scared of them too, if you weren't so painfully uneducated. But what do I expect from a filthy street rat who dropped out of middle school?"

"Whatever you say, princess." He shrugs, completely unbothered, before pointing at something else. "LOOK OUT, THERE'S ONE RIGHT THERE!"

This time, I don't scream and jump like before, because I know he's just trying to get a reaction out of me. This won't work twice in a row.

…

…I do, however, flinch.

"STOP THAT!" I scowl, making him laugh harder.

"It's even funnier the second time!"

"Do that again, and I promise you'll come out of this island with an icicle shoved so far up your ass, you'll be drip-fed water for the rest of your life!"

"Okay, okay, I'll stop. Hehe…" He relents out of pure and overwhelming fear. "We really should work on that phobia of yours. I bet if our enemies knew about it, it'd put you in a bad spot."

"It's not a phobia." I scoff with a roll of my eyes. "It's a perfectly rational aversion to nature's biggest mistake."

In the midst of our bickering, Lucifer, who had been quietly following us the entire time, finally speaks up.

"You're being followed, darling." He warns me.

Though I already knew that.

"Well, whatever you call it," Ichi replies. "I bet you're really happy there's no more Beelzebub devils to worry about, huh?"

"You can say that again…"

After a few minutes of walking, we finally made it to the main plaza. In front of a bar called Esperanza was the warehouse we were looking for. It was incredibly quiet and dark, with only a couple of dimly lit lamps around each pathway.

"That's the place, huh?" Ichi points at the warehouse.

"Yup." I nod, making my way toward it. "C'mon. Let's get this over with."

Though before we open the door, we're interrupted by an unfamiliar voice.

"What do you think you're doing?" He says. "Place is off limits. Back off."

I turn around to look at the upstart, seeing a tall, brown-haired middle-aged man wearing a green polo shirt, old, run-down jeans, and black shoes coming out of the bar. Observe tells me he's no threat. Just a regular ass guy, if somewhat impressive for the average human.

"I don't recognize you. I've never seen you around," He adds as he gets a better look at us. "Who are you? What do you want?"

"We're—" Ichi starts, but I quickly cut him off.

"None of your business," I tell him. "If you know what's good for you, you'd go back to where you came from, little man."

The old man frowns.

"We're here for Lani and Ms. Akane," Ichi says, elbowing my side. "There's someone out there who wants to hurt them. They're not safe here."

"Who?" The man replies, clearly feigning ignorance. "I've never heard of those names. You're in the wrong place, kid. That warehouse is where we store the island's resources. But if you're not gonna move…"

He pulls a pistol out of his hand and points it at us.

"Then I'll make you move."

I scoff, roll my eyes, and kick the door open in spite of his idiotic threat. Lo and behold, our targets are right there, looking at me like deer in headlights. Immediately afterward, the old lady steps in front of the young girl, glaring at us with suspicion and concern.

"And pray tell, who are these two?" I point at them with a smirk. "Strays you didn't know about?"

The dumbass says nothing, but his frown deepens.

"Stop antagonizing him," Ichi mutters, giving me an annoyed glance. "Look, I swear, we just want to keep them safe. The other guy looking for them could be here any second."

Instead of continuing to play dumb, he replies with a valid question, while also practically confirming my suspicions.

"And how do I know you're not working with Bryce?"

I knew it!

"Bryce?!" Ichiban's eyes widen. "That's the Overseer?!"

"Answer my damn question."

Now, I'm not entirely sure why we're humoring this moron when we could just take the two and leave. Not like that peashooter would hurt us in any way.

But instead of interfering, I let Ichi handle this.

"Right, well…" He pauses to collect his thoughts. "I don't know how much you know, but I'm the Red Dragon Emperor and one of the Tojo clan yakuza. My name is Ichiban Kasuga, and this right here is Akane Amamiya, daughter of Tatsu Amamiya. We're currently working with the CIA to put a stop to the Overseer's— or I guess Bryce's plans. We know what he's after, and we won't let him lay a finger on Lani. I promise."

"That's a nice story." The old man replies, still skeptical. "Not sure I believe a word of it, though."

Instead of verbally explaining himself, Ichiban summons his Boosted Gear in its gauntlet form. This makes the old man flinch and back away in genuine shock, a reaction that tells me he knows nothing about the supernatural. Just enough, like how Bryce is a bad guy looking for two innocent people.

"W-what the hell?!"

"This is the Boosted Gear," Ichiban says, raising his gauntlet. "Do you believe me now?"

Almost convinced to shoot us, the old man points his gun at Ichiban's head. I almost want him to pull the trigger and give me an excuse to beat his ass, but before he could do that, the old lady behind us spoke.

"He's telling the truth, Jason." The other Akane says. "He's Masumi's boy."

This prompts us to look at her, equally surprised at the accurate assessment. How did she know? And on a first-name basis already. Wow.

"You know the boss?"

She smiles and nods, the suspicion on her face evaporating in an instant.

"Well, that makes things a lot less complicated." I snort, glancing at Jason. "Convinced? Or do we have to kick your ass for you to get it?"

He remains silent for a moment before lowering his gun.

"Good choice. Come on, we need to go now." I gesture for the young girl to come closer and address Jason. "And for the record, immediately pointing your gun at random teenagers fucking around makes you look like a lunatic."

Lani hesitantly approaches me, but a push from the other Akane makes her trust me enough to take my hand. I carry her and spread my crystal wings as Ichi carries the older woman after activating Cape Mode.

Jason looks at us in utter awe as we float off the ground, making me smirk at him.

"No one will believe you."

Was the last thing I said before flying off into the distance with the little girl in my arms.





– Irina –

Alone in one of the parks of Honolulu, she silently stared at her phone, looking up from it every once in a while in search of Issei. He had sent her a text at first, begging her and Xenovia not to leave, but, well, even if Irina was fine with coming back, her partner was very opposed to it.

But that was how Xenovia was. Although she could tolerate quite a bit, Akane had crossed a line, and she would never let anything like that slide. It was to be expected, honestly. Irina always understood that it was only a question of when, not if, those two would begin to clash. Their personalities weren't very compatible.

Xenovia was stubborn, overly straightforward, and wasn't afraid to speak her mind. It came at the cost of having bad social skills, as most usually misunderstood her for being rude and annoying, but Irina would be lying if she said she didn't envy her partner.

Akane, on the other hand, was outright mean. Even before this incident, Irina had seen how she would treat Issei in particular, and though it might just be the way they communicated, seeing that no one tried to interject, Irina felt it was unnecessarily harsh. Bordering on abusive.

She'd kept it to herself, however. It felt unnecessary to bring up, seeing that Akane had literally saved their lives, offered sincere condolences after David's death, and let them stay in her territory. Irina didn't want to come off as ungrateful. Issei also didn't seem to hate her treatment of him very much, so it wasn't her place to say anything.

If anything, he seemed a lot more jealous of Ichiban than upset at it.

Irina sighed deeply, spotting someone in the park with the corner of her eye.

"Ah, Issei! Over here!" She called out with a smile, and he matched it once he saw her.

"Hey! Sorry if I'm late." He waved. "Honolulu is pretty far from the resort."

"I know. You're fine."

As he approached her, Irina scooted over to give him enough space to sit next to her.

"Where's Xenovia?" He asked, noticing her partner was nowhere to be seen.

"Patrolling." She answered. "We don't really have Akane's resources, so that's the best thing we can do at the moment. Split up and look for any suspicious activities."

Although both of them realized how risky it was to remain within the Overseer's territory, unfortunately, there weren't a lot of options. They even planned to stay the night at Akane's resort, since the hotel they had been staying at was blown up during her fight against Dwight. Clearly, Xenovia didn't think too much about the consequences of splitting up with the rest.

Though even if she did, Irina doubted that would change anything.

"I'm supposed to be patrolling, too," She giggled. "But, well…"

Irina wasn't exactly willing to return, even when Issei asked her to, but she still wanted to see him, so instead of rejecting him outright, she told him to meet up here.

"Do you have a place to stay?" He asked again.

"We're still looking." She told him. "There's this hotel outside the city called Nirvana, but it's too expensive."

And the higher-ups would definitely question them changing hotels at random like this. Why wouldn't they just tell them what's going on? Because there was a real chance the pair would be pulled out of Hawaii entirely. They were already suspicious enough of the recent supernatural incidents.

"…You can stay with us?" Issei offered after a while.

"Issei…"

"L-listen, I know after what happened, it's the last thing you wanna do," He quickly explained himself. "But it's not safe in here! And none of us agrees with what Akane said. She probably didn't even mean it."

Irina wasn't sure about that.

"We can take care of ourselves, Issei." She said before pausing. Irina looked down at her lap and frowned. "…And let's be honest, she was right about me."

"What? No!" Issei disagreed, staring at her in surprise. "Of course, she's not! Why would you say that?"

"It's just… I don't think I'm good enough for this sort of thing." Irina replied. "Being an exorcist, I mean. It's… after the whole thing with Kokabiel, I keep wondering if I'm even fit to be one."

That day had been an eye-opener for her. It was the first real mission that she and Xenovia had ever gone on. True, they hadn't known it was Kokabiel at first, but the higher-ups had considered the possibility, which was why they sent David out to lead them.

Only for him to die in the line of duty, all while they'd gotten in the way. They were practically useless while he, Akane, Ichiban, and the two devil heiresses had pulled their weight. What were they even doing? They were clearly not even close to prepared to handle this kind of threat.

Yet they were the ones who came out of it alive. When they had no right to. It made her feel sick to her stomach.

And now, Irina wasn't sure if she even had what it took to be an exorcist. Even when she trained, hoping to make a difference, wanting to make David's sacrifice worth something, the pace of her progress was so glacial that Irina barely got any stronger. All while her partner's strength soared to heights she couldn't imagine reaching in just a month.

This meant that Irina was the problem, after all.

Maybe she wasn't meant to be an exorcist.

"I'm not particularly strong or smart. I don't really offer anything new to the table. All I do is weigh everyone down." She sighed, leaning back. "No wonder Akane got so mad at me."

"However you feel about yourself doesn't give her the right to say all those terrible things," Issei said. "And they're not even true, in the first place. You're plenty strong, clever, and saved my life down there."

"You saved my life when you pushed me out of the way." She retorted. "All I did was carry you to safety."

"And that's somehow less? Good friends and allies help each other." He reminded her. "It's a two-way street."

Irina said nothing for a moment.

"Look, I get how it feels, alright? I know I'm not the strongest either. And I'm pretty damn dumb, too. Compared to people like Kasuga and Akane, I'm basically nothing. And I feel that sometimes. I mean, I feel pretty jealous of Kasuga." He continued, putting his hand over hers. "But so what? Just because I'm not as strong, I'm supposed to give up? Because I'm scared to mess up, I'm supposed to let others do everything? Screw that."

Irina watched as he brought his other hand up and clenched it.

"Sure, maybe I'll never contribute as much as Akane or Kasuga. Maybe I'll never be the strongest or best at anything, and maybe I'll screw up down the line, but that's fine with me." He said, staring at her with determination. "I've been blessed with a Sacred Gear, and I'll always try to help in my own way. I'll support my friends and do the right thing."

Once again, she remained silent for a moment, but eventually felt the need to respond.

"Doesn't it get difficult?"

"Yeah, and?" Issei blinked. "I don't think it's supposed to be easy."

"Heh. I guess not." Irina smiled, tightly wrapping her hand around his. "Thanks, Issei. I think I needed to hear that."

"U-uh, yeah, for sure…" Her childhood friend replied, suddenly becoming timid. Cute. "Anytime."

Irina noticed his stare flickering between their hands and nowhere, as he struggled to keep his composure. She didn't know what he was thinking— he'd practically started this when he put his hand over hers. Did he not mean it romantically? Well, even if he didn't, he was definitely viewing it that way now.

Yet he didn't seem to be against it. Even though he was crushing on Akane hard. Did she have a chance after all?

She might as well stake her claim.

As her face grew hotter, Irina scooted ever so closer to him, which he most definitely noticed as she felt his hand tightening around hers. Once she felt comfortable enough, she looked at him, and as he caught her stare with the corner of his eye, he mustered up the courage to meet her gaze.

Almost as if he had read her mind, Issei matched her pace and leaned closer, until eventually, their lips met. The sensation was almost indescribable to Irina. It felt strangely soothing, even though her heart threatened to leap out of her chest. She never saw herself doing something so bold. They'd only gone on a single date.

Irina nearly regretted it, but when she felt him just as into this as she was, she knew it was okay. A part of her wondered if his crush on Akane was even real or if she'd conjured it up purely out of her own fear of being rejected, but it was quickly forgotten as she enjoyed the moment.

Once they backed away from each other, realization dawned on them, and they both looked away with their faces going red. Even then, however, they still held each other's hands.

"I-I'm sorry if that came out of the blue." She spoke first, quickly apologizing. "I um…"

"I-it's fine…" He replied, equally embarrassed. "I-I wasn't sure about how you felt about me…"

Why is it so awkward now?! She thought to herself. I want to die.

Irina took a moment to compose herself, not wanting to embarrass herself further.

"T-the truth is, I've been feeling that way for a long time." She said. "Ever since we were kids, in fact. Of course, I didn't really understand my feelings back then, but after meeting you in Kuoh again, I—"

Before she could finish that sentence, she was interrupted by a serrated sword going below her head and pressing into her neck. Her eyes widened, but she remained as still as the one holding the sword.

I didn't even notice him come. I was too comfortable, I… She thought before noticing something grim.

This man was incredibly powerful. Irina knew that if she moved, he'd slit her throat before she could do anything.

"Irina? What's—" Issei's words died in his throat as he glanced at her.

But before he could appropriately respond to the threat and help her, the man spoke.

"Don't move." He said with a deep voice. "Or she dies."

So Issei stayed in his chair.

"Who are you?" He questioned. "What do you want from us?"

The stranger said nothing for a moment, and Irina, without moving her head, glanced up, hoping to get a better look at him. All she could make out was the yellow Palekana outfit. A hooded, sleeveless version. This met the description Akane gave of the person who rescued Dwight.

She had warned that he was surprisingly strong, but Irina hadn't expected this.

"The two of you will come with me." He told them, leaving no room to argue. "Now."

He led Irina away from the chair, almost forcefully dragging her, with Issei carefully following them. The serrated sword was still over her neck the entire time, breaking the skin but not going further, and as she was about to ask where he was taking them, a golden portal suddenly appeared in the park.

The stranger nodded toward the portal, making Issei go through it first. Although hesitant, he did as he was told, and once Issei was through, the man took her there moments later.

She didn't know what would happen to them, but Irina felt horrible for her partner. This guy had snuck up on them because she wasn't on guard as she should have been.

She really was the worst.
